Hoc modo flendum est cuilibet Christiano, qui gratiam baptismalem amisit, vel post pœnitentiam recidivavit, atque cœlestis Sponsi privatus puris amplexibus, jam amplexatur hæc terrena seu stercora, qui nutriebatur in croceis, qui quum in honore esset, non intellexit. Unde scriptum est in Threnis: Deduc quasi torrentem lacrimas per diem et noctem, et non des requiem tibi. Talis utique fuit, qui dixit: Exitus aquarum deduxerunt oculi mei, quia non custodierunt legem tuam.
paras.en: [[1:8|Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth.|Plange quasi virgo accincta sacco super virum pubertatis suæ]] In this way every Christian must weep who has lost baptismal grace, or has relapsed after penance, and, deprived of the pure embraces of the heavenly Bridegroom, now embraces these earthly things, or dung, he who was [[Lam 4:5|brought up in scarlet|nutriebatur in croceis]], who [[Ps 48:13|when he was in honour did not understand|quum in honore esset, non intellexit]] [the margin gives Ps. xlviii, 13 and 21, where the same words stand]. Hence it is written in Lamentations: [[Lam 2:18|Let tears run down like a torrent day and night|Deduc quasi torrentem lacrimas per diem et noctem]], [[Lam 2:18|give thyself no rest|et non des requiem tibi]]. Such certainly was he who said: [[Ps 118:136|My eyes have sent forth springs of water: because they have not kept thy law.|Exitus aquarum deduxerunt oculi mei, quia non custodierunt legem tuam.]]

paras.t: Periit sacrificium et libatio de domo Domini, id est sacrificium illud de quo fertur in Psalmo, Sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus; et in Ecclesiastico, Salutare sacrificium est, attendere mandatis, et discedere ab omni iniquitate; et libatio internæ ac lacrimosæ compunctionis. Ista deficiunt ab his, in quibus abundante ac prævalente iniquitate, caritas refrigescit. Et luxerunt sacerdotes. Boni enim sacerdotes, de tanto subditorum suorum dispendio intime dolent. Quemadmodum enim gloria patris filius sapiens, sic dolor illius est filius stultus.
paras.en: [[1:9|Sacrifice and libation is cut off from the house of the Lord|Periit sacrificium et libatio de domo Domini]], that is, that sacrifice of which it is said in the Psalm, [[Ps 50:19|A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit|Sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus]]; and in Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 35:2|It is a wholesome sacrifice to take heed to the commandments, and to depart from all iniquity|Salutare sacrificium est, attendere mandatis, et discedere ab omni iniquitate]]; and the libation of inward and tearful compunction. These fail in those in whom, as iniquity abounds and prevails, charity grows cold. [[1:9|the priests, the Lord's ministers, have mourned|Et luxerunt sacerdotes]]. For good priests grieve inwardly at so great a loss among their subjects. For as a wise son is the glory of his father[[Prov 10:1||]], so a [[Prov 19:13|foolish son is the grief of his father|dolor illius est filius stultus]].

paras.t: Confusum est vinum: id est, saporosa contemplatio divinorum exhilarans cor, in istis deficit, quia terrena sapiunt, non divina. Elanguit oleum: id est, opera misericordiæ defecerunt in istis. Qui enim sibi nequam est, cui bonus erit? Et omnes quæ sua sunt quærunt, non quæ aliorum.
paras.en: [[1:10|the wine is confounded|Confusum est vinum]]: that is, the savoury contemplation of divine things, which gladdens the heart, fails in them, because they savour [the Latin *sapiunt* means both "taste of" and "have a mind for"] earthly things, not divine. [[1:10|the oil hath languished|Elanguit oleum]]: that is, the works of mercy have failed in them. For [[Ecclus 14:5|He that is evil to himself, to whom will he be good?|Qui enim sibi nequam est, cui bonus erit?]] And [[Phil 2:21|all seek the things that are their own|omnes quæ sua sunt quærunt]], not those of others.

paras.t: Confusi sunt agricolæ, ululaverunt vinitores super frumento et hordeo: id est, boni prælati, doctores et prædicatores, qui fidelium corda vomere prædicationis colunt, purgant, fecundant, de spirituali sterilitate atque ruina populi dolent et erubescunt, quia non affert populus fructus virtutum, quæ per frumentum et hordeum designantur. Unde et Esdras ait: Domine Deus, confundor et erubesco levare faciem meam ante conspectum tuum, quoniam iniquitates nostræ multiplicatæ sunt, et peccata nostra creverunt usque ad cœlum. Populus autem fidelis, vocatur et ager et vinea Dei, dicente ad Corinthios Paulo: Dei agricultura estis, Dei ædificatio estis. Frequenter vero boni pastores formidant ne ex eorum negligentia ac insufficientia accidat imperfectio subditorum: ideo intra se confunduntur, mallentque subesse quam præesse.
paras.en: [[1:11|The husbandmen are ashamed, the vinedressers have howled for the wheat, and for the barley|Confusi sunt agricolæ, ululaverunt vinitores super frumento et hordeo]]: that is, good prelates, doctors and preachers, who till, cleanse and make fruitful the hearts of the faithful with the ploughshare of preaching, grieve and blush at the spiritual barrenness and ruin of the people, because the people does not bring forth the fruits of the virtues, which are signified by the wheat and the barley. Hence Esdras too says: O Lord God, [[1 Esd 9:6|I am confounded and ashamed to lift up my face|confundor et erubesco levare faciem meam]] before thy sight, [[1 Esd 9:6|for our iniquities are multiplied|quoniam iniquitates nostræ multiplicatæ sunt]], [[1 Esd 9:6|and our sins are grown up even unto heaven|et peccata nostra creverunt usque ad cœlum]]. Now the faithful people is called both the field and the vineyard of God, as Paul says to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 3:9|You are God's husbandry: you are God's building|Dei agricultura estis, Dei ædificatio estis]]. And good pastors frequently fear lest the imperfection of their subjects should come about through their own negligence and insufficiency: therefore they are confounded within themselves, and would rather be under others than over them.

paras.t: Malogranatum, et palma, et malum, et omnia ligna agri aruerunt. Homines nominibus arborum designantur. Istud ergo contingit, dum homines diversarum gratiarum generibus adornati, in vitia collabuntur, et infructuosis arboribus similantur, arentes, quia non habent humorem influentiæ Spiritus Sancti. Porro per malogranatum (quæ est arbor medicinalis, habens poma ad edendum amara et granis repleta) figurantur personæ ad aliorum instructionem idoneæ, habentes verba districtæ correptionis, quibus animæ læsiones sanantur, et grana, id est semina verbi cœlestis. Per palmam exprimuntur, qui diu floruerunt in gratia, tam æstate prosperitatis, quam hieme adversitatis. Tales autem aliquando cadunt, quemadmodum Augustinus perhibet se vidisse cedros Libani cadere. Nemo enim securus est, dicente Apostolo, Qui stat, videat ne cadat. Et quo ascensus sublimior, eo casus nocentior. Quia confusum est gaudium spirituale a filiis hominum: qui quum sint carnales, potius filii hominum quam Dei vocantur, quemadmodum testatur Paulus: Quum sit inter vos zelus et contentio, nonne homines estis?
paras.en: [[1:12|the pomegranate tree, and the palm tree, and the apple tree, and all the trees of the field are withered|Malogranatum, et palma, et malum, et omnia ligna agri aruerunt]]. Men are signified by the names of trees. This, then, happens when men adorned with graces of different kinds fall into vices and become like unfruitful trees, withering because they have not the moisture of the inflowing of the Holy Spirit. Further, by the pomegranate (which is a medicinal tree, having fruit bitter to eat and full of seeds) are figured persons fit to instruct others, who have words of strict correction, by which the soul's injuries are healed, and seeds, that is, the seeds of the heavenly word. By the palm are expressed those who have long flourished in grace, both in the summer of prosperity and in the winter of adversity. Yet such men sometimes fall, as Augustine relates that he had seen cedars of Libanus fall. For no one is secure, since the Apostle says, He that standeth, [[1 Cor 10:12|let him take heed lest he fall|videat ne cadat]]. And the loftier the ascent, the more harmful the fall. [[1:12|because joy is withdrawn from the children of men|Quia confusum est gaudium spirituale a filiis hominum]] [Denis reads *spiritual joy*]: who, being carnal, are called sons of men rather than sons of God, as Paul testifies: [[1 Cor 3:3|whereas there is among you envying and contention|Quum sit inter vos zelus et contentio]], [[1 Cor 3:4|are you not men|nonne homines estis]]?

paras.t: Accingite vos, et plangite, sacerdotes; cubate in sacco. Hoc facere habent sacerdotes, prælati solliciti, dum gravis tribulatio imminet: imo quo gregem sibi commissum conspexerint ab invisibilibus aut visibilibus adversariis periculosius impeti, eo amplius humiliare se debent coram Deo, abstinendo, orando, prosternendo, ac diversis modis divinam clementiam invocando, ut tanto benignius adsit, quanto major est indigentia.
paras.en: [[1:13|Gird yourselves, and lament, O ye priests|Accingite vos, et plangite, sacerdotes]]; [[1:13|lie in sackcloth|cubate in sacco]]. This priests and careful prelates must do when grievous tribulation threatens: indeed, the more dangerously they see the flock committed to them attacked by invisible or visible adversaries, the more they ought to humble themselves before God, by abstaining, praying, prostrating themselves, and calling upon the divine clemency in various ways, so that it may come to their help the more kindly the greater the need.

paras.t: Et clamate ad Dominum: A, a, a, diei: quia prope est dies Domini. Hoc de die mortis atque judicii accipi potest, ad quem debet se quilibet cum magna sollicitudine præparare.
paras.en: [[1:14|and cry ye to the Lord|Et clamate ad Dominum]]: [[1:15|Ah, ah, ah, for the day: because the day of the Lord is at hand|A, a, a, diei: quia prope est dies Domini]]. This can be taken of the day of death and of judgement, for which everyone ought to prepare himself with great care.

paras.t: Numquid non coram oculis vestris alimenta perierunt, de domo Dei vestri lætitia et exsultatio? Videmus ad oculum, quomodo nunc a multis deficit panis animæ, panis videlicet bonæ operationis et gratiæ: a quibus spirituale gaudium tollitur, quoniam non in Domino, sed in rebus inanibus gloriantur.
paras.en: [[1:16|Is not your food cut off before your eyes, joy and gladness from the house of our God?|Numquid non coram oculis vestris alimenta perierunt, de domo Dei vestri lætitia et exsultatio?]] We see with our own eyes how the bread of the soul now fails many, the bread, namely, of good works and of grace: from whom spiritual joy is taken away, because they glory not in the Lord but in empty things.

paras.t: Computruerunt jumenta in stercore suo. Hoc spiritualiter expositum est præcedenti articulo, et maxime competit iis qui non ex sola passione vel infirmitate, sed ex habitu malo atque proposito delectantur in immunditiis vitiorum suorum, qui sordent in peccatorum squalore, quos profundum absorbuit, et lætantur quum impie fecerint. Hi sunt tanquam sus lota in volutabro luti. Stercora sunt turpitudines vitiorum, flores autem decor et splendor virtutum.
paras.en: [[1:17|The beasts have rotted in their dung|Computruerunt jumenta in stercore suo]]. This was expounded spiritually in the preceding article, and it applies above all to those who, not from passion or weakness alone, but from evil habit and purpose, delight in the uncleanness of their vices; who are foul in the filth of sins, whom the deep has swallowed up[[Ps 68:16||]], and who [[Prov 2:14|are glad when they have done evil|lætantur quum impie fecerint]] [Denis has *impie*, "wickedly", for *malefecerint*]. These are as a [[2 Pet 2:22|sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire|sus lota in volutabro luti]]. Dung is the foulness of the vices; flowers, the beauty and splendour of the virtues.

paras.t: Quid ingemuit animal? Sic multi fidelium gemunt, quia non est pascua eis, id est spiritualis consolatio, copia gratiæ, optata perfectio. Qui enim zelum justitiæ habent, et quotidie proficere cupiunt, Dominumque in omnibus honorare nituntur, frequenter intra se affliguntur et gemunt quod tot imperfectiones et evagationes miscentur eorum bonis operibus, quod Deo tam fervide ac reverenter non obsequuntur ut cupiunt, quod optatam virtutum celsitudinem non adipiscuntur: estque afflictio ista et gemitus mirabiliter meritorius ac peccati consumptivus.
paras.en: [[1:18|Why did the beasts groan|Quid ingemuit animal]]? So do many of the faithful groan, [[1:18|because there is no pasture for them|quia non est pascua eis]], that is, spiritual consolation, abundance of grace, the perfection they long for. For those who have zeal for justice, desire to advance daily, and strive to honour the Lord in all things, are frequently afflicted within themselves and groan that so many imperfections and wanderings of mind are mingled with their good works, that they do not serve God as fervently and reverently as they desire, and that they do not attain the height of virtue they long for: and this affliction and groaning is wonderfully meritorious and consumes sin.

paras.t: Ad te, Domine, clamabo, dolens et orans pro populo tuo, quia ignis concupiscentiæ seu diabolicæ tentationis, comedit speciosa, id est interiorem ornatum ac venustatem, deserti, id est cordis humani seu populi christiani a te relicti: in quo aliquando fuit pulchritudo virtutum, scientiæ claritas, gratiæ splendor, donorum venustas. Nunc autem in eo, postquam dedit locum diabolo, succubuitque peccato, deordinata ac deformata sunt omnia: ita quod insunt strepitus passionum, peccatorum tumultus, vultusque animæ a Creatore aversus, ad vilia miserabiliter est conversus. Talis anima similis est domui in qua nihil suo loco repositum est, nihil ordinate dispositum, sed cuncta subversa, hinc inde jactata, in qua insuper est fœtor atque tristissimus color. Et sicut in hujuscemodi domo nullus consistere delectatur, sic in anima tali Deus habitare penitus detestatur. Et flamma iræ, indignationis, furoris, concupiscentiæ, cupiditatis, succendit omnia ligna regionis, id est universos habitantes in sæculo: non universos simpliciter, sed tam multos, quod alii respectu eorum perpauci sunt. Jam enim conspicimus, quam pauci his passionibus dominentur.
paras.en: [[1:19|To thee, O Lord, will I cry|Ad te, Domine, clamabo]], grieving and praying for thy people, [[1:19|because fire|quia ignis]] of concupiscence or of diabolical temptation [[1:19|hath devoured the beautiful places|comedit speciosa]], that is, the inner adornment and loveliness, [[1:19|of the wilderness|deserti]], that is, of the human heart, or of the Christian people, forsaken by thee: in which there was once the beauty of the virtues, the brightness of knowledge, the splendour of grace, the loveliness of the gifts. But now in it, after it has given [[Eph 4:27|place to the devil|locum diabolo]] and has yielded to sin, all things are disordered and disfigured: so that the din of the passions and the tumult of sins are in it, and the face of the soul, turned away from its Creator, is miserably turned to vile things. Such a soul is like a house in which nothing is put in its place, nothing set in order, but everything overturned and thrown about this way and that, and in which, besides, there is a stench and a most dismal colour. And as no one likes to stay in a house of this kind, so God utterly abhors to dwell in such a soul. [[1:19|and the flame|Et flamma]] of anger, indignation, fury, concupiscence and covetousness [[1:19|hath burnt all the trees of the country|succendit omnia ligna regionis]], that is, all who dwell in the world: not all absolutely, but so many that the others are very few in comparison with them. For we see already how few master these passions.

paras.t: Sed et bestiæ agri, id est homines qui tanquam jumenta utilia super sese portant onus et jugum Christi, et dicere possunt, Ut jumentum factus sum apud te, quasi area sitiens imbrem, id est cum ingenti affectu, suspexerunt ad te, a te illuminari, consolari ac perfici desiderantes; quoniam exsiccati sunt fontes aquarum, id est, sancti doctores ac prædicatores jam defecerunt ex magna parte, qui tanquam fontes aquæ sapientiæ salutaris, olim impleverunt audientium corda. Nunc autem etsi sint qui audire verbum salutis desiderent, desunt qui efficaciter dicant. Porro sapientes et virtuosæ personæ sunt tanquam fontes aquarum, de quarum plenitudine alii debent haurire fluenta scientiæ, accedendo ad eos, ut doceantur, ædificentur, et dirigantur. Tales fontes fuerunt Apostoli, de quibus cantatur: In Ecclesiis benedicite Deo Domino de fontibus Israel. De quibus et accipi potest illud Isaiæ: Haurietis aquas in gaudio de fontibus Salvatoris.
paras.en: [[1:20|Yea, and the beasts of the field|Sed et bestiæ agri]], that is, men who, like useful beasts of burden, carry upon themselves the burden and yoke of Christ, and can say, [[Ps 72:23|I am become as a beast before thee|Ut jumentum factus sum apud te]], [[1:20|as a garden bed that thirsteth after rain|quasi area sitiens imbrem]], that is, with great longing, [[1:20|have looked up to thee|suspexerunt ad te]], desiring to be enlightened, consoled and made perfect by thee; [[1:20|for the springs of waters are dried up|quoniam exsiccati sunt fontes aquarum]], that is, the holy doctors and preachers have now failed in great part, who, like springs of the [[Ecclus 15:3|water of wholesome wisdom|aquæ sapientiæ salutaris]], once filled the hearts of their hearers. But now, though there are some who desire to hear the word of salvation, there are none to speak it effectually. Further, wise and virtuous persons are like springs of waters, from whose fulness others ought to draw the streams of knowledge, going to them to be taught, edified and directed. Such springs were the Apostles, of whom it is sung: [[Ps 67:27|In the churches bless ye God the Lord, from the fountains of Israel|In Ecclesiis benedicite Deo Domino de fontibus Israel]]. Of them too that saying of Isaias can be taken: [[Is 12:3|Thou shall draw waters with joy out of the saviour's fountains|Haurietis aquas in gaudio de fontibus Salvatoris]].

2.title: Explanatio litteralis capituli secundi: Canite tuba in Sion.
2.title_en: Literal explanation of the second chapter: Blow ye the trumpet in Sion.

paras.t: Hoc loco describit Propheta apertius captivitatem regni Juda, de quo cœpit præcedenti capitulo vaticinari. Canite tuba, id est, sonora altaque voce prædicate quæ subduntur, in Sion, id est in Jerusalem vel in templo. Templum enim et civitas ex una parte fundata erat in monte Sion : ideo Sion quandoque significat urbem, interdum templum, aliquando ipsum montem. Ululate, o vos sacerdotes ac ceteri, in monte sancto meo, id est prædicto monte Sion, electo ad hoc ut in ipso templum construeretur. Conturbentur, id est, paveant atque pœniteant, omnes habitatores terræ Judææ, de qua jam sermo. Quia veniet dies Domini, id est dies in quo Dominus vindicabit peccata Judææ, sicut diu præfatus comminatusque est, quia prope est dies tenebrarum et caliginis, dies nubis et turbinis, id est dies plena miseriis, propter quod tot nominibus terribilium rerum exprimitur. In die etenim hoc erant tenebræ interiores in cordibus Judæorum, et caligo tribulationis seu adversitatis forinsecus; in locis quoque caliginosis se absconderunt. Fuit quoque tunc nubes, id est interpositio inter Deum et eos, ita quod non protegebantur ab eo, nec exaudiebantur : de qua Jeremias ait in Threnis, Opposuisti nubem ne transeat oratio. Fuit etiam tunc turbo tempestatis interioris et exterioris, omnem auferens quietem, tranquillitatem et pacem. Unde in Jeremia legitur : Ecce turbo dominicæ indignationis egredietur, et tempestas erumpens super caput impiorum veniet; non revertetur furor Domini usquedum faciat. Loquitur autem Jeremias ad litteram de eodem, de quo et Joel nunc fatur.
paras.en: In this place the Prophet describes more openly the captivity of the kingdom of Juda, which he began to foretell in the preceding chapter. [[2:1|Blow ye the trumpet|Canite tuba]], that is, proclaim with a loud and high voice what follows, [[2:1|in Sion|in Sion]], that is, in Jerusalem, or in the temple. For the temple and the city were founded in part on mount Sion: therefore *Sion* sometimes means the city, sometimes the temple, and sometimes the mountain itself. [[2:1|sound an alarm|Ululate]] [Latin *ululate*, that is, howl], O you priests and the rest, [[2:1|in my holy mountain|in monte sancto meo]], that is, on the aforesaid mount Sion, chosen for this, that the temple should be built upon it. Let [[2:1|all the inhabitants of the land|omnes habitatores terræ]] of Judæa, of which he is now speaking, [[2:1|tremble|Conturbentur]], that is, fear and repent. [[2:1|because the day of the Lord cometh|Quia veniet dies Domini]], that is, the day on which the Lord will avenge the sins of Judæa, as he has long foretold and threatened, [[2:1|because it is nigh at hand|quia prope est]], [[2:2|A day of darkness, and of gloominess, a day of clouds and whirlwinds|dies tenebrarum et caliginis, dies nubis et turbinis]]: that is, a day full of miseries, for which reason it is expressed by so many names of terrible things. For on that day there was inner darkness in the hearts of the Jews, and the gloom of tribulation or adversity without; and they hid themselves in gloomy places. There was also then a cloud, that is, something set between God and them, so that they were not protected by him, nor heard: of which Jeremias says in the Lamentations, [[Lam 3:44|Thou hast set a cloud before thee, that our prayer may not pass through|Opposuisti nubem ne transeat oratio]]. There was also then a whirlwind of tempest, inner and outer, taking away all quiet, tranquillity and peace. Hence we read in Jeremias: [[Jer 23:19|Behold the whirlwind of the Lord's indignation shall come forth, and a tempest shall break out and come upon the head of the wicked|Ecce turbo dominicæ indignationis egredietur, et tempestas erumpens super caput impiorum veniet]]; [[Jer 23:20|The wrath of the Lord shall not return till he execute it|non revertetur furor Domini usquedum faciat]]. Now Jeremias speaks, according to the letter, of the same thing of which Joel is now speaking.

paras.t: Quasi mane expansum super montes, id est, quemadmodum aurora, quum tetigerit cacumen montis, statim super totam terram diffunditur, populus multus et fortis, id est, sic veniet super Judæam universam festinantissime exercitus adversariorum magnus atque robustus. Videtur autem præcipue loqui de Babyloniis seu Chaldæis, secundum Hieronymum, quamvis intelligi possit de quolibet quatuor populorum dictorum, qui successive vastabant Judæos, videlicet Assyriorum, Chaldæorum, Græcorum, et Romanorum.
paras.en: [[2:2|as the morning spread upon the mountains|Quasi mane expansum super montes]], that is, as the dawn, when it has touched the top of a mountain, is at once spread over the whole land, [[2:2|a numerous and strong people|populus multus et fortis]]: that is, so will a great and mighty army of enemies come with the utmost speed upon all Judæa. Now according to Jerome he seems to speak chiefly of the Babylonians or Chaldeans, though it can be understood of any one of the four peoples already spoken of, who laid waste the Jews one after another, namely the Assyrians, the Chaldeans, the Greeks and the Romans.

paras.t: Similis ei non fuit a principio, et post eum non erit usque in annos generationis et generationis. Secundum hoc apparet, quod Propheta non loquitur nisi de uno speciali populo. Ad quod aliqui dicunt, quod quilibet prædictorum populorum, quoad aliquid, excessit : puta Assyrii in cupiditate, Chaldæi in ferocitate, Græci in dolositate, Romani in potestate. Sic namque de multis Sanctorum cantatur : Non est inventus similis illi. Sed sequendo Hieronymum et Glossam, iste est sensus : Similis in potestate ac feritate, ei, id est populo Chaldæorum venientium contra Jerusalem, non fuit a principio quo reges esse cœperunt in terra : omnia enim regna vicerunt; et post eum, id est post Chaldæos, non erit gens similis eis usque in annos generationis, id est usque ad tempus Alexandri Magni exclusive, qui in tota Græcia imperavit, eratque ipso Nabuchodonosor major atque potentior, et generationis, id est usque ad imperium Romanorum, quorum regnum dicitur ferreum a Daniele, eo quod omnia regna domuerint, sicut ferrum omnia domat.
paras.en: [[2:2|the like to it hath not been from the beginning, nor shall be after it, even to the years of generation and generation|Similis ei non fuit a principio, et post eum non erit usque in annos generationis et generationis]]. By this it appears that the Prophet is speaking of one particular people only. To this some answer that each of the aforesaid peoples excelled in some respect: the Assyrians, say, in covetousness, the Chaldeans in ferocity, the Greeks in guile, the Romans in power. For so it is sung of many of the Saints: [[Ecclus 44:20|there was not found the like to him|Non est inventus similis illi]] [words said of Abraham in Ecclesiasticus, and sung in the Church's office of holy confessors]. But following Jerome and the Gloss, the sense is this: [[2:2|the like|Similis]] in power and fierceness [[2:2|to it|ei]], that is, to the people of the Chaldeans coming against Jerusalem, [[2:2|hath not been from the beginning|non fuit a principio]] when kings first began to be on the earth: for they conquered all kingdoms; and [[2:2|after it|et post eum]], that is, after the Chaldeans, there [[2:2|shall be|non erit]] no nation like them [[2:2|even to the years of generation|usque in annos generationis]], that is, up to the time of Alexander the Great, exclusive [that is, up to but not including his time], who ruled over all Greece and was greater and mightier than Nabuchodonosor himself, [[2:2|and generation|et generationis]], that is, up to the empire of the Romans, whose kingdom is called iron by Daniel, because they subdued all kingdoms, as iron subdues all things[[Dan 2:40||]].

paras.t: Ante faciem ejus ignis vorans, id est, Chaldæi in suo accessu loca quæ poterant, incenderunt in terra Juda, scilicet villas et viculos; et post eum exurens flamma, id est, adepto triumpho, dum civitates egredi cœperunt, templum, Jerusalem, ac ceteras urbes Judææ combusserunt, ut patet quarto libro Regum et in Jeremia. Quasi hortus voluptatis, id est, sicut paradisus plenus est omni amœnitate, sic terra coram eo, id est, sic Judæa plena fuit divitiis, pulchra ac deliciosa, antequam Chaldæi eam ingressi sunt; et post eum, id est abeunte Chaldæorum exercitu, solitudo deserti, id est, terra ista ita vastata manebit et spoliata, quod solitudini similis erit. Unde per Jeremiam dixerat Dominus: In solitudinem redigam locum istum. Neque est qui effugiat eum. Hoc dicitur propter paucitatem Judæorum evadentium manus Chaldæorum. Aliqui tamen evaserunt, videlicet Johanan filius Caree cum aliis, de quibus in Jeremia habetur. Sedecias autem cum principibus fugiens, comprehensus est a Chaldæis.
paras.en: [[2:3|Before the face thereof a devouring fire|Ante faciem ejus ignis vorans]]: that is, the Chaldeans, as they came on, set fire to what places they could in the land of Juda, namely the villages and hamlets; [[2:3|and behind it a burning flame|et post eum exurens flamma]]: that is, having won the victory, when they began to leave the cities, they burned the temple, Jerusalem and the other cities of Judæa, as is plain from the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 25:9||]] and from Jeremias[[Jer 39:8||]][[Jer 52:13||]]. [[2:3|like a garden of pleasure|Quasi hortus voluptatis]]: that is, as paradise[[Gen 2:8||]] is full of every delight, so was [[2:3|the land|terra]] [[2:3|before it|coram eo]], that is, so was Judæa full of riches, fair and delightful, before the Chaldeans entered it; [[2:3|and behind it|et post eum]], that is, when the army of the Chaldeans goes away, [[2:3|a desolate wilderness|solitudo deserti]]: that is, this land will remain so laid waste and despoiled that it will be like a wilderness. Hence the Lord had said through Jeremias: I will bring this place to desolation[[Jer 22:5||]][[Jer 22:6||]][[Jer 25:9||]][[Jer 34:22||]] [the margin gives Jer. xxii, 5, 6; xxv, 9; xxxiv, 22, etc.; Denis sums up these threats in words of his own]. [[2:3|neither is there any one that can escape it|Neque est qui effugiat eum]]. This is said because so few of the Jews escaped the hands of the Chaldeans. Some, however, did escape, namely Johanan the son of Caree with others, of whom we read in Jeremias[[Jer 43:2||]]. But Sedecias, fleeing with the princes, was taken by the Chaldeans[[4 Kings 25:4||]][[4 Kings 25:5||]][[4 Kings 25:6||]].

paras.t: Quasi aspectus equorum, adspectus eorum, id est, Chaldæorum exercitus solo visu horribilis erit; et quasi equites, sic current, ita quod velocissimi erunt ac agiles, sicque Judæi fugere non valebunt.
paras.en: [[2:4|The appearance of them is as the appearance of horses|Quasi aspectus equorum, adspectus eorum]]: that is, the army of the Chaldeans will be dreadful at the mere sight; [[2:4|and they shall run like horsemen|et quasi equites, sic current]], so that they will be very swift and nimble, and so the Jews will not be able to flee.

paras.t: Sicut sonitus quadrigarum super capita montium exsilient, id est, cum grandi strepitu venient, cum fragore armorum, cum impetu exercituum, cum gressu celerrimo aviditate vastandi Judæos. Venient quoque sicut sonitus flammæ ignis devorantis stipulam, id est, omnia destruent, sicut flamma, quæ ignis est, devorat stipulam; velut populus fortis præparatus ad prælium, id est bene armatus et convenienter dispositus. Hæc dictio, Velut, dicit hic veritatem, non similitudinem tantum.
paras.en: [[2:5|They shall leap like the noise of chariots upon the tops of mountains|Sicut sonitus quadrigarum super capita montium exsilient]]: that is, they will come with a great din, with the crash of arms, with the onset of armies, with the swiftest step, in their eagerness to lay waste the Jews. They will come also [[2:5|like the noise of a flame of fire devouring the stubble|sicut sonitus flammæ ignis devorantis stipulam]]: that is, they will destroy all things, as the flame, which is fire, devours stubble; [[2:5|as a strong people prepared to battle|velut populus fortis præparatus ad prælium]]: that is, well armed and fittingly drawn up. This word [[2:5|as|Velut]] here expresses the truth, not a likeness only.

paras.t: A facie ejus cruciabuntur populi, id est, Judæi visis eis, in magno erunt timore ac desolatione; omnes vultus redigentur in ollam, id est, ollæ igni appositæ similes erunt. Quemadmodum enim hujusmodi olla fuligine atque nigredine maculatur, sic facies Judæorum præ timore et lacrimis quasi combusti parebunt, juxta illud in Threnis: Denigrata est super carbones facies eorum, et non sunt cogniti in plateis. Hoc quoque accidere potuit ex fumositate ignium quos in urbibus Judæorum succenderunt Chaldæi. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt: Omnes vultus sicut adustio ollæ.
paras.en: [[2:6|At their presence the people shall be in grievous pains|A facie ejus cruciabuntur populi]]: that is, the Jews, on seeing them, will be in great fear and desolation; [[2:6|all faces shall be made like a kettle|omnes vultus redigentur in ollam]]: that is, they will be like pots set on the fire. For as such a pot is stained with soot and blackness, so the faces of the Jews will look as if burnt, for fear and tears, according to that in the Lamentations: [[Lam 4:8|Their face is now made blacker than coals, and they are not known in the streets|Denigrata est super carbones facies eorum, et non sunt cogniti in plateis]]. This could also have come about from the smoke of the fires which the Chaldeans lit in the cities of the Jews. Hence the Septuagint translated: All faces as the burning of a pot.

paras.t: Sicut fortes current; quasi viri bellatores ascendent murum. In locis facilibus immorandum non arbitror. Istud autem ex præhabitis clarum est, scilicet quod Chaldæi per terram Judæ velocissime cucurrerunt, et murum Jerusalem ceterarumque urbium muros viriliter ascenderunt. Viri in viis suis gradientur, id est, Chaldæi ordinate procedent ad prælium, non nimis compresse, ne se invicem impediant, nec nimis separate, ne adversarii inter ipsos subintrent; et non declinabunt a semitis suis, id est a tam ordinato progressu, nec fugient, sed unusquisque locum vel hostem sibi occurrentem invadet.
paras.en: [[2:7|They shall run like valiant men: like men of war they shall scale the wall|Sicut fortes current; quasi viri bellatores ascendent murum]]. I do not think one should linger over easy places. This one is clear from what has been said: namely, that the Chaldeans ran through the land of Juda with the greatest speed, and manfully scaled the wall of Jerusalem[[4 Kings 25:4||]] and the walls of the other cities. [[2:7|the men shall march every one on his way|Viri in viis suis gradientur]]: that is, the Chaldeans will advance to battle in order, not too closely packed, lest they hinder one another, nor too far apart, lest the enemy slip in among them; [[2:7|and they shall not turn aside from their ranks|et non declinabunt a semitis suis]] [Latin *a semitis suis*, literally from their paths]: that is, from so orderly an advance, nor will they flee, but each will attack the place or the enemy that meets him.

paras.t: Unusquisque fratrem suum non coarctabit, id est, nullus de exercitu Chaldæorum, proximum suum Chaldæum per nimiam appropinquationem premet; singuli in calle suo ambulabunt, non declinando a semitis suis, ut dictum est. Sed et per fenestras cadent, id est, Chaldæi ostiis obseratis irruent per fenestras præ nimio desiderio occidendi Judæos, et non demolientur, id est, ex casu tali non conterentur neque lædentur, tanquam bene armati, vel circa talem modum cadendi experti.
paras.en: [[2:8|No one shall press upon his brother|Unusquisque fratrem suum non coarctabit]]: that is, no one in the army of the Chaldeans will press upon his neighbour, a fellow Chaldean, by coming too close; [[2:8|they shall walk every one in his path|singuli in calle suo ambulabunt]], so as not to [[2:7|turn aside from their ranks|declinando a semitis suis]], as was said. [[2:8|yea, and they shall fall through the windows|Sed et per fenestras cadent]]: that is, the Chaldeans, finding the doors barred, will rush in through the windows from their excessive desire to slay the Jews, [[2:8|and shall take no harm|et non demolientur]]: that is, they will not be crushed or hurt by such a fall, being well armed, or practised in that way of falling.

paras.t: Urbem Jerusalem ingredientur, in muro ejus current, considerando civitatem; domos Judæorum conscendent cum scalis vel similibus machinis, per fenestras intrabunt quasi fur, id est improvise et subito.
paras.en: [[2:9|They shall enter into the city|Urbem Jerusalem ingredientur]] of Jerusalem, [[2:9|they shall run upon the wall|in muro ejus current]] of it, surveying the city; [[2:9|they shall climb up the houses|domos Judæorum conscendent]] of the Jews with ladders or like engines, [[2:9|they shall come in at the windows, as a thief|per fenestras intrabunt quasi fur]]: that is, unforeseen and suddenly.

paras.t: A facie ejus, id est ex præsentia Chaldæorum, contremuit terra, id est, plebs Judæam inhabitans, timore concussa est. Vel sensus est, quod præ multitudine exercitus Chaldæorum, terra in qua incedebant, tremere videbatur. Moti sunt cœli, id est, Judæis in tribulatione positis, immutati a solito influxu, cursu vel statu videbantur. Patientibus quippe adversa præ terroris magnitudine cœlum ruere, et terra fluctuare videtur. Unde et Dominus comminatur se daturum perversis cœlum desuper ferreum, et terram æneam. Vel, Moti sunt cœli, id est cives cœlestes, scilicet angeli, hominum custodes : qui moti dicuntur, quoniam circa hominum punitionem inter se pugnare et sibi invicem resistere dicuntur, proponendo divino conspectui causas singulorum, prout Daniel plenius dicit : quod tamen fit sine discordia, secundum Gregorium, qui pugnam hanc exponit de angelis sanctis. Vel, moti sunt compassione, non quod compassionis affectus sit vere in eis, quum sint impassibiles, sed per modum compatientis se habent, succurrendo afflictis.
paras.en: [[2:10|At their presence|A facie ejus]], that is, from the presence of the Chaldeans, [[2:10|the earth hath trembled|contremuit terra]]: that is, the common people dwelling in Judæa were shaken with fear. Or the sense is that, for the multitude of the army of the Chaldeans, the land in which they marched seemed to tremble. [[2:10|the heavens are moved|Moti sunt cœli]]: that is, to the Jews set in tribulation they seemed changed from their wonted influence, course or state. For to those who suffer adversity the heaven seems to fall and the earth to heave, from the greatness of their terror. Hence the Lord too threatens that he will give the perverse [[Lev 26:19|the heaven above as iron, and the earth as brass|cœlum desuper ferreum, et terram æneam]]. Or, [[2:10|the heavens are moved|Moti sunt cœli]], that is, the citizens of heaven, namely the angels, the guardians of men: who are said to be moved because, concerning the punishment of men, they are said to fight among themselves and to resist one another, setting before the sight of God the causes of each, as Daniel says more fully[[Dan 10:13||]][[Dan 10:20||]]: which yet is done without discord, according to Gregory, who explains this fight as one of the holy angels. Or, they are *moved* with compassion: not that the feeling of compassion is truly in them, since they are impassible, but they behave after the manner of one who feels compassion, by succouring the afflicted.

paras.t: Sol et luna obtenebrati sunt, et stellæ retraxerunt splendorem suum. Quemadmodum in Deuteronomio Moyses scripsit, luminaria cœli condidit Deus in ministerium cunctis gentibus : idcirco dum homines in maximam devolvuntur calamitatem, cladem, pressuram, dicuntur contenebrari, mœrere et immutari. Unde quum Dominus in Ezechiele prædixisset dejectionem Pharaonis, adjecit : Operiam cœlos sacco, quum exstinctus fueris, et mœrere super te faciam luminaria cœli. Simili modo in Isaia, descripta Babylonis punitione, adjectum est : Stellæ cœli et splendor earum non expandent lumen suum; obscuratus est sol in ortu suo, et luna non splendebit in lumine suo. Hæc nempe est consuetudo prophetalis eloquii. Communiter quoque tempus adversitatis, vocamus tenebrosum et nubilum. Verum, ut tangit Glossa, per solem intelligi potest rex Juda, a Chaldæis devictus, præcipue Sedecias; per lunam, regina; per stellas, principes regis, qui quum a Chaldæis comprehenderentur, in tenebras, hoc est in magnam infortuniorum caliginem versi sunt.
paras.en: [[2:10|the sun and moon are darkened, and the stars have withdrawn their shining|Sol et luna obtenebrati sunt, et stellæ retraxerunt splendorem suum]]. As Moses wrote in Deuteronomy, God made the lights of heaven [[Deut 4:19|for the service of all the nations|in ministerium cunctis gentibus]]: therefore, when men are cast down into the greatest calamity, disaster and affliction, these are said to be darkened, to mourn and to be changed. Hence when the Lord in Ezechiel had foretold the overthrow of Pharao, he added: [[Ezech 32:7|I will cover the heavens, when thou shalt be put out|Operiam cœlos sacco, quum exstinctus fueris]] [Denis's wording adds *sacco*, with sackcloth], and [[Ezech 32:8|I will make all the lights of heaven to mourn over thee|mœrere super te faciam luminaria cœli]]. In like manner in Isaias, after the punishment of Babylon has been described, it is added: [[Is 13:10|the stars of heaven, and their brightness shall not display their light: the sun shall be darkened in his rising, and the moon shall not shine with her light|Stellæ cœli et splendor earum non expandent lumen suum; obscuratus est sol in ortu suo, et luna non splendebit in lumine suo]]. For this is the custom of prophetic speech. We too commonly call a time of adversity dark and cloudy. But, as the Gloss touches on, by the *sun* can be understood the king of Juda, overcome by the Chaldeans, chiefly Sedecias; by the *moon*, the queen; by the *stars*, the king's princes, who, when they were taken by the Chaldeans, were turned into darkness, that is, into a great gloom of misfortunes.

paras.t: Et Dominus dedit vocem suam ante faciem exercitus sui : id est, exercitui Chaldæorum, qui dicitur exercitus Dei, tanquam divinæ exsecutor justitiæ, dedit Deus virtutem terrendi Judæos et potenter vociferandi contra omnes, ita quod clamor et fama præcedens omnes perterruit, conveniretque Judæis, quod ab Isaia de aliis dicitur : Torsiones et dolores tenebunt quasi parturientis, et cor omne tabescet. Quia multa sunt nimis castra ejus, id est, exercitus Chaldæorum (qui dicuntur castra vel exercitus Dei, quia divina voluntate contra Judæos venerunt) sunt valde copiosi numero et virtute. Propter quod subditur : quia fortia et facientia verbum ejus, id est, propheticam annuntiationem implentes, qua Deus per Prophetas annuntiavit captivitatem Judæorum a Chaldæis. Hanc enim multi Prophetæ præfati sunt, maxime Jeremias. Vel, Facientia verbum ejus, id est, verbo interioris inspirationis consentientes, quo inspiratum fuerat eis contra Judæos venire. Hinc enim in Jeremia Deus nominat Nabuchodonosor servum suum.
paras.en: [[2:11|And the Lord hath uttered his voice before the face of his army|Et Dominus dedit vocem suam ante faciem exercitus sui]]: that is, to the army of the Chaldeans, which is called the army of God as the executor of divine justice, God gave power to terrify the Jews and to cry out mightily against all, so that the clamour and the report going before them struck terror into all, and there befell the Jews what Isaias says of others: [[Is 13:8|Gripings and pains, shall take hold of them|Torsiones et dolores tenebunt]], as of a woman in labour, and [[Is 13:7|every heart of man shall melt|cor omne tabescet]] [Denis joins Is 13:8 and 13:7, in words of his own]. [[2:11|for his armies are exceedingly great|Quia multa sunt nimis castra ejus]] [Latin *castra*, literally camps]: that is, the hosts of the Chaldeans (who are called the camps or army of God, because they came against the Jews by the will of God) are very abundant in number and strength. For which reason it is added: [[2:11|for they are strong, and execute his word|quia fortia et facientia verbum ejus]]: that is, fulfilling the prophetic announcement by which God announced through the Prophets the captivity of the Jews by the Chaldeans. For many Prophets foretold it, Jeremias most of all. Or, [[2:11|execute his word|Facientia verbum ejus]]: that is, consenting to the word of inner inspiration by which it had been inspired in them to come against the Jews. For hence in Jeremias God calls Nabuchodonosor his servant.

paras.t: Magnus enim dies Domini, et terribilis valde : id est, dies quo Deus per Chaldæos puniet regnum Juda, erit magnus, id est districtæ atque justissimæ ultionis, et terribilis, his qui in eo horrenda patientur tormenta. Dicitur enim dies magnus, propter magna quæ in eo fiunt, aut facta commemorantur. Et generaliter tempus accipit denominationem ab his quæ in eo geruntur. Hinc enim dies mali dicuntur; et, Sufficit diei malitia sua. Et Michæas disseruit : Non ambulabitis superbi, quoniam tempus pessimum est. Nihilo minus dicit Apostolus : Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile. Et tempore nihil pretiosius fertur. Et quis sustinebit eum? id est, quis Judæorum poterit tam dira ferre supplicia, aut manus evadere Chaldæorum? De hoc etenim terribili die Dominus dixit per Ezechielem : Conflabo vos, et succendam vos in igne furoris mei ; et conflabimini in medio ejus, sicut conflatur argentum in medio fornacis.
paras.en: [[2:11|for the day of the Lord is great and very terrible|Magnus enim dies Domini, et terribilis valde]]: that is, the day on which God will punish the kingdom of Juda through the Chaldeans will be *great*, that is, a day of strict and most just vengeance, and *terrible* to those who will suffer dreadful torments in it. For a day is called great because of the great things that are done in it, or that are recalled as done. And generally a time takes its name from the things that are done in it. Hence days are called evil; and, [[Matt 6:34|Sufficient for the day is the evil thereof|Sufficit diei malitia sua]]. And Micheas declared: [[Mich 2:3|you shall not walk haughtily, for this is a very evil time|Non ambulabitis superbi, quoniam tempus pessimum est]]. No less does the Apostle say: [[2 Cor 6:2|Behold, now is the acceptable time|Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile]]. And nothing is said to be more precious than time. [[2:11|and who can stand it?|Et quis sustinebit eum?]] That is, which of the Jews will be able to bear such dire punishments, or escape the hands of the Chaldeans? For of this terrible day the Lord said through Ezechiel: [[Ezech 22:20|I will melt you down|Conflabo vos]], and [[Ezech 22:21|will burn you in the fire of my wrath, and you shall be melted in the midst thereof|succendam vos in igne furoris mei ; et conflabimini in medio ejus]], [[Ezech 22:22|As silver is melted in the midst of the furnace|sicut conflatur argentum in medio fornacis]].

paras.t: Hucusque posita est comminatio Dei, et instantis persecutionis prophetalis prænuntiatio. Consequenter inducitur ad pœnitentiam admonitio salutaris. Nunc ergo dicit Dominus, id est, prædicta comminatus est Dominus mala per me, ut faciatis quæ sequuntur, et evadatis atque salvemini. Convertimini ad me, conversione perfecta et integra, utpote in toto corde vestro, id est intellectu et voluntate, per fidem, caritatem et opera, ne vobis conveniat quod de reprobis dictum est in Osee : Divisum est cor eorum; nunc interibunt. Cor autem hoc loco pro anima (cujus vires sunt intellectus et voluntas) vel pro superiori parte animæ sumitur. Sic conversus fuit ad Deum Psalmista, qui toties profitetur : Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto corde meo. Denique, opportune docentur Judæi hoc modo converti ad Dominum, quoniam in exterioribus observantiis et cærimonialibus justificationibus superflue confidebant, quia non erant vere interni atque devoti. Propter hoc Christus in Evangelio de hypocrisi maxime arguit Scribas et Pharisæos; et per Isaiam testatus est : Populus hic labiis me honorat, cor autem eorum longe est a me.
paras.en: Up to this point God's threat has been set down, and the prophetic foretelling of the persecution at hand. Next comes a wholesome exhortation to penance. [[2:12|Now, therefore, saith the Lord|Nunc ergo dicit Dominus]]: that is, the Lord has threatened the aforesaid evils through me so that you may do what follows, and escape and be saved. [[2:12|Be converted to me|Convertimini ad me]] with a perfect and entire conversion, that is, [[2:12|with all your heart|in toto corde vestro]], that is, with understanding and will, through faith, charity and works, lest what is said of the reprobate in Osee befit you: [[Osee 10:2|Their heart is divided: now they shall perish|Divisum est cor eorum; nunc interibunt]]. Now *heart* is taken here for the soul (whose powers are understanding and will), or for the higher part of the soul. So was the Psalmist converted to God, who so often professes: [[Ps 9:2|I will give praise to thee, O Lord, with my whole heart|Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto corde meo]][[Ps 110:1||]][[Ps 137:1||]]. Moreover, the Jews are fittingly taught to be converted to the Lord in this way, because they trusted overmuch in outward observances and ceremonial justifications, since they were not truly inward and devout. For this reason Christ in the Gospel reproves the Scribes and Pharisees above all for hypocrisy[[Matt 23:28||]][[Luke 12:1||]]; and through Isaias he testified: [[Matt 15:8|This people honoureth me with their lips: but their heart is far from me|Populus hic labiis me honorat, cor autem eorum longe est a me]][[Is 29:13||]] [Denis gives the words of Isaias in the form in which Christ quotes them in Matt 15:8].

paras.t: In jejunio, quod est actus abstinentiæ ac temperantiæ, et fletu pro propriis ac alienis peccatis, qui est actus pœnitentiæ, et planctu, pro desiderio gratiæ in præsenti, et gloriæ in futuro, vel pro liberatione ab imminente captivitate : qui fletus causatur ex caritate.
paras.en: [[2:12|in fasting|In jejunio]], which is an act of abstinence and temperance, [[2:12|and in weeping|et fletu]] for one's own and others' sins, which is an act of penance, [[2:12|and mourning|et planctu]], out of desire for grace in the present and glory in the future, or for deliverance from the captivity that threatens: which weeping is caused by charity.

paras.t: Et scindite corda vestra, ejus lapideam duritiam abjiciendo, malas cogitationes expellendo, et ad divinæ gratiæ receptionem illud in omnibus disponendo. Porro hæc scissio præinductæ totalitati qua ad Deum converti præcipimur, non repugnat, sed præparat ad eamdem, quia utrumque est spirituale. Denique scissio ista aliud prorsus non est, nisi spiritualis circumcisio, ad quam in Deuteronomio admonet Moyses : Circumcidite præputium cordis vestri, et cervicem vestram ne induretis amplius. Unde de Judæis ita non scissis in corde, scriptum est apud Jeremiam : Omnes gentes habent præputium, omnis autem domus Israel incircumcisi sunt corde. Hæc itaque scissio, est peccatorum et passionum ejectio. Et non vestimenta vestra. Solebant Judæi vestes lacerare, dum blasphemiam audierunt, vel gravem inciderunt mœrorem seu adversitatem. Unde et audita Christi responsione, Caiphas scidit vestimenta sua, dicens : Blasphemavit. Jubentur ergo Judæi corda magis quam indumenta scindere, et in interioribus potius quam in exterioribus perfectionem ac pœnitentiæ veritatem reponere. Non tamen, ut arbitror, absolute prohibetur scissio vestium in casibus præinductis, quum fuerit consuetudo laudabilis, dum convenienter circumstantionata exstiterat. Hinc enim Paulus et Barnabas vestimenta sua scidisse scribuntur, dum idolorum sacerdos voluit eis sacrificare. Aliqui autem dicunt, quod Judæi habuerunt vanitatem quamdam, quam et Christiani plurimi habent, in corporali vestium fractilatione seu scissione, et dicunt hoc eis prohiberi verbis præhabitis.
paras.en: [[2:13|And rend your hearts|Et scindite corda vestra]], by casting away its stony hardness, driving out evil thoughts, and disposing it in all things to receive divine grace. And this rending is not at odds with the wholeness spoken of above, with which we are commanded to be converted to God, but prepares for it, since both are spiritual. Indeed this rending is nothing else at all than spiritual circumcision, to which Moses exhorts in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 10:16|Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and stiffen your neck no more|Circumcidite præputium cordis vestri, et cervicem vestram ne induretis amplius]]. Hence of the Jews not thus rent in heart it is written in Jeremias: [[Jer 9:26|all the nations are uncircumcised in the flesh, but all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in the heart|Omnes gentes habent præputium, omnis autem domus Israel incircumcisi sunt corde]]. This rending, then, is the casting out of sins and passions. [[2:13|and not your garments|Et non vestimenta vestra]]. The Jews used to tear their clothes when they heard blasphemy, or fell into grievous sorrow or adversity. Hence, when he had heard Christ's answer, Caiphas [[Matt 26:65|rent his garments, saying: He hath blasphemed|scidit vestimenta sua, dicens : Blasphemavit]]. The Jews are therefore bidden to rend their hearts rather than their clothing, and to place perfection and the truth of penance in inward things rather than outward. Yet, as I think, the rending of garments in the cases mentioned is not forbidden absolutely, since it was a praiseworthy custom when done in fitting circumstances. For hence Paul and Barnabas are written to have rent their garments when the priest of the idols wished to sacrifice to them[[Acts 14:13||]]. But some say that the Jews had a certain vanity, which very many Christians have too, in the bodily tearing or rending of garments, and they say that this is forbidden them by the words given above.

paras.t: Et convertimini ad Dominum Deum vestrum, in quo tota salus vestra consistit, a quo peccando aversi, elongati, et abalienati fuistis. Non enim nisi ad Deum verum debet nostra finalis esse conversio, juxta illud Jeremiæ : Si reverteris, Israel, ad me convertere. Quia benignus in se ipso, id est naturaliter bonus et pius. Propter quod dicit Psalmista : Laudate Dominum, quia bonus Dominus ; psallite nomini ejus, quoniam suave. Et misericors est per effectum, id est clemens in ignoscendo, auxiliando, salvando. Misericors dicitur quasi cor miserum habens, in quantum miseriam alterius quasi propriam accipit. Sic autem Deus non appellatur misericors, sed per similitudinem operis et bonitatis caritatisque effectum, in quantum aliorum miseriam relevat, quasi esset ipsius.
paras.en: [[2:13|and turn to the Lord your God|Et convertimini ad Dominum Deum vestrum]], in whom all your salvation consists, from whom by sinning you have been turned away, removed far off and estranged. For our final conversion must be to none but the true God, according to that of Jeremias: [[Jer 4:1|If thou wilt return, O Israel|Si reverteris, Israel]], [[Jer 4:1|return to me|ad me convertere]]. [[2:13|for he is gracious|Quia benignus]] in himself, that is, by nature good and kind. For which reason the Psalmist says: [[Ps 134:3|Praise ye the Lord, for the Lord is good: sing ye to his name, for it is sweet|Laudate Dominum, quia bonus Dominus ; psallite nomini ejus, quoniam suave]]. [[2:13|and merciful|Et misericors est]] in effect, that is, clement in pardoning, helping, saving. One is called *merciful* [Latin *misericors*, as if *miserum cor*, a wretched heart] as having a heart made wretched, inasmuch as he takes another's misery as his own. But God is not called merciful in this way, but by likeness of work and by the effect of goodness and charity, inasmuch as he relieves the misery of others as though it were his own.

paras.t: Patiens, non statim ulciscendo, sed impiorum conversionem ac pœnitentiam longanimiter præstolando. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico habetur : Altissimus est patiens redditor ; atque in Psalmo : Deus judex justus, fortis et patiens. Si autem patiens dicatur a patientia, quæ est virtus moralis passionem tristitiæ frenans ac moderans, sic Deus non est patiens, nisi eo modo quo fertur misericors et iratus, vel etiam contristatus, quum dicat Apostolus : Nolite contristare Spiritum Sanctum Dei. Et in Genesi dicitur : Tactus dolore cordis intrinsecus.
paras.en: [[2:13|patient|Patiens]], not taking vengeance at once, but awaiting with long-suffering the conversion and penance of the wicked. For which reason we have in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 5:4|the most High is a patient rewarder|Altissimus est patiens redditor]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 7:12|God is a just judge, strong and patient|Deus judex justus, fortis et patiens]]. But if *patient* is said from patience, which is the moral virtue that bridles and moderates the passion of sorrow, then God is not patient, except in the way in which he is said to be merciful and angry, or even grieved, since the Apostle says: [[Eph 4:30|grieve not the holy Spirit of God|Nolite contristare Spiritum Sanctum Dei]]. And in Genesis it is said: [[Gen 6:6|being touched inwardly with sorrow of heart|Tactus dolore cordis intrinsecus]].

paras.t: Et multæ misericordiæ, propter diversitatem effectuum divinæ clementiæ. Quamvis enim misericordia Dei in se una simplexque consistat, nihilo minus multa vocatur propter diversos effectus. Mille etenim modis novit Deus suis succurrere. Propter quod orat Psalmista : Secundum multitudinem miserationum tuarum respice in me. Rursusque ait : Misericordias Domini in æternum cantabo. Et præstabilis super malitia, id est, indulgentiam præstans post conversionem de malo pœnæ quod fuerat comminatus, ita quod non infert malum pœnæ veraciter pœnitenti. Sumitur enim hoc loco, secundum Hieronymum, malitia pro tormento, de quo loquitur Amos : Si erit malum in civitate, quod Dominus non fecit? Hinc apud Jeremiam loquitur Deus : Si pœnitentiam egerit gens illa a malo suo, quod locutus sum adversus eam, agam et ego pœnitentiam super malo quod cogitavi ut facerem ei.
paras.en: [[2:13|and rich in mercy|Et multæ misericordiæ]] [literally of many mercies], because of the diversity of the effects of the divine clemency. For although the mercy of God in itself is one and simple, it is nonetheless called *many* because of its diverse effects. For God knows a thousand ways to succour his own[[2 Pet 2:9||]]. For which reason the Psalmist prays: [[Ps 68:17|look upon me according to the multitude of thy tender mercies|Secundum multitudinem miserationum tuarum respice in me]]. And again he says: [[Ps 88:2|The mercies of the Lord I will sing for ever|Misericordias Domini in æternum cantabo]]. [[2:13|and ready to repent of the evil|Et præstabilis super malitia]] [Denis takes *præstabilis* from *præstare*, to grant]: that is, granting indulgence, after conversion, from the evil of punishment that he had threatened, so that he does not inflict the evil of punishment on one who truly repents. For *evil* [Latin *malitia*] is taken here, according to Jerome, for torment, of which Amos speaks: [[Amos 3:6|Shall there be evil in a city, which the Lord hath not done?|Si erit malum in civitate, quod Dominus non fecit?]] Hence in Jeremias God says: [[Jer 18:8|If that nation against which I have spoken, shall repent of their evil, I also will repent of the evil that I have thought to do to them|Si pœnitentiam egerit gens illa a malo suo, quod locutus sum adversus eam, agam et ego pœnitentiam super malo quod cogitavi ut facerem ei]].

paras.t: His verbis magnifice commendatur nobis superineffabilis misericordia Dei, ita ut maximam Deo injuriam faciat, atque in Spiritum Sanctum peccet, qui desperat. Hinc quoque habetur in Psalmo : Et tu, Domine Deus, miserator et misericors, patiens et multæ misericordiæ et verax. Itemque in Exodo : Dominator Domine, misericors et clemens, patiens et multæ misericordiæ, et verax, qui custodis misericordiam in millia, qui aufers iniquitatem et scelera atque peccata.
paras.en: By these words the more than ineffable mercy of God is splendidly commended to us, so that he who despairs does God the greatest injury, and sins against the Holy Ghost. Hence too we have in the Psalm: [[Ps 85:15|And thou, O Lord, art a God of compassion, and merciful, patient, and of much mercy, and true|Et tu, Domine Deus, miserator et misericors, patiens et multæ misericordiæ et verax]]. And likewise in Exodus: [[Ex 34:6|O the Lord, the Lord God, merciful and gracious, patient and of much compassion, and true|Dominator Domine, misericors et clemens, patiens et multæ misericordiæ, et verax]], [[Ex 34:7|Who keepest mercy unto thousands: who takest away iniquity, and wickedness, and sin|qui custodis misericordiam in millia, qui aufers iniquitatem et scelera atque peccata]].

paras.t: Quis scit si convertatur et ignoscat Deus? Verba ista dupliciter accipi possunt. Primo, per modum perterritionis, tanquam dicat Propheta : Multa jam dixi de misericordia Dei, sed sententiam repeto, nec debetis præsumere vel peccare in spe, aut fieri negligentes : quis enim scit (id est, impossibile vel difficile est scire) an Deus ab ira sua et comminatione convertatur ad indulgendum ? quoniam in aliquibus suis sententiis inflexibilis invenitur implacabilisque quibusdam, sicut ad Jeremiam testatur de obduratis Judæis : Si steterint Moyses et Samuel coram me, non est anima mea ad populum istum. Et Salomon : Quem ille (inquit) despexerit, nemo corrigere potest. Verumtamen dubium non est quin his qui toto corde convertuntur ad Deum, ignoscat.
paras.en: [[2:14|Who knoweth but he will return, and forgive|Quis scit si convertatur et ignoscat Deus]]? These words can be taken in two ways. First, by way of striking fear, as though the Prophet were saying: I have now said much of the mercy of God, but I repeat the sentence, and you must not presume, or sin in hope, or grow negligent: for who knows (that is, it is impossible or difficult to know) whether God will turn from his wrath and threatening to pardon? For in some of his sentences he is found inflexible, and implacable towards certain men, as he testifies to Jeremias concerning the hardened Jews: [[Jer 15:1|If Moses and Samuel shall stand before me, my soul is not towards this people|Si steterint Moyses et Samuel coram me, non est anima mea ad populum istum]]. And Solomon: [[Eccles 7:14|whom he|Quem ille]] (he says) [[Eccles 7:14|hath despised|despexerit]], [[Eccles 7:14|no man can correct|nemo corrigere potest]]. Yet there is no doubt that he forgives those who turn to God with their whole heart.

paras.t: Secundo leguntur hæc verba per modum consolationis et provocationis ad pœnitentiam, quasi dicat sanctus Joel : Quamvis jam multa prædixi, o Judæi, de vestra mox futura captivitate, nihilo minus pœnitentiam agite, et nolite diffidere : quis enim scit si convertatur a rigore justitiæ ad lenitatem clementiæ, et ignoscat vobis Deus, et relinquat post se benedictionem, id est, post visitationem et castigationem parcat, gratiamque infundat, et beneficia sua multiplicet ? tanquam diceret : Prophetica prænuntiatio aliquando pertinet ad prophetiam prædestinationis, quæ semper impletur, ita quod in illa Deus nequaquam convertitur ; quandoque autem ad prophetiam comminationis, quæ sæpe per preces vel pœnitentiam impeditur, sicut de morte Ezechiæ, subversioneque Ninive. Sic in proposito dubium est an prophetica revelatio mihi de vestra captivitate facta, sit prædestinationis vel comminationis vaticinium : et hoc certo sciri non potest, nisi Deus revelet.
paras.en: Secondly, these words are read by way of consolation and of rousing to penance, as though holy Joel were saying: Although I have now foretold many things, O Jews, of your captivity soon to come, nonetheless do penance, and do not lose hope: for [[2:14|who knoweth but he will return|quis enim scit si convertatur]] from the rigour of justice to the mildness of clemency, [[2:14|and forgive|et ignoscat]] you (God, that is), [[2:14|and leave a blessing behind him|et relinquat post se benedictionem]], that is, after the visitation and chastisement spare you, and pour in grace, and multiply his benefits? As if he said: Prophetic foretelling sometimes belongs to the prophecy of predestination, which is always fulfilled, so that in it God in no way turns; but sometimes to the prophecy of threatening [that is, a prophecy of what will come unless men amend, as against one of what God has decreed shall come], which is often hindered by prayers or penance, as with the death of Ezechias and the overthrow of Ninive[[Is 38:1||]][[Jon 3:4||]]. So in the present case it is doubtful whether the prophetic revelation made to me of your captivity is a prophecy of predestination or of threatening; and this cannot be known for certain unless God reveals it.

paras.t: Dicunt quoque nonnulli, quod Joel nescivit ad quod genus prophetiæ pertineret vaticinatio sua de præinductis punitionibus Judæorum. Hoc tamen non arbitror certum. Quamvis enim dicat, Quis scit si convertatur, etc.? non excludit se ipsum, sed innuit quod impossibile vel difficile sit hoc sciri, et paucis admodum vel nemini constet. Verumtamen certum est quod Spiritus Sanctus, qui secundum beneplacitum suum tangit animas Prophetarum, eas clarius seu obscurius illustrando, interdum sic futura revelat Prophetis, quod licet sciant talia sibi divinitus revelata, ignorant tamen utrum ad prædestinationis vel comminationis pertineant prophetiam : ut constat in Jona, qui scivit sibi a Deo prædictum de Ninive subversione, sed ignoravit an hoc infallibiliter impleretur, vel per illorum pœnitentiam impediretur.
paras.en: Some also say that Joel did not know to which kind of prophecy his foretelling of the punishments of the Jews, set out above, belonged. Yet I do not think this certain. For although he says, [[2:14|Who knoweth but he will return|Quis scit si convertatur]], etc.? he does not exclude himself, but hints that it is impossible or difficult for this to be known, and that it is clear to very few or to none. Yet it is certain that the Holy Ghost, who touches the souls of the Prophets according to his good pleasure, enlightening them more clearly or more obscurely, sometimes reveals the future to the Prophets in such a way that, though they know such things have been revealed to them by God, they do not know whether they belong to the prophecy of predestination or of threatening: as is clear in Jonas, who knew that the overthrow of Ninive had been foretold to him by God[[Jon 3:4||]], but did not know whether it would be infallibly fulfilled, or hindered by their penance.

paras.t: Hæc verba Joelis dixit etiam rex Ninive : Quis, inquit, scit si convertatur et ignoscat Deus, et revertatur a furore iræ suæ, et non peribimus? Dicitur autem Deus converti, non quod varietur in se, sed quoniam aliter et aliter se habet ad nos. Juxta quod scriptum est in Psalmo : Deus, tu conversus vivificabis nos.
paras.en: The king of Ninive also said these words of Joel: [[Jon 3:9|Who|Quis]], he says, [[Jon 3:9|can tell if God will turn, and forgive: and will turn away from his fierce anger, and we shall not perish?|scit si convertatur et ignoscat Deus, et revertatur a furore iræ suæ, et non peribimus?]] Now God is said to turn, not because he varies in himself, but because he stands towards us now in one way, now in another; according to what is written in the Psalm: [[Ps 84:7|Thou wilt turn, O God, and bring us to life|Deus, tu conversus vivificabis nos]].

paras.t: Sacrificium, id est oblatio de solidis, et libamen, id est oblatio de liquidis (ut dictum est plenius), Domino Deo nostro offerantur pro venia impetranda.
paras.en: [[2:14|sacrifice|Sacrificium]], that is, an offering of solid things, [[2:14|and libation|et libamen]], that is, an offering of liquids (as was said more fully above[[Joel 1:9||]]), are to be offered [[2:14|to the Lord your God|Domino Deo nostro]] [Denis reads nostro, “our God”] to obtain pardon.

paras.t: Consequenter Dominus præcipit Prophetis, sacerdotibus, sive doctoribus Synagogæ : Canite tuba in Sion : quod in principio expositum fuit; sanctificate jejunium, id est, abstinentiam corporalem adornate per abstinentiam a peccatis, vocate cœtum, congregate populum, sanctificate ecclesiam, id est, collectionem fidelium ad cordis puritatem disponite, vel sceleratos a synagoga excludite, coadunate senes, congregate parvulos, et sugentes ubera, id est, omnem prorsus differentiam plebis colligite, ut pariter invocent Dominum, sicque multitudinis oratio celeriter sortiatur effectum. Infantes quoque adducantur, ut cum parentibus Domino præsentati, tempore necessitatis atque angustiæ oculos divinæ pietatis ad misericordiam provocent. Hoc Judæi facere consueverunt, ut patet secundo Paralipomenon. Egrediatur sponsus de cubili suo, et sponsa de thalamo suo, id est, etiam noviter copulati, carnali amplexu suspenso, ad communem orationis confluant locum, ut in tanto periculo precibus vacent, non voluptati.
paras.en: Next the Lord commands the Prophets, the priests or teachers of the Synagogue: [[2:15|Blow the trumpet in Sion|Canite tuba in Sion]], which was explained at the beginning[[2:1||]]; [[2:15|sanctify a fast|sanctificate jejunium]], that is, adorn bodily abstinence with abstinence from sins; [[2:15|call a solemn assembly|vocate cœtum]], [[2:16|Gather together the people, sanctify the church|congregate populum, sanctificate ecclesiam]], that is, dispose the gathering of the faithful to purity of heart, or shut the wicked out of the synagogue; [[2:16|assemble the ancients, gather together the little ones, and them that suck at the breasts|coadunate senes, congregate parvulos, et sugentes ubera]], that is, gather together every kind of people without exception, that they may call upon the Lord together, and so the prayer of the multitude may quickly obtain its effect. Let the infants also be brought, so that, presented to the Lord with their parents, in a time of need and distress they may move the eyes of the divine goodness to mercy. This the Jews were accustomed to do, as is clear from the second book of Paralipomenon[[2 Par 20:13||]]. Then: [[2:16|let the bridegroom go forth from his bed, and the bride out of her bridal chamber|Egrediatur sponsus de cubili suo, et sponsa de thalamo suo]], that is, let even the newly wedded, refraining from carnal embrace, flock to the common place of prayer, so that in so great a danger they may give themselves to prayers, not to pleasure.

paras.t: Inter vestibulum et altare plorabunt sacerdotes. Secundum Glossam, duplex fuit altare : unum in templo, quod vocabatur altare incensi ; aliud in porticu ante fores templi, quod dicebatur altare holocaustorum. Itaque sensus est : Inter vestibulum et altare, id est in spatio existenti inter altare incensi et altare holocaustorum, plorabunt sacerdotes pro suis ac populi culpis. Ipsi enim debebant portare peccata populi Israel, et gratiam impetrare subjectis, quum fuerint medii inter Deum et plebem. Ministri Domini, quia ad cultum templi et altaris singulariter electi ac deputati, ut dictum est clarius. Et dicent : Parce, Domine, parce populo tuo, id est, Judæis a pœnis debitis propitieris. Repetitio, Parce, seriositatis et magnæ affectionis indicium est. Parce ergo, o Domine, malum culpæ clementer delendo; parce, mala pœnæ tollendo. Et ne des hereditatem tuam, id est populum Judæorum, de quo per Isaiam locutus es, Hereditas mea Israel; et Psalmista, Salvum fac populum tuum, Domine, et benedic hereditati tuæ ; in opprobrium, id est, in confusibilem subjectionem, ut dominentur eis nationes, puta Chaldæi, seu aliæ gentes. Unde et Jeremias orat : Ne des nos in opprobrium propter nomen tuum, neque facias nobis contumeliam. Vile enim atque probrosum est fidelibus, infidelibus tradi ac subjici.
paras.en: [[2:17|Between the porch and the altar the priests|Inter vestibulum et altare plorabunt sacerdotes]]. According to the Gloss, there were two altars: one in the temple, which was called the altar of incense; the other in the porch before the doors of the temple, which was called the altar of holocausts. So the sense is: Between the porch and the altar, that is, in the space lying between the altar of incense and the altar of holocausts, the priests shall weep for their own faults and the people’s. For it was theirs to [[Num 18:23|bear the sins of the people|portare peccata populi]] of Israel[[Ex 28:38||]], and to obtain grace for those under them, since they were mediators between God and the people. [[2:17|the Lord’s ministers|Ministri Domini]], because they were singularly chosen and appointed to the service of the temple and the altar, as was said more clearly above[[Joel 1:9||]]. [[2:17|and shall say: Spare, O Lord, spare thy people|Et dicent : Parce, Domine, parce populo tuo]], that is, be merciful to the Jews and spare them the punishments due. The repetition, Spare, is a sign of earnestness and great affection. Spare, then, O Lord, by mercifully blotting out the evil of guilt; spare, by taking away the evils of punishment. [[2:17|and give not thy inheritance|Et ne des hereditatem tuam]], that is, the people of the Jews, of whom thou hast spoken through Isaias: [[Is 19:25|Israel is my inheritance|Hereditas mea Israel]]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 27:9|Save, O Lord, thy people, and bless thy inheritance|Salvum fac populum tuum, Domine, et benedic hereditati tuæ]]; [[2:17|to reproach|in opprobrium]], that is, to a shameful subjection, [[2:17|that the heathens should rule over them|ut dominentur eis nationes]], namely the Chaldeans, or other nations. Hence Jeremias too prays: [[Jer 14:21|Give us not to be a reproach, for thy name's sake, and do not disgrace|Ne des nos in opprobrium propter nomen tuum, neque facias nobis contumeliam]] us. For it is a vile and shameful thing for the faithful to be handed over and made subject to unbelievers.

paras.t: Deinde ait : Quare dicunt in populis, id est, cur nationes dicunt de Judæis, Ubi est Deus eorum ? quasi dicant : Non potest eos defendere. Sic enim dixerunt gentiles prævalentes Judæis, Deum verum blasphemando, et populum ejus subsannando quod frustra coleret Deum suum. Et quia hoc cedit ad inhonorationem et injuriam Dei, Moyses et alii Prophetæ frequenter deprecati sunt Deum, ut gratiam populo suo impenderet, ne talia verba dicerentur a gentibus. Propter quod orat Psalmista : Non nobis, Domine, non nobis; sed nomini tuo da gloriam; super misericordia tua et veritate tua, ne forte dicant in gentibus, Ubi est Deus eorum? Et in Isaia Dominus asserit : Propter me ego faciam, ut non blasphemer. Unde jam subditur :
paras.en: Then he says: [[2:17|Why should they say among the nations|Quare dicunt in populis]], that is, why do the nations say of the Jews, [[2:17|Where is their God|Ubi est Deus eorum]]? as if they said: He cannot defend them. For so the gentiles spoke when they prevailed over the Jews, blaspheming the true God, and mocking his people for worshipping their God in vain. And because this tends to the dishonour and injury of God, Moses and the other Prophets often besought God[[Ex 32:12||]] to bestow grace on his people, lest such words be spoken by the gentiles. For this reason the Psalmist prays: [[Ps 113:9|Not to us, O Lord, not to us; but to thy name give glory.|Non nobis, Domine, non nobis; sed nomini tuo da gloriam]] [[Ps 113:10|For thy mercy, and for thy truth's sake: lest the Gentiles should say: Where is their God?|super misericordia tua et veritate tua, ne forte dicant in gentibus, Ubi est Deus eorum?]] [the margin gives Ps. cxiii, 1, 2 “according to the Hebrew”, that is, the Hebrew Psalm 115; in the Vulgate these are Ps 113:9–10]. And in Isaias the Lord declares: [[Is 48:11|for my own sake will I do it, that I may not be blasphemed|Propter me ego faciam, ut non blasphemer]]. Hence there now follows:

paras.t: Zelatus est Dominus terram suam, id est, populum suum afflictum et pœnitentem dilexit, et pepercit populo suo ne abundantiori tristitia absorberetur.
paras.en: [[2:18|The Lord hath been zealous for his land|Zelatus est Dominus terram suam]], that is, he loved his people, afflicted and penitent, [[2:18|and hath spared his people|et pepercit populo suo]], lest it be swallowed up by too great sorrow.

paras.t: Propterea modo subjungitur consolatio populi. Et respondit Dominus, vel per Prophetas loquendo, vel operibus populi pœnitentis vicem reddendo : quod est respondere non ad verba, sed facta ; estque reale responsum. Secundum quem modum dicitur Deus sæpe in Scripturis hominibus respondisse, quando videlicet juxta exigentiam actuum humanorum proportionabiliter reddit seu facit. Sic et Isaias profatur : Peccata nostra responderunt nobis.
paras.en: Therefore the consolation of the people is now added. [[2:19|And the Lord answered|Et respondit Dominus]], either by speaking through the Prophets, or by repaying the works of the penitent people in kind: which is to answer not words but deeds; and it is a real answer [that is, an answer given in things done, not in words]. In this way God is often said in the Scriptures to have answered men, namely when he repays or acts in due proportion to what human acts call for. So too Isaias declares: [[Is 59:12|our sins have testified against us|Peccata nostra responderunt nobis]] [the Latin responderunt is literally “have answered”, the word used of the Lord in this verse].

paras.t: Et dixit Dominus populo suo promittens eis bona post exercitationem in malo : Ecce ego mittam vobis frumentum, et vinum, et oleum, id est, terra fertilis erit, et omnia victui necessaria gignentur in ea abundanter, et replebimini in eis, id est, usque ad sufficientiam eis vescemini. Hoc factum est sub Ezechia, contritis ab angelo Assyriis in terra Juda. Alii dicunt, istud impletum post famem quæ fuit tempore Eliæ et Achab, vel eam quæ erat sub Eliseo et Joram rege Israel. Denique de fertilitate illa sub Ezechia, in Isaia clarissime legitur. Misit quoque Dominus populo Juda frumentum, vinum et oleum, quoniam Assyriis interfectis, victualia quæ secum attulerant, manserunt Judæis, sicut et cetera spolia.
paras.en: [[2:19|and said to his people|Et dixit Dominus populo suo]], promising them good things after their trial in evil: [[2:19|Behold I will send you corn, and wine, and oil|Ecce ego mittam vobis frumentum, et vinum, et oleum]], that is, the land shall be fruitful, and all things needful for food shall be brought forth in it in abundance, [[2:19|and you shall be filled with them|et replebimini in eis]], that is, you shall eat of them to sufficiency. This was done under Ezechias, when the Assyrians had been crushed by the angel in the land of Juda[[4 Kings 19:35||]]. Others say that this was fulfilled after the famine that was in the time of Elias and Achab[[3 Kings 18:2||]], or the one that was under Eliseus and Joram king of Israel[[4 Kings 4:38||]][[4 Kings 6:25||]]. Lastly, of that fruitfulness under Ezechias one reads most clearly in Isaias[[Is 37:30||]][[4 Kings 19:29||]]. The Lord also sent the people of Juda corn, wine and oil, since, when the Assyrians had been slain, the provisions they had brought with them were left to the Jews, as were the rest of the spoils.

paras.t: Et non dabo vos ultra opprobrium in gentibus, id est, infidelium potestati ac servituti ultra non tradam vos. Quod intelligi potest dupliciter : Primo, conditionaliter, utpote si in Dei servitio fideliter steterint. Sic enim divinæ promissiones factæ regibus et populo veteris Testamenti communiter intelliguntur. Secundo, quod dictio, Ultra, non dicit perpetuitatem, sed notabilem durationem, quemadmodum in Isaia habetur : Non levabit gens ultra gladium contra gentem, nec exercebuntur ultra ad prælium. Et quarto libro Regum narratur, quod Syri non apposuerunt ultra venire in terram Israel, postquam Eliseus duxit eos quadam cæcitate percussos ad regem Israel in Samaria : et tamen illic mox subditur, quod rex Syriæ congregato exercitu, ingressus est terram Israel.
paras.en: [[2:19|and I will no more make you a reproach among the nations|Et non dabo vos ultra opprobrium in gentibus]], that is, I will no more hand you over to the power and bondage of unbelievers. This can be understood in two ways. First, conditionally, namely if they stand faithfully in the service of God; for so the divine promises made to the kings and people of the old Testament are commonly understood. Secondly, in that the word No more [Latin ultra, “any further”] does not mean perpetuity but a notable length of time; as we have in Isaias: [[Is 2:4|nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they be exercised any more to war|Non levabit gens ultra gladium contra gentem, nec exercebuntur ultra ad prælium]]. And in the fourth book of Kings it is told that the Syrians came no more into the land of Israel[[4 Kings 6:23||]], after Eliseus had led them, struck with a kind of blindness, to the king of Israel in Samaria; and yet it is added there soon after that the king of Syria gathered an army and entered the land of Israel[[4 Kings 6:24||]].

paras.t: Et eum qui ab aquilone est, id est regem ac populum Assyriorum habitantem in partibus Aquilonis, procul faciam a vobis : quando videlicet angelus Domini una nocte percussit in castris Assyriorum centum octoginta quinque millia.
