Et expellam eum in terram inviam et desertam. Rex enim Assyriorum percussus non fuit plaga illa, sed cum paucis fugit, et per deserta loca in propria rediit confusus, pavensque. Faciem ejus contra mare orientale, id est primam partem exercitus Assyriorum respicientem ad mare orientale, et extremum ejus, id est ultimam partem sui exercitus respicientem ad mare novissimum, expellam a vobis, totum pene exercitum per angelum occidendo. Mare enim orientale nunc dicitur, quod vergit ad orientem, ubi olim erant Sodoma et Gomorrha, Adama et Seboim, nuncque vocatur mare Mortuum, quoniam nullum animal manet vivum in eo. Mare vero occidentale appellatur, quod est ad occidentem, et ducit in Ægyptum, in cujus littore Ascalon, Azotus, Gaza, Joppe, Cæsarea sunt, etc.
paras.en: [[2:20|the northern enemy|Et eum qui ab aquilone est]], that is, the king and people of the Assyrians dwelling in the regions of the North, [[2:20|I will remove far off from you|procul faciam a vobis]]: namely when the angel of the Lord in one night [[4 Kings 19:35|slew in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and eighty-five thousand|percussit in castris Assyriorum centum octoginta quinque millia]]. [[2:20|and I will drive him into a land unpassable, and desert|Et expellam eum in terram inviam et desertam]]. For the king of the Assyrians was not struck by that blow, but fled with a few, and returned through desert places to his own land, confounded and afraid[[4 Kings 19:36||]]. [[2:20|with his face towards the east sea|Faciem ejus contra mare orientale]], that is, the first part of the army of the Assyrians, facing the eastern sea, [[2:20|and his hinder part|et extremum ejus]], that is, the last part of his army, facing [[2:20|towards the utmost sea|ad mare novissimum]], I will drive away from you, slaying almost the whole army by the angel. For the eastern sea is so called because it lies towards the east, where Sodom and Gomorrha, Adama and Seboim once were; and it is now called the Dead Sea, because no living creature stays alive in it. But the western sea is the one that lies to the west and leads to Egypt, on whose shore are Ascalon, Azotus, Gaza, Joppe, Cæsarea, etc.

paras.t: Et ascendet fœtor ejus, et ascendet putredo ejus. Hoc non videtur ad litteram accipi posse de Assyriis ab angelo interfectis, quia illorum corpora in cinerem sunt redacta, et igne consumpta. Unde Glossa dicit hoc mystice intelligendum. Hieronymus vero dicit, quod Propheta sic loquitur, quoniam servat metaphoram de locustis cœptam, quarum cadavera magnum causant fœtorem in aere. Videtur quoque de rege Assyriorum litteraliter dictum atque impletum, qui a propriis filiis ignominiose occisus, in fœtorem et putredinem versus est. Quia superbe egit contra Judæos, ut patet quarto Regum. Maximas enim blasphemias scripsit ad Ezechiam : Non te, inquiens, decipiat Deus tuus, qui non poterit te salvare de manu hac. Unde apud Isaiam Dominus ait ad eum : Quum fureres contra me, superbia tua ascendit in aures meas. Ex quo patet, stultam esse expositionem eorum qui ista de locustis exponunt ; et argumenta eorum ex nunc dictis soluta sunt. Non enim quum alicujus populi pœna describitur, necesse est omnia ad singulos pertinere, sed frequenter transit Scriptura de parte ad totum, et econverso.
paras.en: [[2:20|and his stench shall ascend, and his rottenness shall go up|Et ascendet fœtor ejus, et ascendet putredo ejus]]. This does not seem able to be taken literally of the Assyrians slain by the angel, since their bodies were reduced to ashes and consumed by fire. Hence the Gloss says that this is to be understood mystically. Jerome, however, says that the Prophet speaks thus because he keeps up the metaphor of the locusts begun earlier, whose carcasses cause a great stench in the air. It also seems to have been said, and fulfilled, literally of the king of the Assyrians, who, shamefully slain by his own sons[[4 Kings 19:37||]], was turned to stench and rottenness. [[2:20|because he hath done proudly|Quia superbe egit]] against the Jews, as is clear from the fourth book of Kings. For he wrote the greatest blasphemies to Ezechias: [[Is 37:10|Let not|Non te]], he said, [[Is 37:10|thy God deceive thee|decipiat Deus tuus]], who [[4 Kings 18:29|shall not be able to deliver|non poterit te salvare]] thee out of this hand [the margin gives Is 37:10 and 4 Kings 18:29; the letter itself is at 4 Kings 19:10]. Hence in Isaias the Lord says to him: [[Is 37:29|When thou wast mad against me, thy pride came up to my ears|Quum fureres contra me, superbia tua ascendit in aures meas]]. From this it is clear that the exposition of those who expound these things of locusts is foolish, and their arguments are answered by what has just been said. For when the punishment of some people is described, it is not necessary that everything should apply to each one; but Scripture often passes from the part to the whole, and the other way about.

paras.t: Consequenter inducitur beneficiorum promissio, et consolatio Judæorum. Promittitque Dominus bona præinductis malis pœnalibus directe contraria. Noli timere timore mundano, carnali, et inordinato, nimis metuendo de futura caristia, sterilitate, pressura, terra, id est, plebs Judaica habitans in Judæa ; exsulta et lætare, quoniam magnificavit Dominus, id est, magnifice prænuntiavit et egit, ut faceret, id est, abundantiam victualium tribueret vobis, sicut spopondit.
paras.en: Next is brought in the promise of benefits and the consolation of the Jews; and the Lord promises good things directly contrary to the penal evils set out before. [[2:21|Fear not|Noli timere]] with a worldly, carnal and inordinate fear, dreading too much the dearth, barrenness and distress to come, [[2:21|O land|terra]], that is, the Jewish people dwelling in Judea; [[2:21|be glad, and rejoice: for the Lord hath done great things|exsulta et lætare, quoniam magnificavit Dominus]], that is, has magnificently foretold and done it, that he might do it [Latin ut faceret, words the Douay-Rheims takes into “hath done great things”], that is, that he might grant you abundance of provisions, as he promised[[4 Kings 19:29||]].

paras.t: Nolite timere, animalia regionis, id est, jumenta et bestiæ silvestres in regno Juda manentes ; quia germinaverunt, id est, fructum fecerunt, speciosa deserti, id est campi spatiosi, et arbores in desertis plantatæ. Ideo subditur : quia lignum attulit fructum suum, id est, arbores fructuosæ fuerunt, ficus et vinea dederunt virtutem suam, id est, fecunditatem et largitatem ostenderunt, præbendo hominibus uvas et ficus. Sumitur autem hoc loco ficus pro arbore, puta ficulnea. Denique Propheta loquebatur de futura fertilitate et abundantia terræ per modum præteriti. Alloquitur quoque irrationabilia animalia : non quod putaverit ea suam intelligere vocem, vel quod haberent timorem proprie dictum de futura sterilitate ac fame, quum non præconcipiant talia, nisi forte naturali quodam instinctu ; sed alloquitur talia, ut homines ad intelligentiam advertentiamque inducat, quemadmodum quotidie provocamus universa creata ad laudem benedictionemque Dei, dicendo : Benedicite, omnia opera Domini, Domino ; benedicite, bestiæ et pecora, Domino ; laudate Dominum de terra, dracones, etc.
paras.en: [[2:22|Fear not, ye beasts of the fields|Nolite timere, animalia regionis]], that is, the beasts of burden and the wild beasts living in the kingdom of Juda; for [[2:22|the beautiful places of the wilderness|speciosa deserti]], that is, the spacious plains, and the trees planted in the deserts, [[2:22|are sprung|germinaverunt]], that is, have borne fruit. Therefore it is added: [[2:22|for the tree hath brought forth its fruit|quia lignum attulit fructum suum]], that is, the trees were fruitful, [[2:22|the fig tree, and the vine have yielded their strength|ficus et vinea dederunt virtutem suam]], that is, they showed fruitfulness and bounty, yielding grapes and figs to men. Here fig (ficus) is taken for the tree, that is, the fig tree [ficus can mean the fruit or the tree; Denis adds ficulnea, which means the tree only]. Further, the Prophet was speaking of the future fertility and abundance of the land in the manner of the past. He also addresses the irrational animals: not that he thought they understood his voice, or that they had fear, properly so called, of the barrenness and famine to come, since they do not foresee such things, except perhaps by a certain natural instinct; but he addresses such creatures in order to lead men to understanding and attention, just as daily we call upon all created things to the praise and blessing of God, saying: [[Dan 3:57|All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord|Benedicite, omnia opera Domini, Domino]]; ye [[Dan 3:81|beasts and cattle, bless the Lord|benedicite, bestiæ et pecora, Domino]]; [[Ps 148:7|Praise the Lord from the earth, ye dragons|laudate Dominum de terra, dracones]], etc.

paras.t: Et filiæ Sion, id est, habitatores Jerusalem, omnisque populus Judæorum, qui frequenter per Sion significatur, exsultate et lætamini in Domino Deo vestro, tanquam in objecto, fonte, causa ac fine omnis sanctæ lætitiæ, id est in consideratione bonitatis beneficiorumque ejus ; quia dedit vobis doctorem justitiæ. Per hunc doctorem, quidam intelligunt ipsum prophetam Joelem et similes sibi, quos Deus dedit tunc ad Judæorum eruditionem. Potest quoque referri ad Christum, de quo dictum est in Osee : Tempus requirendi Dominum, quum venerit qui docebit vos justitiam. Frequenter namque Prophetæ loquendo de rebus sui temporis, oculos cordis convertunt ad tempus atque mysteria Christi, cujus beneficia spiritualia, per corporalia beneficia Judæis ante collata, præfigurabantur. Dicit hic quidam, quod aliqui dicunt Joelem prophetasse tempore Elisei, et quod Hieronymus dicat eum antea prophetasse, videlicet tempore Isaiæ. Verum si historia libri Regum rite pensetur, invenitur Isaias non præcessisse Eliseum, sed magis econtra. Eliseus enim defunctus est decem tribubus nondum captis : post quarum captivitatem diu prophetavit et vixit Isaias, usque ad tempus Manassæ ; cœpit tamen prophetare ante decem tribuum captivitatem.
paras.en: [[2:23|And you, O children of Sion|Et filiæ Sion]] [Denis reads filiæ, “daughters”, where the Vulgate has filii, “children”], that is, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all the people of the Jews, which is often signified by Sion, [[2:23|rejoice, and be joyful in the Lord your God|exsultate et lætamini in Domino Deo vestro]], as in the object, fountain, cause and end of all holy gladness, that is, in the consideration of his goodness and his benefits; [[2:23|because he hath given you a teacher of justice|quia dedit vobis doctorem justitiæ]]. By this teacher some understand the prophet Joel himself and those like him, whom God gave at that time for the instruction of the Jews. It can also be referred to Christ, of whom it is said in Osee: [[Osee 10:12|the time to seek the Lord is, when he shall come that shall teach you justice|Tempus requirendi Dominum, quum venerit qui docebit vos justitiam]]. For the Prophets often, when speaking of the things of their own time, turn the eyes of the heart to the time and the mysteries of Christ, whose spiritual benefits were prefigured by the bodily benefits bestowed on the Jews before. A certain writer says here that some say Joel prophesied in the time of Eliseus, and that Jerome says he prophesied earlier, namely in the time of Isaias. But if the history of the book of Kings is rightly weighed, it is found that Isaias did not come before Eliseus, but rather the contrary. For Eliseus died[[4 Kings 13:20||]] while the ten tribes had not yet been taken captive[[4 Kings 15:29||]][[4 Kings 17:6||]]; after their captivity Isaias prophesied and lived a long time, until the time of Manasses; yet he began to prophesy before the captivity of the ten tribes[[Is 1:1||]].

paras.t: Et descendere faciet ad vos imbrem matutinum, id est pluviam aptam et fecundantem, quum semen in terram projicitur, et serotinum, id est aptum tempore messis, secundum Glossam, sicut in principio dedit, quum non peccassent in eum filii Israel, et antequam sterilitas præinducta illata est.
paras.en: [[2:23|and he will make the early|Et descendere faciet ad vos imbrem matutinum]] rain to come down to you, that is, rain that is suited and makes fruitful when the seed is cast into the earth, [[2:23|and the latter|et serotinum]], that is, suited to the time of harvest, according to the Gloss, [[2:23|as in the beginning|sicut in principio]] he gave it, when the children of Israel had not sinned against him, and before the barrenness spoken of above was brought upon them.

paras.t: Et implebuntur areæ, id est horrea, frumento, et redundabunt torcularia vino et oleo, id est, in torcularibus vinum et oleum copiose excutientur.
paras.en: [[2:24|And the floors shall be filled|Et implebuntur areæ]], that is, the barns, [[2:24|with wheat|frumento]], [[2:24|and the presses shall overflow with wine, and oil|et redundabunt torcularia vino et oleo]], that is, wine and oil shall be pressed out in abundance in the presses.

paras.t: Et reddam vobis annos quos comedit locusta, bruchus, et rubigo, et eruca, id est, annos tantæ fertilitatis dabo vobis, quanta fuit sterilitas annorum quorum fructus et germina devoraverunt Assyrii vel Chaldæi, per locustam et bruchum significati, vel animalia illa minuta : qui Assyrii vel quæ bestiolæ erant fortitudo mea magna, id est potens effectus omnipotentiæ meæ, quia per illos potenter et rigorose ultus sum vestra peccata, et demolitus germina vestra ; quam fortitudinem misi in vos puniendos per illam.
paras.en: [[2:25|And I will restore to you the years which the locust, and the bruchus, and the mildew, and the palmerworm hath eaten|Et reddam vobis annos quos comedit locusta, bruchus, et rubigo, et eruca]], that is, I will give you years of as great fertility as was the barrenness of the years whose fruits and shoots the Assyrians or Chaldeans devoured, who are signified by the locust and the bruchus; or else those little creatures themselves: which Assyrians, or which little beasts, were [[2:25|my great host|fortitudo mea magna]] [Latin fortitudo, literally “strength”], that is, the mighty working of my omnipotence, because through them I mightily and rigorously avenged your sins and destroyed your crops; [[2:25|which|quam]] strength [[2:25|I sent upon you|misi in vos]], to punish you by it.

paras.t: Et comedetis vescentes fructibus terræ, et saturabimini, id est, sufficientiam multam habebitis, et laudabitis nomen Domini Dei vestri, qui fecit mirabilia vobiscum, id est, qui primo mirabiliter vos afflixit et castigavit, et nunc mirabilem copiam rerum contulit, et consolationem miraculosam ac maximam post vehementem tribulationem induxit, ita ut vere dicatis : Hæc mutatio dexteræ Excelsi. Hoc totum fecerunt ac perceperunt Judæi sub Ezechia occisis Assyriis.
paras.en: [[2:26|And you shall eat in plenty|Et comedetis vescentes]] [Latin vescentes, literally “feeding”], feeding on the fruits of the earth, [[2:26|and shall be filled|et saturabimini]], that is, you shall have great sufficiency, [[2:26|and you shall praise the name of the Lord your God; who hath done wonders with you|et laudabitis nomen Domini Dei vestri, qui fecit mirabilia vobiscum]], that is, who first wondrously afflicted and chastised you, and has now bestowed a wonderful abundance of things, and brought in a miraculous and very great consolation after vehement tribulation, so that you may truly say: [[Ps 76:11|this is the change of the right hand of the most High|Hæc mutatio dexteræ Excelsi]]. All this the Jews did and received under Ezechias, when the Assyrians had been slain.

paras.t: Et non confundetur populus meus in æternum, dummodo in cultu meo perseveraverit. Vel, licet temporalem incurrat confusionem, illa tamen non semper durabit, sed æternaliter salvus erit populus prædestinatus, pœnitens, patiensque in adversis. Quidam asserit in Hebræo haberi, Non confundetur populus meus in sæculum. Per quod non perpetuitas designatur, sed tempus usque ad jubilæum, quamvis jubilæus per modicos distet annos. Sed Hieronymi ita et Septuaginta interpretum translatio habet, In æternum. Unde potius puto, quod verbum Hebraicum sit æquivocum ad utrumque. Tales tamen promissiones intelligendæ sunt conditionaliter, vel pro tempore ultra solitum magno, quemadmodum secundo Regum Dominus dixit per Nathan ad David de filiis Israel : Habitabo cum eis, et non turbabuntur amplius, nec addent filii iniquitatis ut affligant eum sicut prius. Idem quoque habetur primo libro Paralipomenon. Insuper quod dictum est, Non confundetur populus meus in æternum, intelligi potest præcise de his qui erant sub Ezechia, de quibus Propheta nunc loquitur, nec oportet eadem de universis posteris verificari. Ezechias autem toto tempore vitæ suæ post occisionem Assyriorum magnam habuit pacem.
paras.en: [[2:26|and my people shall not be confounded for ever|Et non confundetur populus meus in æternum]] [Denis reads in æternum; the Vulgate has in sempiternum, with the same meaning], so long as it perseveres in my worship. Or: though it incur temporal confusion, that will not last for ever, but the people that is predestined, penitent, and patient in adversity, shall be saved eternally. A certain writer asserts that the Hebrew has: My people shall not be confounded unto the age [Latin in sæculum]; by which not perpetuity is signified, but the time up to the jubilee, although the jubilee is but a few years distant. But the translation of Jerome, and likewise that of the Seventy, has For ever. Hence I rather think that the Hebrew word is equivocal, bearing either sense. Such promises, however, are to be understood conditionally, or of a time unusually long, as in the second book of Kings the Lord said through Nathan to David of the children of Israel: I will dwell with them, and they [[2 Kings 7:10|shall be disturbed no more: neither shall the children of iniquity afflict them any more as they did before|non turbabuntur amplius, nec addent filii iniquitatis ut affligant eum sicut prius]] [Denis quotes freely; the words I will dwell with them are not in the verse]. The same is found also in the first book of Paralipomenon[[1 Par 17:9||]]. Moreover, what was said, [[2:26|my people shall not be confounded for ever|Non confundetur populus meus in æternum]], can be understood precisely of those who were under Ezechias, of whom the Prophet is now speaking; nor need the same be verified of all their descendants. And Ezechias had great peace for the whole time of his life after the slaughter of the Assyrians[[2 Par 32:22||]].

paras.t: Et scietis per harum promissionum impletionem atque effectum, seu beneficiorum meorum collationem, quia, id est quod, in medio Israel, id est Judæorum, ego sum per gratiam specialem tanquam in populo peculiari. Unde per Moysen Dominus ait frequenter : Ego sum qui habito in medio filiorum Israel. Et ego Dominus Deus vester per singularem providentiam qua vos guberno, et de necessariis ad salutem provideo, et non est amplius ; et non confundetur populus meus in æternum, id est, ab hostibus non vincetur, nec contumeliis afficietur, secundum sensum jam tactum.
paras.en: [[2:27|And you shall know|Et scietis]], by the fulfilment and effect of these promises, or by the bestowal of my benefits, [[2:27|that|quia]] [Denis glosses quia with quod: here it means “that”, not “because”] [[2:27|in the midst of Israel|in medio Israel]], that is, of the Jews, [[2:27|I am|ego sum]] by special grace, as in a peculiar people. Hence the Lord often says through Moses: I am he [[Num 35:34|that dwell among the children of Israel|qui habito in medio filiorum Israel]]. [[2:27|and I am the Lord your God|Et ego Dominus Deus vester]], by the singular providence by which I govern you and provide you with what is needful for salvation, [[2:27|and there is none besides|et non est amplius]]; [[2:27|and my people shall not be confounded forever|et non confundetur populus meus in æternum]], that is, it shall not be conquered by enemies, nor treated with insult, in the sense already touched on.

paras.t: Postremo, in Scripturis veteris Testamenti ubertim promittit Deus Judæis sua præcepta servantibus temporalium copiam rerum. Sed quum temporalia bona seu corporales divitiæ non sint dignum atque efficiens præmium actuum virtuosorum (qui quum ex caritate procedant, meritorii sunt vitæ æternæ), innotescit quod sub tali promissione implicite intelligatur promissio remunerationis quantum ad spiritualia bona, quæ sunt dona gratiæ in præsenti, et munera gloriæ in futuro. Rudi etenim populo promittenda erant temporalia bona, ut per ea ad Dei alliceretur obsequium, a cujus famulatu aliter recessisset.
paras.en: Lastly, in the Scriptures of the old Testament God abundantly promises the Jews who keep his precepts a plenty of temporal things. But since temporal goods or bodily riches are not a worthy and effectual reward of virtuous acts (which, when they proceed from charity, are meritorious of eternal life), it becomes plain that under such a promise there is implicitly understood a promise of reward in spiritual goods, which are the gifts of grace in the present and the rewards of glory in the future. For temporal goods had to be promised to an unschooled people, so that by them it might be drawn to the service of God, from whose service it would otherwise have withdrawn.

2.title: Expositio tropologica ejusdem capituli secundi.
2.title_en: Tropological exposition of the same second chapter.

paras.t: Prædicatoribus, doctoribus, atque prælatis Ecclesiæ dicitur : Canite tuba, id est, voce sonora, fiduciali, affectuosa, prædicate, in Sion, id est in Ecclesia, quæ speculando cœlestia Sion vocatur. Sion nempe speculatio interpretatur. Ululate in monte sancto meo, id est in Ecclesia militanti, quæ conversationem habendo in cœlis, atque angelicam vitam ducendo in terris, mons sanctus nominatur, de quo scriptum est in Isaia : Venite, ascendamus ad montem Domini, et ad domum Dei nostri. Unde in Daniele lapis sine manibus præcisus, fertur crevisse in montem magnum, constituendo universalem Ecclesiam toto orbe diffusam. Hinc ad Hebræos legitur : Accessistis ad montem Sion, et ad civitatem Dei viventis. In hoc igitur monte ululandum est, ex consideratione defectus fidelium, in quibus prævalente peccato caritas refrigescit. Jam enim status Ecclesiæ ad magnum devolutus est lapsum, et tantam in ea est videre miseriam in pessima conversatione multorum, ut ardens Dei zelator, fratrumque verus amator, dicere habeat cum Jeremia : Deducant oculi mei lacrimas per diem et noctem, et non taceant, quoniam contritione magna contrita est virgo filia populi mei.
paras.en: To the preachers, doctors and prelates of the Church it is said: [[2:1|Blow ye the trumpet|Canite tuba]], that is, preach with a voice that is resounding, confident and full of feeling, [[2:1|in Sion|in Sion]], that is, in the Church, which is called Sion from its contemplating heavenly things; for Sion is interpreted *contemplation* [*speculatio*, a looking out, as from a watch-tower]. [[2:1|sound an alarm in my holy mountain|Ululate in monte sancto meo]] [*ululate*, literally howl or wail], that is, in the Church militant, which is named the holy mountain because it has its conversation in heaven[[Phil 3:20||]] and leads the life of angels on earth; of which it is written in Isaias: [[Is 2:3|Come and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord|Venite, ascendamus ad montem Domini]], and to the house of our God [Isaias has *of the God of Jacob*]. Hence in Daniel the stone cut out without hands is said to have grown into a great mountain[[Dan 2:34||]][[Dan 2:35||]], by forming the universal Church spread throughout the whole world. Hence we read in Hebrews: [[Heb 12:22|you are come to mount Sion and to the city of the living God|Accessistis ad montem Sion, et ad civitatem Dei viventis]]. On this mountain, then, we must howl, at the thought of the falling away of the faithful, in whom, as sin prevails, charity grows cold[[Matt 24:12||]]. For the state of the Church has now sunk into a great decline, and so great a misery is to be seen in it in the most wicked conduct of many, that an ardent zealot for God and a true lover of his brethren may well say with Jeremias: [[Jer 14:17|Let my eyes shed down tears night and day, and let them not cease, because the virgin daughter of my people is afflicted with a great affliction|Deducant oculi mei lacrimas per diem et noctem, et non taceant, quoniam contritione magna contrita est virgo filia populi mei]].

paras.t: Conturbentur omnes habitatores terræ, id est, homines universi sua pensando peccata, timore et tremore concutiantur, et pœnitentiam agant. Hæc autem conturbatio bona est, pacem carnalem, vanam securitatem, corporalisque delectationis tollens quietem. De qua ait Psalmista : Anima mea turbata est valde ; et Isaias, Conturbatus sum, inquiens, quum viderem. Sic enim turbari debemus, audiendo verba Dei increpatoria, comminatoria, aut vindicatoria, secundum quod Jeremias scribit : Contritum est cor meum in medio mei, contremuerunt omnia ossa mea a facie Domini, et a facie verborum sanctorum ejus. Quia veniet dies Domini, id est hora generalis seu particularis judicii, quo nihil est horribilius. Hinc et Jacobus dicit : Adventus Domini appropinquabit ; ecce judex ante januam adsistit.
paras.en: [[2:1|let all the inhabitants of the land tremble|Conturbentur omnes habitatores terræ]], that is, let all men, weighing their sins, be shaken with fear and trembling, and do penance. This disturbance is good, for it takes away carnal peace, vain security, and the repose of bodily pleasure. Of it the Psalmist says: [[Ps 6:4|my soul is troubled exceedingly|Anima mea turbata est valde]]; and Isaias: [[Is 21:3|I was troubled|Conturbatus sum]], he says, [[Is 21:3|at the seeing of it|quum viderem]]. For so we ought to be troubled when we hear the words of God that rebuke, threaten or avenge, as Jeremias writes: [[Jer 23:9|My heart is broken within me, all my bones tremble|Contritum est cor meum in medio mei, contremuerunt omnia ossa mea]] [[Jer 23:9|at the presence of the Lord, and at the presence of his holy words|a facie Domini, et a facie verborum sanctorum ejus]]. [[2:1|because the day of the Lord cometh|Quia veniet dies Domini]], that is, the hour of the general or of the particular judgment [that is, of the Last Judgment, or of the judgment of each soul at death], than which nothing is more dreadful. Hence James too says: [[Jas 5:8|the coming of the Lord is at hand|Adventus Domini appropinquabit]]; [[Jas 5:9|Behold the judge standeth before the door|ecce judex ante januam adsistit]].

paras.t: Quia prope est dies tenebrarum et caliginis, dies nubis et turbinis. Tantus enim horror mortis est et utriusque judicii, quod explicari non potest. Sed et dies Domini, tanquam fur in nocte, ita veniet. Nubes quoque et caligo in circuitu ejus; et in circuitu ejus tempestas valida.
paras.en: [[2:1|because it is nigh at hand|Quia prope est]]: [[2:2|A day of darkness, and of gloominess, a day of clouds and whirlwinds|dies tenebrarum et caliginis, dies nubis et turbinis]]. For so great is the horror of death and of both judgments that it cannot be told. But also [[1 Thess 5:2|the day of the Lord shall so come as a thief in the night|dies Domini, tanquam fur in nocte, ita veniet]]. And [[Ps 96:2|Clouds and darkness are round about him|Nubes quoque et caligo in circuitu ejus]]; and [[Ps 49:3|a mighty tempest shall be round about him|in circuitu ejus tempestas valida]].

paras.t: Quasi mane expansum super montes, populus multus et fortis : id est, sicut lux auroræ a cacumine montis per totam terram repente diffunditur; sic populus multus et fortis, id est angelorum exercitus, cujus ministerio consummabitur judicium, subito a cœlo per universum orbem discurret, cineres suscitandorum colligendo, suscitatosque nondum glorificatos ad judicii locum portando. Similis ei non fuit a principio. Nulla enim gens exercitui angelico potest comparari.
paras.en: [[2:2|as the morning spread upon the mountains|Quasi mane expansum super montes]], [[2:2|a numerous and strong people|populus multus et fortis]]: that is, as the light of dawn is suddenly spread from the top of a mountain over the whole land, so a numerous and strong people, that is, the army of angels, by whose ministry the judgment will be accomplished, will suddenly run from heaven through the whole world, gathering the ashes of those who are to be raised, and carrying them, raised but not yet glorified, to the place of judgment. [[2:2|the like to it hath not been from the beginning|Similis ei non fuit a principio]]. For no nation can be compared with the angelic army.

paras.t: Ante faciem ejus ignis vorans. Ignis conflagrationis, omnia viva in terra consumpturus seu occisurus, horam judicii et angelorum descensum quoad prædicta opera exercenda præcedet : qui tamen durabit usque ad finem judicii. Ideo subditur : Et post eum exurens flamma. Ignis enim conflagrationis, durante judicio, incendet perversos; consummato autem judicio, et electis ad cœlum euntibus, ignis iste involvet damnatos, atque cum eis ingredietur infernum. Unde habetur in Psalmo : Ignis ante ipsum præcedet, et inflammabit in circuitu inimicos ejus.
paras.en: [[2:3|Before the face thereof a devouring fire|Ante faciem ejus ignis vorans]]. The fire of the conflagration [that is, the fire that will burn up the world at the end], which is to consume or kill all living things on earth, will go before the hour of judgment and the descent of the angels to carry out the works just spoken of; yet it will last until the end of the judgment. Therefore it is added: [[2:3|and behind it a burning flame|Et post eum exurens flamma]]. For the fire of the conflagration will burn the wicked while the judgment lasts; and when the judgment is finished, and the elect are going to heaven, that fire will wrap round the damned and enter hell with them. Hence we have in the Psalm: [[Ps 96:3|A fire shall go before him, and shall burn his enemies round about|Ignis ante ipsum præcedet, et inflammabit in circuitu inimicos ejus]].

paras.t: Quasi hortus voluptatis terra coram eo. Veniente angelica turba ad vastandam terram, erit ipsa terra adhuc divitiis plena, antequam scilicet ignis conflagrationis eruperit. Erunt quoque tunc multi justi, Antichristo occiso, qui propter spirituales divitias atque delicias, horto voluptatis seu paradiso comparantur. Et post eum solitudo deserti : quia peracto judicio, nullus remanebit habitator in terra ; neque est qui effugiat eum, id est, nullus impiorum manum angelorum evadet ; sed ut ait Salvator, In consummatione sæculi exibunt angeli, et separabunt malos de medio justorum, et mittent eos in caminum ignis: et denuo, Mittet Filius hominis angelos suos, et colligent de regno ejus omnia scandala.
paras.en: [[2:3|the land is like a garden of pleasure before it|Quasi hortus voluptatis terra coram eo]]. When the angelic host comes to lay waste the earth, the earth itself will still be full of riches, that is, before the fire of the conflagration has broken out. There will also be many just men at that time, after Antichrist has been slain, who for their spiritual riches and delights are compared to a garden of pleasure, or paradise[[Gen 2:8||]]. [[2:3|and behind it a desolate wilderness|Et post eum solitudo deserti]]: because when the judgment is over no inhabitant will remain on the earth; [[2:3|neither is there any one that can escape it|neque est qui effugiat eum]], that is, none of the wicked will escape the hand of the angels; but, as the Saviour says, [[Matt 13:49|at the end of the world. The angels shall go out, and shall separate the wicked from among the just|In consummatione sæculi exibunt angeli, et separabunt malos de medio justorum]], [[Matt 13:50|And shall cast them into the furnace of fire|et mittent eos in caminum ignis]]; and again, [[Matt 13:41|The Son of man shall send his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all scandals|Mittet Filius hominis angelos suos, et colligent de regno ejus omnia scandala]].

paras.t: Angelorum quoque adspectus et occursus, terribilis erit damnandis. Propterea subditur : Quasi adspectus equorum, adspectus eorum, etc. Velut populus fortis præparatus ad prælium. De quo in Apocalypsi : Factum est prælium in cœlo ; Michael et angeli ejus præliabantur cum dracone. A facie ejus, id est hujus angelici exercitus, cruciabuntur populi. Qui enim modo non acquiescunt inspirationibus angelorum custodum suorum, habebunt eos in die judicii contra se in testimonium justæ damnationis et ingratitudinis suæ. Horribile quoque tunc erit corporalibus cernere oculis acies angelorum, quia tunc visibiliter apparebunt.
paras.en: The sight and the onset of the angels, too, will be terrible to those who are to be damned. Therefore it is added: [[2:4|The appearance of them is as the appearance of horses|Quasi adspectus equorum, adspectus eorum]], etc. [[2:5|as a strong people prepared to battle|Velut populus fortis præparatus ad prælium]]. Of which it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 12:7|there was a great battle in heaven: Michael and his angels fought with the dragon|Factum est prælium in cœlo ; Michael et angeli ejus præliabantur cum dracone]]. [[2:6|At their presence|A facie ejus]], that is, of this angelic army, [[2:6|the people shall be in grievous pains|cruciabuntur populi]]. For those who do not now consent to the inspirations of their guardian angels will have them against themselves on the day of judgment, as witness to their just damnation and their ingratitude. It will also be dreadful then to see with bodily eyes the ranks of the angels, for then they will appear visibly.

paras.t: Viri in viis suis gradientur, id est, angeli qui tunc in forma virorum apparebunt (ut dicitur in Actibus, quod duo viri steterunt juxta illos), ordinate procedent ad prosequendum quod Deus injunxerit eis; et non declinabunt a semitis suis, quia nec magis, nec minus acturi sunt, quam increata Dei sapientia ipsis præfixerit. Nunquam enim constitutos sibi a lege divina terminos transgredientur secundum divinum et magnum Dionysium.
paras.en: [[2:7|the men shall march every one on his way|Viri in viis suis gradientur]], that is, the angels, who will then appear in the form of men (as it is said in the Acts that [[Acts 1:10|two men stood by them|duo viri steterunt juxta illos]]), will go forward in order to carry out what God has enjoined on them; [[2:7|and they shall not turn aside from their ranks|et non declinabunt a semitis suis]] [*semitis*, paths], because they will do neither more nor less than the uncreated Wisdom of God has appointed for them. For, according to the divine and great Dionysius, they never pass beyond the bounds set for them by the divine law.

paras.t: Sed et per fenestras cadent. Fenestræ, hominis sunt sensus, per quos spiritus boni et mali ad animam introire dicuntur, secundum quod homo sensus bene aut male custodit. Unde Jeremias : Mors, inquit, intravit per fenestras vestras.
paras.en: [[2:8|yea, and they shall fall through the windows|Sed et per fenestras cadent]]. The windows are the senses of man, through which good and evil spirits are said to enter the soul, according as a man guards his senses well or ill. Hence Jeremias: [[Jer 9:21|death|Mors]], he says, [[Jer 9:21|is come up through our windows|intravit per fenestras vestras]] [Denis has *intravit per fenestras vestras*, has entered through your windows].

paras.t: Urbem, id est Ecclesiam, ingredientur : de qua dicitur in Psalmo, Gloriosa dicta sunt de te, civitas Dei; et in Apocalypsi, Vidi civitatem sanctam Jerusalem. In muro current, id est, ubique bonos a malis segregabunt.
paras.en: [[2:9|the city|Urbem]], that is, the Church, [[2:9|They shall enter into|ingredientur]]: of which it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 86:3|Glorious things are said of thee, O city of God|Gloriosa dicta sunt de te, civitas Dei]]; and in the Apocalypse: I [[Apoc 21:2|saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem|Vidi civitatem sanctam Jerusalem]]. [[2:9|they shall run upon the wall|In muro current]], that is, everywhere they will separate the good from the wicked.

paras.t: A facie ejus contremuit terra, moti sunt cœli, sol et luna obtenebrati sunt, etc., id est, a terrore divini judicii, et propter ea quæ fient in die novissimo, immutanda sunt omnia ista, secundum quod Christus ait in Evangelio : Erunt signa in sole et luna et stellis, arescentibus hominibus præ timore : nam et virtutes cœlorum movebuntur.
paras.en: [[2:10|At their presence the earth hath trembled, the heavens are moved: the sun and moon are darkened|A facie ejus contremuit terra, moti sunt cœli, sol et luna obtenebrati sunt]], etc., that is, from the terror of the divine judgment, and because of what will happen on the last day, all these things are to be changed, as Christ says in the Gospel: [[Luke 21:25|there shall be signs in the sun and in the moon and in the stars|Erunt signa in sole et luna et stellis]], [[Luke 21:26|Men withering away for fear|arescentibus hominibus præ timore]]: [[Luke 21:26|For the powers of heaven shall be moved|nam et virtutes cœlorum movebuntur]].

paras.t: Et Dominus dedit vocem suam ante faciem exercitus sui : id est, angeli sancti habebunt ex divino imperio efficaciam operandi quæ dicta sunt; quia multa sunt nimis castra ejus, quia fortia et facientia verbum ejus. Castra hæc Dei, sunt sancti angeli, quos constat esse innumerabiles, et ad omne opus Deo placitum robustissimos, divino quoque imperio ad nutum in omnibus obedientes. De quibus in Daniele legitur : Millia millium ministrabant ei, et decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei ; et in Psalmo : Benedicite Domino, angeli ejus, potentes virtute, facientes verbum illius ad audiendam vocem sermonum ejus. Hinc secundum principem theologorum beatissimum Dionysium, omnes angelici spiritus appellantur virtutes, tanquam potentes sine difficultate ad omnem operationem sibi convenientem. Præterea, quod angeli sancti dicantur castra Dei, constat ex eo quod scriptum est in Genesi : Abiit Jacob itinere quod cœperat, fueruntque ei obviam angeli Dei, quos quum vidisset, dixit : Castra Dei sunt hæc. De quibus et apud Job dicitur : Numquid est numerus militum ejus? et super quem non surget lumen illius? Unde et Deus communiter in Prophetis Dominus exercituum, id est cœlestium agminum, nuncupatur.
paras.en: [[2:11|And the Lord hath uttered his voice before the face of his army|Et Dominus dedit vocem suam ante faciem exercitus sui]]: that is, the holy angels will have from the divine command the power to work the things that have been said; [[2:11|for his armies are exceedingly great, for they are strong, and execute his word|quia multa sunt nimis castra ejus, quia fortia et facientia verbum ejus]]. These camps of God [*castra*, camps, armies] are the holy angels, who are known to be numberless, most mighty for every work pleasing to God, and obedient in all things to the divine command at a nod. Of them we read in Daniel: [[Dan 7:10|thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times a hundred thousand stood before him|Millia millium ministrabant ei, et decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 102:20|Bless the Lord, all ye his angels: you that are mighty in strength, and execute his word, hearkening to the voice of his orders|Benedicite Domino, angeli ejus, potentes virtute, facientes verbum illius ad audiendam vocem sermonum ejus]]. Hence, according to the prince of theologians, the most blessed Dionysius, all the angelic spirits are called *virtues* [*virtutes*, that is, powers], as being able without difficulty for every operation befitting them. Moreover, that the holy angels are called the camps of God is clear from what is written in Genesis: [[Gen 32:1|Jacob also went on the journey he had begun: and the angels of God met him|Abiit Jacob itinere quod cœperat, fueruntque ei obviam angeli Dei]]: [[Gen 32:2|And when he saw them, he said: These are the camps of God|quos quum vidisset, dixit : Castra Dei sunt hæc]]. Of them it is said in Job too: [[Job 25:3|Is there any numbering of his soldiers? and upon whom shall not his light arise?|Numquid est numerus militum ejus? et super quem non surget lumen illius?]] Hence also God is commonly called in the Prophets the Lord of hosts, that is, of the heavenly armies.

paras.t: Magnus enim dies Domini, id est dies extremi judicii : qui magnus asseritur, propter magna divinæ justitiæ opera quæ fient in ea ; et terribilis valde injustis. Justis tamen optabilis est suavisque erit, Christo dicente : His fieri incipientibus, levate capita vestra (id est, animas lætificate), quia appropinquat redemptio vestra. Et quis injustorum sustinebit eum? id est, quis poterit injustorum tolerare calamitatem atque horrenda hujus diei supplicia? Et tamen ea tolerare erit necesse. Hinc Petrus ait : Si justus vix salvabitur, impius et peccator ubi parebunt? In secunda quoque Canonica sua loquitur Petrus : Adveniet dies Domini tanquam fur : in quo cœli magno impetu transient, elementa vero calore solventur; terra autem, et quæ in ipsa sunt opera, exurentur. Quum ergo hæc omnia dissolvenda sint, quales oportet nos esse in sanctis conversationibus et pietatibus, exspectantes et properantes in adventum diei Domini nostri Jesu Christi, in quo cœli ardentes solventur, et elementa ignis calore tabescent? Constat ergo, quam terribilis intolerabilisque dies ista consistet. Veniet enim tempus, quale non fuit ab eo, ex quo gentes esse cœperunt usque ad tempus illud, ut legitur in Daniele.
paras.en: [[2:11|for the day of the Lord is great|Magnus enim dies Domini]], that is, the day of the last judgment, which is called great because of the great works of divine justice that will be done in it; [[2:11|and very terrible|et terribilis valde]] to the unjust. Yet to the just it is to be desired, and will be sweet, as Christ says: [[Luke 21:28|when these things begin to come to pass|His fieri incipientibus]], [[Luke 21:28|lift up your heads|levate capita vestra]] (that is, gladden your souls), [[Luke 21:28|because your redemption is at hand|quia appropinquat redemptio vestra]]. [[2:11|and who|Et quis]] of the unjust [[2:11|can stand it|sustinebit eum]]? that is, who will be able to bear the calamity of the unjust and the dreadful torments of this day? And yet it will be necessary to bear them. Hence Peter says: [[1 Pet 4:18|if the just man shall scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?|Si justus vix salvabitur, impius et peccator ubi parebunt?]] In his second Canonical epistle also Peter says: [[2 Pet 3:10|the day of the Lord shall come as a thief, in which the heavens shall pass away with great violence and the elements shall be melted with heat and the earth and the works which are in it shall be burnt up|Adveniet dies Domini tanquam fur : in quo cœli magno impetu transient, elementa vero calore solventur; terra autem, et quæ in ipsa sunt opera, exurentur]]. [[2 Pet 3:11|Seeing then that all these things are to be dissolved, what manner of people ought you to be in holy conversation and godliness?|Quum ergo hæc omnia dissolvenda sint, quales oportet nos esse in sanctis conversationibus et pietatibus]] [[2 Pet 3:12|Looking for and hasting unto the coming of the day of the Lord, by which the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with the burning heat?|exspectantes et properantes in adventum diei Domini nostri Jesu Christi, in quo cœli ardentes solventur, et elementa ignis calore tabescent?]] [Denis has *nos*, we, for *you*.] It is clear, then, how terrible and unbearable that day will be. For [[Dan 12:1|a time shall come, such as never was from the time that nations began, even until that time|Veniet enim tempus, quale non fuit ab eo, ex quo gentes esse cœperunt usque ad tempus illud]], as we read in Daniel.

paras.t: Nunc ergo dicit Dominus : Convertimini ad me in toto corde vestro, in jejunio et fletu, etc. Sic et nos converti debemus ad Dominum totis præcordiis, universisque cordis nostri medullis, ut tota nostra affectio sit fixa in Deo, eique cuncta interiora nostra forti unione adhæreant : quia pro quanta parte affectio nostra in rebus creatis dispergitur, pro tanto minor est ad Deum cordis conversio. Debemus autem converti in jejunio, quo vitia comprimuntur, mens elevatur, virtutes et præmia acquiruntur, præterita delicta dimittuntur, futura tormenta redimuntur. Pessimum genus quoque dæmoniorum, non nisi in oratione atque jejunio ejicitur, ut ait Salvator. Porro, quod per salutare jejunium oratio exaudiatur, et sapientia vera cordi infundatur, innotescit ex eo quod Gabriel locutus est Danieli : Ex die primo quo posuisti cor tuum ad intelligendum, ut affligeres te in conspectu Domini Dei tui, exaudita sunt verba tua, et ego veni ut docerem te.
paras.en: [[2:12|Now, therefore, saith the Lord. Be converted to me with all your heart, in fasting, and in weeping|Nunc ergo dicit Dominus : Convertimini ad me in toto corde vestro, in jejunio et fletu]], etc. So we too ought to be turned to the Lord with our whole breast and all the marrow of our heart, so that our whole affection may be fixed on God and all our inward parts may cleave to him with a strong union: for by as much as our affection is scattered among created things, by so much the less is the heart's turning to God. And we ought to be turned in fasting, by which vices are kept down, the mind is raised up, virtues and rewards are gained, past sins are forgiven, and future torments are redeemed. The worst kind of demons, too, [[Matt 17:20|is not cast out but by prayer and fasting|non nisi in oratione atque jejunio ejicitur]], as the Saviour says. Further, that through wholesome fasting prayer is heard and true wisdom is poured into the heart, is made known from what Gabriel said to Daniel: [[Dan 10:12|from the first day that thou didst set thy heart to understand, to afflict thyself in the sight of thy God, thy words have been heard|Ex die primo quo posuisti cor tuum ad intelligendum, ut affligeres te in conspectu Domini Dei tui, exaudita sunt verba tua]], and [[Dan 10:14|I am come to teach thee|ego veni ut docerem te]] [these last words are from Dan 10:14; v. 12 ends *and I am come for thy words*].

paras.t: Debemus insuper converti in fletu ex desiderio patriæ, ex displicentia propriæ culpæ, ex Christi compassione, ex totius mundi multiplici transgressione atque errore. Scindere etiam corda, non vestimenta : in quo multorum stultissima vanitas increpatur, fractilantium indumenta, quod prorsus ad nihil est utile, nisi ad stultorum damnationem.
paras.en: We ought, moreover, to be turned in weeping: from longing for our heavenly country, from displeasure at our own fault, from compassion with Christ, and for the manifold transgression and error of the whole world. Also: [[2:13|rend your hearts, and not your garments|Scindere etiam corda, non vestimenta]]; in which is rebuked the most foolish vanity of many who slash their garments [*fractilantium indumenta*: who cut their clothes into fringes and slashes, a fashion of Denis's day], which is of no use at all except to the damnation of fools.

paras.t: Sacrificium laudis ac obedientiæ, vel oblatio dominici corporis, et libamen pii fletus, seu oblatio sanguinis Christi, offerantur Domino Deo nostro.
paras.en: Let [[2:14|sacrifice|Sacrificium]] of praise and obedience, or the offering of the Lord's body, [[2:14|and libation|et libamen]] of loving tears, or the offering of Christ's blood, be offered [[2:14|to the Lord|Domino]] our God.

paras.t: Canite tuba evangelicæ prædicationis in Sion, id est in Ecclesia, corripiendo inquietos, consolando pusillanimes, docendoque singulos secundum quod capere possunt, et expedit. Vocate cœtum, congregate populum, etc., id est, omne genus Christianorum, juvenes ac virgines, senes et juniores, colligite spiritualiter in fide et caritate, ut multitudinis credentium sit cor unum et anima una, et id ipsum dicant omnes, nec habeant schismata. Istud quoque fit corporaliter, quando ad festa et processiones jubentur concurrere omnes.
paras.en: [[2:15|Blow the trumpet|Canite tuba]] of the gospel preaching [[2:15|in Sion|in Sion]], that is, in the Church, by rebuking the unquiet, comforting the faint-hearted, and teaching each one according to what he can take in and what is expedient. [[2:15|call a solemn assembly|Vocate cœtum]], [[2:16|Gather together the people|congregate populum]], etc., that is, gather spiritually in faith and charity every kind of Christian, young men and maidens, old and young, so that [[Acts 4:32|the multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul|multitudinis credentium sit cor unum et anima una]], and all may speak the same thing and have no schisms. This is also done bodily, when all are bidden to come together for feasts and processions.

paras.t: Congregate parvulos, et sugentes ubera Ecclesiæ (de quibus in Canticis, Meliora sunt ubera tua vino), id est, innocentes, pios, ac humiles coadunate sub alis vestræ protectionis, o veri pastores ac doctores, ne fallantur aut opprimantur. De talibus loquitur Petrus : Quasi modo geniti infantes, lac concupiscite; et Christus, Abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis. Egrediatur sponsus de cubili suo, et sponsa de thalamo suo, quatenus juxta Apostolum, ex consensu ad tempus abstineant, ut vacent orationi, et qui habent uxores, sint tanquam non habentes, ne fiant sicut equus et mulus, quibus non est intellectus.
paras.en: [[2:16|gather together the little ones, and them that suck at the breasts|Congregate parvulos, et sugentes ubera]] of the Church (of which it is said in the Canticle: [[Cant 1:1|thy breasts are better than wine|Meliora sunt ubera tua vino]]), that is, gather the innocent, the devout and the humble under the wings of your protection, O true shepherds and teachers, lest they be deceived or oppressed. Of such Peter speaks: [[1 Pet 2:2|As newborn babes|Quasi modo geniti infantes]], [[1 Pet 2:2|desire the rational milk|lac concupiscite]] [Denis leaves out *rationabile, sine dolo*]; and Christ: [[Matt 11:25|thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to little ones|Abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis]]. [[2:16|let the bridegroom go forth from his bed, and the bride out of her bridal chamber|Egrediatur sponsus de cubili suo, et sponsa de thalamo suo]], so that, according to the Apostle, they may abstain [[1 Cor 7:5|by consent, for a time|ex consensu ad tempus]], [[1 Cor 7:5|that you may give yourselves to prayer|ut vacent orationi]], and [[1 Cor 7:29|they also who have wives be as if they had none|qui habent uxores, sint tanquam non habentes]], lest they [[Ps 31:9|become like the horse and the mule, who have no understanding|fiant sicut equus et mulus, quibus non est intellectus]].

paras.t: Inter vestibulum et altare plorabunt sacerdotes, etc. Sic in locis materialis ecclesiæ, et in conventu fidelium, flere debent sacerdotes Christi pro suis populique delictis, et pro persecutionum ac tentationum salubri cessatione, quatenus quietam et tranquillam vitam agamus in omni pietate et castitate. Et ne des hereditatem tuam in opprobrium, ut dominentur eis nationes. Hoc merito omnes instanter peteremus, præsertim quum jam videamus nostram et Christi hereditatem, Terram sanctam (et plurimos Christianos) in manus traditam Sarracenorum ac hostium Dei. Christi nempe hereditas, plebs est fidelis, de qua ait in Psalmo : Hereditas mea præclara est mihi.
paras.en: [[2:17|Between the porch and the altar the priests, the Lord's ministers, shall weep|Inter vestibulum et altare plorabunt sacerdotes]], etc. So in the places of the material church, and in the assembly of the faithful, the priests of Christ ought to weep for their own sins and the people's, and for a wholesome end to persecutions and temptations, [[1 Tim 2:2|that we may lead a quiet and a peaceable life in all piety and chastity|quietam et tranquillam vitam agamus in omni pietate et castitate]]. [[2:17|and give not thy inheritance to reproach, that the heathens should rule over them|Et ne des hereditatem tuam in opprobrium, ut dominentur eis nationes]]. This we should all rightly beg with insistence, especially since we now see our inheritance and Christ's, the Holy Land (and very many Christians), given into the hands of the Saracens and the enemies of God. For Christ's inheritance is the faithful people, of which he says in the Psalm: [[Ps 15:6|my inheritance is goodly to me|Hereditas mea præclara est mihi]].

paras.t: Zelatus est zelo magni […] ecclesiæ degentem in terris, de Jesu Christo accipitur illud in Psalmo : Benedixisti, Domine, terram tuam. Unde dicit Apostolus : In fide vivo Filii Dei, qui dilexit me, et tradidit semetipsum pro me. De quo in Apocalypsi asseritur : Qui dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo. Ipse enim est pastor bonus, qui posuit animam suam pro ovibus suis. Et pepercit populo suo christiano pœnitenti.
paras.en: [[2:18|hath been zealous|Zelatus est]] with the zeal of great […] of the Church dwelling on earth; of Jesus Christ is understood that word in the Psalm: [[Ps 84:2|Lord, thou hast blessed thy land|Benedixisti, Domine, terram tuam]]. Hence the Apostle says: [[Gal 2:20|I live in the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and delivered himself for me|In fide vivo Filii Dei, qui dilexit me, et tradidit semetipsum pro me]]. Of him it is declared in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 1:5|who hath loved us and washed us from our sins in his own blood|Qui dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo]]. For he is [[John 10:14|the good shepherd|pastor bonus]], who laid down his life for his sheep[[John 10:15||]]. [[2:18|and hath spared his people|Et pepercit populo suo]], the Christian people, when it repents.

paras.t: Et dixit populo suo : Ecce ego mittam vobis frumentum, et vinum, et oleum, id est corpus et sanguinem Christi, quæ sub speciebus panis et vini conficiuntur. Per oleum quoque signatur spiritualis unctio Spiritus Sancti. Vel, per frumentum intelligitur operatio virtuosa, nutriens mentem; per vinum autem, gratia contemplationis, quæ operationem efficit saporosam. Et non dabo vos ultra opprobrium in gentibus. Quum Christus dat suis fidelibus gratiam tam honestæ et irreprehensibilis conversationis, quod benefaciendo obmutescere faciunt imprudentium hominum ignorantiam, tunc non dat eos opprobrium in gentibus. Ad quam perfectionem admonet Petrus, dicens in prima sua canonica epistola : Conversationem vestram inter gentes habentes bonam, ut in eo quod detrectant de vobis tanquam malefactoribus, ex bonis operibus vos considerantes, glorificent Deum. Hoc est vincere in bono malum. Unde et Moyses ait in Deuteronomio : Hæc est vestra sapientia et intellectus coram hominibus, ut audientes universi præcepta hæc, dicant : En populus sapiens et intelligens. Sic honorificantes se honorificat Deus.
paras.en: [[2:19|and said to his people: Behold I will send you corn, and wine, and oil|Et dixit populo suo : Ecce ego mittam vobis frumentum, et vinum, et oleum]], that is, the body and blood of Christ, which are consecrated under the species of bread and wine. By the oil, too, is signified the spiritual anointing of the Holy Ghost. Or, by the corn is understood virtuous action, which nourishes the mind; and by the wine, the grace of contemplation, which makes action savoury. [[2:19|and I will no more make you a reproach among the nations|Et non dabo vos ultra opprobrium in gentibus]]. When Christ gives his faithful the grace of a life so honourable and blameless that by doing well they [[1 Pet 2:15|put to silence the ignorance of foolish men|obmutescere faciunt imprudentium hominum ignorantiam]], then he does not make them a reproach among the nations. To this perfection Peter exhorts, saying in his first canonical epistle: [[1 Pet 2:12|Having your conversation good among the Gentiles: that whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may, by the good works which they shall behold in you, glorify God|Conversationem vestram inter gentes habentes bonam, ut in eo quod detrectant de vobis tanquam malefactoribus, ex bonis operibus vos considerantes, glorificent Deum]]. This is to [[Rom 12:21|overcome evil by good|vincere in bono malum]]. Hence Moses too says in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 4:6|this is your wisdom, and understanding in the sight of nations, that hearing all these precepts, they may say: Behold a wise and understanding people|Hæc est vestra sapientia et intellectus coram hominibus, ut audientes universi præcepta hæc, dicant : En populus sapiens et intelligens]]. So does God honour those who honour him[[1 Kings 2:30||]].

paras.t: Et eum qui ab aquilone est, id est diabolus, qui dixit, Sedebo in monte testamenti, in lateribus aquilonis : habitat enim in cordibus in quibus refriguit caritas, quæ per aquilonem, locum et ventum frigidum, designantur; procul faciam a vobis, faciendo cum tentatione proventum. Hinc dicitur ad Romanos : Deus conteret […] Christus in Joanne, Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras. Propter quod Jacobus jubet : Resistite diabolo, et fugiet a vobis. Et expellam eum in terram inviam et desertam, ut ambulet per loca arida et inaquosa, quærens requiem, nec inveniens; vel in infernum, quæ est terra tenebrosa et operta mortis caligine; vel in corda reproborum, in quibus non est via virtutum, sed a gratia sunt deserta. Et ascendet fœtor ejus, id est, suggestiones ejus pestiferæ ascendent atque inficient animas plurimorum; et ascendet putredo ejus, id est opera corruptionis putrida ac mortua, qualia sunt fœtidissima opera carnis, quæ dæmone suggerente exsurgunt in multis, qui contumeliis afficiunt corpora sua in semetipsis.
paras.en: [[2:20|the northern enemy|Et eum qui ab aquilone est]] [literally, *him that is from the north*], that is, the devil, who said: [[Is 14:13|I will sit in the mountain of the covenant, in the sides of the north|Sedebo in monte testamenti, in lateribus aquilonis]]; for he dwells in the hearts in which charity has grown cold[[Matt 24:12||]], which are signified by the north, a cold place and a cold wind; [[2:20|I will remove far off from you|procul faciam a vobis]], for he [[1 Cor 10:13|will make also with temptation issue|faciendo cum tentatione proventum]]. Hence it is said to the Romans: God shall crush[[Rom 16:20||]] […] [the text breaks off here; Romans has *the God of peace crush Satan under your feet speedily*] Christ in John: [[John 12:31|now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]]. For this reason James bids: [[Jas 4:7|resist the devil: and he will fly from you|Resistite diabolo, et fugiet a vobis]]. [[2:20|and I will drive him into a land unpassable, and desert|Et expellam eum in terram inviam et desertam]], so that he may walk through dry and waterless places, [[Luke 11:24|seeking rest: and not finding|quærens requiem, nec inveniens]]; or into hell, which is [[Job 10:21|a land that is dark and covered with the mist of death|terra tenebrosa et operta mortis caligine]]; or into the hearts of the reprobate, in which there is no way of virtue, but which are deserted by grace. [[2:20|and his stench shall ascend|Et ascendet fœtor ejus]], that is, his pestilent suggestions will rise up and infect the souls of very many; [[2:20|and his rottenness shall go up|et ascendet putredo ejus]], that is, works of corruption, rotten and dead, such as the most foul works of the flesh, which at the devil's suggestion spring up in many, who [[Rom 1:24|dishonour their own bodies among themselves|contumeliis afficiunt corpora sua in semetipsis]].

paras.t: Noli timere, terra, id est, Ecclesia; exsulta et lætare, quoniam magnificavit Dominus ut faceret tecum gratiam maximam, ita ut dicere possis : Benedictus Dominus, quoniam mirificavit misericordiam suam mihi. Propter quod dicit Apostolus : Gaudete in Domino semper; iterum dico, Gaudete : Dominus prope est.
paras.en: [[2:21|Fear not, O land|Noli timere, terra]], that is, O Church; [[2:21|be glad, and rejoice: for the Lord hath done great things|exsulta et lætare, quoniam magnificavit Dominus ut faceret]], working with thee the greatest grace, so that thou mayest say: [[Ps 30:22|Blessed be the Lord, for he hath shewn his wonderful mercy to me|Benedictus Dominus, quoniam mirificavit misericordiam suam mihi]]. For this reason the Apostle says: [[Phil 4:4|Rejoice in the Lord always: again, I say, rejoice|Gaudete in Domino semper; iterum dico, Gaudete]]: [[Phil 4:5|The Lord is nigh|Dominus prope est]].

paras.t: Nolite timere, animalia regionis, id est, homines jugum divinorum præceptorum super vos tanquam pia jumenta portantes; quia germinaverunt, id est, in bonis operibus fructuosa fuerunt, speciosa deserti, id est corda gentilium seu impiorum conversorum ad Deum. Unde in Isaia habetur : Lætabitur deserta et invia, et exsultabit solitudo. Quia lignum attulit fructum suum, id est Christus, qui est lignum vitæ : quia et Salomon ait de sapientia, quod sit lignum vitæ omnibus apprehendentibus eam. De se ipso quoque dicit Salvator : Si in viridi ligno hæc faciunt, in arido quid fiet? Tunc enim Christus attulit fructum suum, quando redemit genus humanum, multosque filios adduxit in gloriam, et peccatores per gratiam justificavit, quemadmodum Isaias prænuntiavit : In die illa erit germen Domini in gloria et magnificentia, et fructus terræ sublimis. Potest quoque exponi de ligno crucis, per quod salvatus est mundus. Ficus et vinea, id est ecclesiasticæ personæ, Spiritus Sancti dulcedine atque operibus adornatæ (ita ut ficus et vinea appellentur propter dulcedinis fecunditatisque gratiam), dederunt virtutem suam, id est, opera virtuosa produxerunt, et alios converterunt.
paras.en: [[2:22|Fear not, ye beasts of the fields|Nolite timere, animalia regionis]], that is, you men who carry the yoke of the divine commandments upon you[[Matt 11:29||]] like gentle beasts of burden; because there [[2:22|are sprung|germinaverunt]], that is, have been fruitful in good works, [[2:22|the beautiful places of the wilderness|speciosa deserti]], that is, the hearts of the Gentiles or of the ungodly converted to God. Hence we have in Isaias: [[Is 35:1|The land that was desolate and impassable shall be glad, and the wilderness shall rejoice|Lætabitur deserta et invia, et exsultabit solitudo]]. [[2:22|for the tree hath brought forth its fruit|Quia lignum attulit fructum suum]], that is, Christ, who is the tree of life: for Solomon too says of wisdom that she is [[Prov 3:18|a tree of life to them that lay hold on her|lignum vitæ omnibus apprehendentibus eam]]. Of himself also the Saviour says: [[Luke 23:31|if in the green wood they do these things, what shall be done in the dry?|Si in viridi ligno hæc faciunt, in arido quid fiet?]] For Christ brought forth his fruit when he redeemed mankind, [[Heb 2:10|brought many children into glory|multosque filios adduxit in gloriam]], and justified sinners by grace, as Isaias foretold: [[Is 4:2|In that day the bud of the Lord shall be in magnificence and glory, and the fruit of the earth shall be high|In die illa erit germen Domini in gloria et magnificentia, et fructus terræ sublimis]]. It can also be expounded of the wood of the cross [*lignum* means both tree and wood], by which the world was saved. [[2:22|the fig tree, and the vine|Ficus et vinea]], that is, persons of the Church adorned with the sweetness and the works of the Holy Ghost (so that they are called fig tree and vine because of the grace of sweetness and fruitfulness), [[2:22|have yielded their strength|dederunt virtutem suam]] [*virtutem*, strength or virtue], that is, have brought forth virtuous works and converted others.

paras.t: Et filiæ Sion, id est, animæ speculativæ, seu filii Ecclesiæ, exsultate in Domino Deo vestro, id est Patre æterno, ei gratias referendo; quia dedit vobis doctorem justitiæ, utpote Christum, qui ait : Vos vocatis me, Magister et Domine; et iterum, Unus est magister vester Christus. Vel, per doctorem justitiæ, potest intelligi quilibet bonus ac sapiens prælatus, prædicator seu doctor, qui verbo ac opere docet justitiam : quod est magnum beneficium Dei. Qualis enim rector civitatis, tales et habitantes in ea. Vel potest intelligi Spiritus Sanctus, de quo dixit Christus : Docebit vos omnem veritatem. Et descendere faciet ad vos imbrem matutinum, id est gratiam prævenientem seu fidei doctrinam, et boni propositi inspirationem, et serotinum, id est gratiam subsequentem, vel gloriam consummatam, aut sapientiam contemplativorum, quam Paulus loquitur inter perfectos, quæ est solidus cibus et ultimata quædam perfectio; sicut in principio, id est in primitiva Ecclesia, feci.
paras.en: [[2:23|And you, O children of Sion|Et filiæ Sion]] [Denis reads *filiæ*, daughters, for *filii*, children], that is, contemplative souls, or sons of the Church, [[2:23|rejoice|exsultate]] [[2:23|in the Lord your God|in Domino Deo vestro]], that is, in the eternal Father, giving thanks to him; [[2:23|because he hath given you a teacher of justice|quia dedit vobis doctorem justitiæ]], namely Christ, who says: [[John 13:13|You call me Master and Lord|Vos vocatis me, Magister et Domine]]; and again: [[Matt 23:10|one is your master, Christ|Unus est magister vester Christus]][[Matt 23:8||]]. Or by the teacher of justice may be understood any good and wise prelate, preacher or doctor who teaches justice by word and deed, which is a great gift of God. For [[Ecclus 10:2|what manner of man the ruler of a city is, such also are they that dwell therein|Qualis enim rector civitatis, tales et habitantes in ea]]. Or the Holy Ghost may be understood, of whom Christ said: [[John 16:13|he will teach you all truth|Docebit vos omnem veritatem]]. [[2:23|and he will make the early|Et descendere faciet ad vos imbrem matutinum]] rain to come down to you, that is, prevenient grace [that is, grace that goes before the good act of the will; *subsequent* grace follows and helps it], or the teaching of the faith and the inspiration of a good purpose, [[2:23|and the latter rain|et serotinum]], that is, subsequent grace, or glory made perfect, or the wisdom of the contemplatives, which Paul speaks [[1 Cor 2:6|among the perfect|inter perfectos]], which is solid food and a certain final perfection; [[2:23|as in the beginning|sicut in principio]], that is, as I did in the primitive Church.

paras.t: Et implebuntur areæ, id est Ecclesiæ particulares, congregationes devotæ, seu corda fidelium, frumento, id est spirituali alimento; et redundabunt torcularia, id est præfati fideles tribulationibus pressi, vino internæ refectionis, et oleo piissimæ consolationis. De quibus legitur in Proverbiis : Venite, comedite panem meum, et bibite vinum quod miscui vobis. Qui enim in tribulationibus patiens est, consolari meretur, dicente Apostolo : Sicut pro Christo abundant tribulationes nostræ, ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra.
paras.en: [[2:24|And the floors shall be filled|Et implebuntur areæ]], that is, particular churches, devout communities, or the hearts of the faithful, [[2:24|with wheat|frumento]], that is, with spiritual food; [[2:24|and the presses shall overflow|et redundabunt torcularia]], that is, the faithful just spoken of, pressed by tribulations, [[2:24|with wine|vino]] of inward refreshment, [[2:24|and oil|et oleo]] of most loving consolation. Of these we read in Proverbs: [[Prov 9:5|Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine which I have mingled for you|Venite, comedite panem meum, et bibite vinum quod miscui vobis]]. For he who is patient in tribulations deserves to be consoled, as the Apostle says: As our tribulations abound for Christ, [[2 Cor 1:5|so also by Christ doth our comfort abound|ita et per Christum abundat consolatio nostra]] [Paul has *as the sufferings of Christ abound in us*].

paras.t: Et reddam vobis annos quos comedit locusta, bruchus, eruca, etc., id est, tantam spiritualium divitiarum seu gratiarum copiam tribuam vobis, quantam habuistis antequam per invisibilium seu visibilium hostium tentamenta, dona gratiarum amisistis, ita quod posteriora vestra erunt meliora prioribus.
paras.en: [[2:25|And I will restore to you the years which the locust, and the bruchus, and the mildew, and the palmerworm hath eaten|Et reddam vobis annos quos comedit locusta, bruchus, eruca]], etc., that is, I will give you as great an abundance of spiritual riches or graces as you had before you lost the gifts of grace through the temptations of invisible or visible enemies, so that your latter state will be better than your former.

paras.t: Et in his bonis spiritualiter epulabimini, et laudabitis nomen Domini Dei vestri, qui fecit vobiscum mirabilia, id est admirabilem morum conversionem, et subitam cordis ad Deum conversionem, supernaturalem Sancti Spiritus illustrationem, propriæ voluntatis omnimodam abnegationem, mundi contemptum, ita ut subito de superbis efficeremini humiles, de iracundis mites, de gulosis et luxuriosis casti ac sobrii, de mundanis ac vanis timorati atque claustrales. Hæc sunt quotidiana mirabilia Dei, soli Deo possibilia, tanto mirabiliora quanto spiritualiora. Unde et Petrus in prima sua Canonica : Virtutes, inquit, annuntietis ejus qui de tenebris vos vocavit in admirabile lumen suum. Facit quoque Deus nobiscum quotidie mirabilia in Sacramento altaris, ceterisque specialibus beneficiis, consolationibus et visitationibus cordis. Et non confundetur populus meus christianus, id est, effectu spei suæ non privabitur, in æternum. Sed qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum; qui autem me erubuerit et meos sermones, erubescam et ego eum, et confundetur in sempiternum.
paras.en: And on these good things you will feast spiritually [Denis's gloss on *you shall eat in plenty*], [[2:26|and you shall praise the name of the Lord your God; who hath done wonders with you|et laudabitis nomen Domini Dei vestri, qui fecit vobiscum mirabilia]], that is, the wonderful conversion of your ways, the sudden turning of the heart to God, the supernatural enlightenment of the Holy Ghost, the complete denial of your own will, contempt of the world; so that suddenly from proud you were made humble, from wrathful meek, from gluttons and lechers chaste and sober, from worldly and vain men God-fearing men of the cloister. These are the daily wonders of God, possible to God alone, the more wonderful the more spiritual they are. Hence Peter too in his first Canonical epistle: That you may [[1 Pet 2:9|declare his virtues|Virtutes]], he says, [[1 Pet 2:9|who hath called you out of darkness into his marvelous light|annuntietis ejus qui de tenebris vos vocavit in admirabile lumen suum]]. God also does wonders with us daily in the Sacrament of the altar, and in his other special benefits, consolations and visitations of the heart. [[2:26|and my people shall not be confounded|Et non confundetur populus meus]], the Christian people, that is, it will not be deprived of the effect of its hope, [[2:26|for ever|in æternum]]. But he [[Matt 10:32|that shall confess me before men, I will also confess him|qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum]]; but [[Luke 9:26|he that shall be ashamed of me and of my words|qui autem me erubuerit et meos sermones]], I also will be ashamed of him, and he shall be confounded for ever.

paras.t: Et scietis quia in medio Israel, id est Ecclesiæ divina fideliter contemplantis, ego sum, habitando per caritatem et gratiam in corde credentium, quemadmodum fassus sum : Ubi fuerint duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, ibi in medio eorum sum. Quamvis enim nemo certe sciat se esse in caritate sine speciali revelatione, quoniam nescit homo an amore dignus sit, an odio, nihilo minus conjecturaliter et probabiliter valde scire hoc potest, dum sentit se prædicto modo conversum, et vitia detestantem, verbumque Dei hilariter audientem, atque ad Dei obsequia pronum.
paras.en: [[2:27|And you shall know|Et scietis]] [[2:27|in the midst of Israel|quia in medio Israel]], that is, of the Church that faithfully contemplates divine things, [[2:27|that I am|ego sum]], dwelling by charity and grace in the hearts of believers, as I have declared: [[Matt 18:20|where there are two or three gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them|Ubi fuerint duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, ibi in medio eorum sum]]. For although no one knows for certain, without a special revelation, that he is in charity, since [[Eccles 9:1|man knoweth not whether he be worthy of love, or hatred|nescit homo an amore dignus sit, an odio]], nevertheless he can know it by conjecture and with great probability [that is, from signs, not with the certainty of faith], when he feels himself converted in the way just described, detesting vices, hearing the word of God gladly, and ready for the service of God.

paras.t: Postremo, circa prædicta dicit Hieronymus : Nunquam tuta est humana fragilitas; et quanto virtutibus crescimus, tanto magis timere debemus, ne de sublimibus corruamus.
paras.en: Lastly, on what has been said, Jerome says: Human frailty is never safe; and the more we grow in virtues, the more we ought to fear lest we fall from the heights.

2.title: Elucidatio capituli tertii: Et erit post hæc: effundam spiritum meum.
2.title_en: Explanation of the third chapter: And it shall come to pass after this, that I will pour out my spirit.
2.note: Denis's third chapter begins at 2:28 (as in the Hebrew). This article's introduction and its commentary on 2:28–32 are shown here; the rest, on chapter 3, is shown under that chapter.

paras.t: PRÆSENS capitulum, teste Hieronymo, est difficillimum, quum laboriosissimum sit sequentia præcedentibus nectere. Porro quod principium hujus capituli ad litteram intelligendum sit pro tempore Christi, quando post resurrectionem dominicam, sancti Apostoli et qui cum eis fuerant congregati, receperunt Spiritum Sanctum in forma seu signo visibili, apostolica auctoritate probatur. Quum enim in die Pentecostes suscepta plenitudine Spiritus Sancti, beati Apostoli mane hora tertia templum ingressi cœpissent omnium gentium linguis loqui, et mysteria Christi invictissime sermocinari, admirantes Judæi dixerunt : Quidnam vult hoc esse? Aliqui vero irridentes dicebant, quia musto pleni sunt isti. Quo audito, stans Petrus cum undecim, dixit : Viri Judæi, hoc vobis notum sit. Non enim, ut vos æstimatis, hi ebrii sunt, sed hoc est quod dictum est per prophetam Joel : Et erit in novissimis diebus, dicit Dominus : Effundam de Spiritu meo super omnem carnem. Sed huic sensui difficultatem facit, quod statim post verba a principe Apostolorum allegata, sanctus Joel subjunxit : Quia ecce in diebus illis, et in tempore illo, quum convertero captivitatem Juda et Jerusalem, congregabo omnes gentes, et deducam eas in vallem Josaphat, et disceptabo cum eis ibi, etc. Quod communiter explanatur ad litteram pro tempore secundi adventus Christi, seu pro die judicii : ex quo videtur, ad idem tempus referendum principium hujus capituli. Multaque alia in hoc subsequuntur capitulo, quæ maximam involutionem efficiunt. Propter quod expositores satis diversimode exponunt hunc textum.
paras.en: THE present chapter [in Denis's division the third chapter of Joel begins here, at what is now 2:28, as it does in the Hebrew], as Jerome testifies, is most difficult, since it is a very laborious thing to link what follows with what goes before. Now, that the beginning of this chapter is to be understood literally of the time of Christ, when after the Lord's resurrection the holy Apostles, and those who had been gathered together with them, received the Holy Ghost in a visible form or sign, is proved by apostolic authority. For when, on the day of Pentecost[[Acts 2:1||]], the blessed Apostles, having received the fulness of the Holy Ghost, had gone into the temple in the morning at the third hour and begun to speak in the tongues of all nations, and to discourse most invincibly of the mysteries of Christ, the Jews in wonder said: [[Acts 2:12|What meaneth this?|Quidnam vult hoc esse?]] And some, mocking, said: [[Acts 2:13|These men are full of new wine|musto pleni sunt isti]]. On hearing this, [[Acts 2:14|Peter standing up with the eleven|stans Petrus cum undecim]] said: [[Acts 2:14|Ye men of Judea|Viri Judæi]], [[Acts 2:14|be this known to you|hoc vobis notum sit]]. [[Acts 2:15|For these are not drunk, as you suppose|Non enim, ut vos æstimatis, hi ebrii sunt]]. [[Acts 2:16|But this is that which was spoken of by the prophet Joel|sed hoc est quod dictum est per prophetam Joel]]: [[Acts 2:17|And it shall come to pass, in the last days, (saith the Lord), I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh|Et erit in novissimis diebus, dicit Dominus : Effundam de Spiritu meo super omnem carnem]]. But a difficulty is raised against this sense by the fact that, straight after the words cited by the prince of the Apostles, holy Joel added: [[3:1|For behold in those days, and in that time when I shall bring back the captivity of Juda, and Jerusalem|Quia ecce in diebus illis, et in tempore illo, quum convertero captivitatem Juda et Jerusalem]], [[3:2|I will gather together all nations and will bring them down into the valley of Josaphat: and I will plead with them there|congregabo omnes gentes, et deducam eas in vallem Josaphat, et disceptabo cum eis ibi]], etc. This is commonly explained literally of the time of Christ's second coming, or of the day of judgement: from which it seems that the beginning of this chapter is to be referred to the same time. And many other things follow in this chapter which cause the greatest entanglement. For this reason the expositors expound this text in quite different ways.

paras.t: Verum sequendo beatissimum archiapostolum Petrum, dicendum quod principium hujus capituli litteraliter loquitur pro tempore primitivæ Ecclesiæ atque dominicæ passionis, resurrectionis, ac Spiritus Sancti missionis. Ut sit sensus : Et erit, id est fiet, post hæc, id est post tempus et gesta quæ in præcedenti capitulo sunt descripta, ubi Judæis promissa fuit magna beneficiorum exhibitio post tribulationem eis illatam ab Assyriis seu Chaldæis : Effundam spiritum meum, id est, Spiritum Sanctum a me procedentem, liberaliter dabo ac mittam, super omnem carnem, id est super omnem hominem : ut sit distributio non pro singulis generum, sed pro generibus singulorum, videlicet super viros ac feminas, super senes ac juvenes, divites et pauperes, nobiles et ignobiles, vel super Judæos et gentiles. Unde in Actibus dixerunt Judæi, audito quod Cornelius centurio et qui cum eo fuerunt, recepissent Spiritum Sanctum in signo sensibili : Ergo et in nationes gratia Dei effusa est. Patetque in toto libro apostolicorum Actuum, quomodo tempore primitivæ Ecclesiæ gentibus data est admirabilis gratia. Per carnem itaque intelligit hominem, sicut et Isaias quum ait : Videbit omnis caro salutare Dei nostri ; et Joannes, Verbum caro factum est ; itemque Psalmista, Ad te omnis caro veniet. Proprie quoque accipitur hic caro pro homine habente cor non durum, lapideum, obstinatum, sed pium, molle, atque per modum carnis tenerum, ad Spiritus Sancti susceptionem dispositum.
paras.en: But following the most blessed archapostle Peter, we must say that the beginning of this chapter speaks literally of the time of the primitive Church, and of the Lord's passion and resurrection, and the sending of the Holy Ghost.
