So that the sense is: [[2:28|And it shall come to pass|Et erit]], that is, it shall be done, [[2:28|after this|post hæc]], that is, after the time and the deeds described in the preceding chapter, where a great showing of benefits was promised to the Jews after the tribulation brought on them by the Assyrians or Chaldeans: [[2:28|I will pour out my spirit|Effundam spiritum meum]], that is, I will freely give and send the Holy Ghost, who proceeds from me, [[2:28|upon all flesh|super omnem carnem]], that is, upon every man: so that the distribution holds not for every single one of each kind, but for single ones of every kind [a scholastic distinction: "all flesh" means men of every sort, not every man without exception], namely upon men and women, upon old and young, rich and poor, noble and lowly, or upon Jews and Gentiles. Hence in the Acts the Jews, having heard that Cornelius the centurion and those who were with him had received the Holy Ghost in a sign perceptible to the senses, said: So then [[Acts 10:45|the grace of the Holy Ghost was poured out upon the Gentiles also|et in nationes gratia Dei effusa est]] [Denis has "the grace of God"]. And it is plain throughout the whole book of the Acts of the Apostles how, in the time of the primitive Church, wonderful grace was given to the Gentiles. By *flesh*, then, he understands man, as Isaias too does when he says[[Is 40:5||]]: [[Luke 3:6|all flesh shall see the salvation of God|Videbit omnis caro salutare Dei nostri]] [Denis's words are those in which Luke 3:6 gives this prophecy of Isaias, with "of our God" from Is 52:10; Is 40:5 itself reads "all flesh together shall see, that the mouth of the Lord hath spoken"]; and John: [[John 1:14|the Word was made flesh|Verbum caro factum est]]; and likewise the Psalmist: [[Ps 64:3|all flesh shall come to thee|Ad te omnis caro veniet]]. *Flesh* is also taken here, properly, for a man whose heart is not hard, stony, obstinate, but devout, soft, and tender after the manner of flesh, disposed to receive the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Et prophetabunt filii vestri et filiæ vestræ, id est Apostoli aliique discipuli Christi et Apostolorum ex Judaismo conversi, et multæ discipulæ Christi et Apostolorum, quarum aliquæ cum Apostolis in die Pentecostes receperunt Spiritum Sanctum in cœnaculo illo grandi, in quo Christus fecit novissimam Cœnam. Unde in Actibus habetur, quod Apostoli erant perseverantes in oratione cum mulieribus et Maria Matre Jesu et fratribus ejus. Philippus quoque unus de septem diaconis, habuit quatuor filias virgines prophetissas. Sed et Philippus apostolus scribitur duas habuisse filias sanctissimas prophetissas. Hi autem fuerunt filii et filiæ Judæorum. Quanta vero prophetaverunt Apostoli, præsertim Joannes in Apocalypsi, patet partim in scripturis eorum.
paras.en: [[2:28|And your sons and your daughters shall prophesy|Et prophetabunt filii vestri et filiæ vestræ]], that is, the Apostles and other disciples of Christ and of the Apostles converted from Judaism, and many women disciples of Christ and of the Apostles, some of whom received the Holy Ghost together with the Apostles on the day of Pentecost, in that great upper room in which Christ held the Last Supper[[Luke 22:12||]]. Hence we have in the Acts that the Apostles [[Acts 1:14|were persevering|erant perseverantes]] [[Acts 1:14|in prayer with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren|in oratione cum mulieribus et Maria Matre Jesu et fratribus ejus]]. Philip too, one of the seven deacons[[Acts 21:8||]], had [[Acts 21:9|four daughters, virgins, who did prophesy|quatuor filias virgines prophetissas]]. And Philip the apostle as well is written to have had two most holy daughters who were prophetesses [so Polycrates of Ephesus, quoted by Eusebius, Church History III, 31]. Now these were sons and daughters of the Jews. And how much the Apostles prophesied, John above all in the Apocalypse, is plain in part from their writings.

paras.t: Senes vestri, o Judæi, id est seniores in primitiva Ecclesia, qui vere senes fuerunt, ætate, sapientia et moribus, somnia somniabunt, id est, prophetales revelationes, quæ communiter dantur tempore somni, recipient atque intelligent. In somno enim aptior est anima ad revelationem cœlestem ac prophetalem, propter imaginativæ quietem, et ab exterioribus sensibus abstractionem. Propter quod scriptum est in Job : Per somnium in visione nocturna aperit aures virorum. In Numeris quoque Dominus Aaron et Mariæ ait : Si fuerit inter vos Propheta, in visione apparebo ei, vel per somnium loquar ad eum. Talia ergo somnia non sunt vana ac solita omnibus. Tale etiam fuit somnium Pauli, quando vir Macedo apparuit Paulo dormienti, dicens, Transiens in Macedoniam, adjuva nos : prout in Actibus legitur. Et juvenes vestri visiones videbunt, id est, divinas revelationes habebunt, vel propheticas visiones intelligent. Unde in Ecclesia Antiochiæ erant doctores et Prophetæ, atque in aliis locis diversis, puta in Tyro, ut in Actibus recitat Lucas.
paras.en: [[2:28|Your old men|Senes vestri]], O Jews, that is, the elders in the primitive Church, who were truly old in age, wisdom and conduct, [[2:28|shall dream dreams|somnia somniabunt]]: that is, they shall receive and understand prophetic revelations, which are commonly given in time of sleep. For in sleep the soul is more apt for heavenly and prophetic revelation, because of the quiet of the imagination and its withdrawal from the outward senses. Wherefore it is written in Job: [[Job 33:15|By a dream in a vision by night|Per somnium in visione nocturna]] [[Job 33:16|he openeth the ears of men|aperit aures virorum]]. In Numbers too the Lord says to Aaron and Mary: [[Num 12:6|If there be among you a prophet|Si fuerit inter vos Propheta]], [[Num 12:6|I will appear to him in a vision, or I will speak to him in a dream|in visione apparebo ei, vel per somnium loquar ad eum]]. Such dreams, then, are not vain, nor common to all. Such too was the dream of Paul, when a man of Macedonia appeared to Paul as he slept, saying: [[Acts 16:9|Pass over into Macedonia and help us|Transiens in Macedoniam, adjuva nos]], as we read in the Acts. [[2:28|And your young men shall see visions|Et juvenes vestri visiones videbunt]], that is, they shall have divine revelations, or understand prophetic visions. Hence in the church of Antioch there were doctors and prophets[[Acts 13:1||]], and in various other places, for instance at Tyre[[Acts 21:4||]], as Luke relates in the Acts.

paras.t: Sed et super servos meos et ancillas meas, de quibus jam dictum est, vel alios ordinis et gradus inferioris, videlicet super credentes communiter, in diebus illis, tempore evangelicæ legis ac gratiæ, crescente quotidie primitiva Ecclesia, effundam spiritum meum, dona Sancti Spiritus infundendo, quamvis non prophetaverint. In primitiva quippe Ecclesia dabatur communiter baptizatis Spiritus Sanctus in signo visibili, etiam ad diversos effectus gratiæ gratis datæ, ita ut loquerentur linguis, miracula facerent, prophetarent : quod fiebat per impositionem manus Apostolorum, ut patet in Actibus.
paras.en: [[2:29|Moreover, upon my servants and handmaids|Sed et super servos meos et ancillas meas]], of whom we have already spoken, or others of lower order and rank, namely upon believers in general, [[2:29|in those days|in diebus illis]], in the time of the law of the Gospel and of grace, as the primitive Church grew daily, [[2:29|I will pour forth my spirit|effundam spiritum meum]], pouring in the gifts of the Holy Ghost, even if they did not prophesy. For in the primitive Church the Holy Ghost was commonly given to the baptized in a visible sign, even for various effects of grace *gratis data* [that is, graces freely given for the good of others, such as tongues, miracles and prophecy, as distinct from the grace that makes a man holy], so that they spoke in tongues, worked miracles, and prophesied: which was done by the laying on of the Apostles' hands, as is plain in the Acts[[Acts 8:17||]].

paras.t: Porro quod dictum est, Effundam Spiritum meum, potest esse verbum Patris, vel Filii, vel utriusque simul, in quantum sunt unum principium, unusque spirator et fons Spiritus Sancti, quum in utroque sit una natura, eademque voluntas, quemadmodum tres Personæ sunt unus Creator. Denique Spiritus Sanctus, qui est Deus verus, incommutabilis et immensus, dicitur dari sive effundi, non quod mutetur aut variet locum, sed quoniam dona ejus donantur et liberaliter effunduntur. De hac Spiritus Sancti effusione dictum est apud Isaiam : Effundam Spiritum meum super semen tuum, et benedictionem meam super stirpem tuam. In Zacharia quoque dicitur : Effundam super domum David Spiritum gratiæ et precum. Per verba etiam præinducta prænunciavit Propheta, quod tempore jam præfato daretur Spiritus Sanctus et gratia prophetiæ multo abundantius quam unquam ante : quod in tantum verum est, ut dicat Joannes, Spiritus nondum erat datus, quia Jesus nondum erat glorificatus : quia et ista tam copiosa et evidens Spiritus Sancti effusio, erat declaratio glorificationis Christi in anima et corpore, usque ad sessionem in dextera Patris.
paras.en: Now the words [[2:28|I will pour out my spirit|Effundam Spiritum meum]] may be the word of the Father, or of the Son, or of both together, inasmuch as they are one principle and one spirator and fount of the Holy Ghost [spirator: he who breathes forth the Holy Ghost; Father and Son breathe him forth as one], since in both there is one nature and the same will, just as the three Persons are one Creator. Further, the Holy Ghost, who is true God, unchangeable and immense, is said to be given or poured out, not because he is changed or moves from place to place, but because his gifts are given and freely poured out. Of this outpouring of the Holy Ghost it is said in Isaias: [[Is 44:3|I will pour out my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thy stock|Effundam Spiritum meum super semen tuum, et benedictionem meam super stirpem tuam]]. In Zacharias too it is said: [[Zach 12:10|I will pour out upon the house of David|Effundam super domum David]] [[Zach 12:10|the spirit of grace, and of prayers|Spiritum gratiæ et precum]]. By the words set down above, moreover, the Prophet foretold that in the time already mentioned the Holy Ghost and the grace of prophecy would be given far more abundantly than ever before: which is so true that John says: [[John 7:39|as yet the Spirit was not given, because Jesus was not yet glorified|Spiritus nondum erat datus, quia Jesus nondum erat glorificatus]]: for this so copious and evident outpouring of the Holy Ghost was the declaration of Christ's glorification in soul and body, even to his sitting at the right hand of the Father.

paras.t: Et dabo prodigia in cælo et in terra, sanguinem, et ignem, et vaporem fumi. Quidam hunc locum usque ad illud, Et erit, Omnis qui invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit, referunt ad tempus secundi adventus Christi. Sed quum S. Petrus apostolus omnia verba ista alleget, et illo in tempore impleta affirmet, consequens, ut sicut præcedentia, ita et ista ad primum Christi referantur adventum, et ad Paracleti missionem.
paras.en: [[2:30|And I will shew wonders in heaven; and in earth, blood, and fire, and vapour of smoke.|Et dabo prodigia in cælo et in terra, sanguinem, et ignem, et vaporem fumi]] Some refer this passage, up to the words [[2:32|And it shall come to pass, that every one that shall call upon the name of the Lord, shall be saved|Et erit, Omnis qui invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit]], to the time of Christ's second coming. But since St. Peter the apostle cites all these words[[Acts 2:19||]] [the margin gives Acts 2:16–21] and affirms that they were fulfilled at that time, it follows that, like what goes before, these too are to be referred to Christ's first coming and to the sending of the Paraclete.

paras.t: Christo ergo pendente in crucis patibulo, data sunt prodigia magna in cælo : quia obscuratus est sol tempore oppositionis, ita quod luna plena exsistens, et soli directe opposita, rediit, seque soli supernaturaliter supposuit : circa quam eclipsim multa mirabilia contigerunt, quemadmodum in epistola ad magnum atque sanctissimum Polycarpum, sacratissimus, divinissimus, atque magnus theologus Dionysius protestatur. Rursus datum fuit prodigium in cælo, dum Christo Patrem orante, te, Pater, clarifica Filium tuum ; venit vox, dicens : Et clarificavi, et iterum clarificabo. Tunc enim quidam dixerunt, tonitruum factum esse. Alii dixerunt, Angelus ei locutus est : et hi verum profati sunt. Maximum quoque prodigium in cælo peractum est, dum Christo in die ascensionis cum patribus ad patriam ascendente, nubes eum suscepit, et angeli sancti occurrentes, quasdam quæstiones moverunt. Sed et in nocte dominicæ nativitatis cælestis exercitus descendit, ac cecinit, Gloria in altissimis Deo : quando et stella Magis apparuit. Daboque prodigia in terra : quando videlicet Christo in cruce levato, terra mota est, petræ scissæ, monumenta aperta, et multa corpora sanctorum surrexerunt cum Christo. Et in hora dominicæ resurrectionis, sicut Matthæus narrat, terræ motus factus est magnus. Angelus enim Domini descendit de cælo, et accedens revolvit lapidem : præ cujus timore custodes sepulcri facti sunt quasi exanimes. Denique Christus adhuc conversans in terra, infinita fecit miracula, et in nomine ejus sui discipuli multa sunt prodigia operati.
paras.en: So while Christ hung on the gibbet of the cross, great wonders were given [[2:30|in heaven|in cælo]]: for [[Luke 23:45|the sun was darkened|obscuratus est sol]] at the time of opposition [that is, at the full moon, when the moon stands opposite the sun and cannot naturally eclipse it], in such a way that the moon, being full and directly opposite the sun, came back and supernaturally placed itself beneath the sun: and about this eclipse many wonders happened, as the most sacred, most divine and great theologian Dionysius testifies in his letter to the great and most holy Polycarp [Dionysius the Areopagite, Letter VII]. Again a wonder was given in heaven when, as Christ prayed to the Father: Father, [[John 17:1|Glorify thy Son|clarifica Filium tuum]] [these words are from John 17:1; in the passage the margin gives, John 12:28, Christ says "Father, glorify thy name"], there came a voice saying: [[John 12:28|I have both glorified it and will glorify it again|Et clarificavi, et iterum clarificabo]]. For then some said that it had thundered[[John 12:29||]]. Others said: [[John 12:29|An angel spoke to him|Angelus ei locutus est]]: and these spoke the truth. A very great wonder too was wrought in heaven when, as Christ on the day of the ascension was going up with the fathers to the fatherland, [[Acts 1:9|a cloud received him|nubes eum suscepit]], and the holy angels, coming to meet him, raised certain questions[[Is 63:1||]][[Ps 23:8||]] [the margin gives Is. lxiii, 1, 2 and Ps. xxiii, 7–10: "Who is this that cometh from Edom?" and "Who is this King of Glory?"]. And in the night of the Lord's nativity, too, the heavenly host came down and sang: [[Luke 2:14|Glory to God in the highest|Gloria in altissimis Deo]]; when the star also appeared to the Magi[[Matt 2:2||]]. [[2:30|And I will shew wonders|Daboque prodigia]] [[2:30|in earth|in terra]]: namely when, Christ being lifted up on the cross, [[Matt 27:51|the earth quaked and the rocks were rent|terra mota est, petræ scissæ]], [[Matt 27:52|the graves were opened: and many bodies of the saints|monumenta aperta, et multa corpora sanctorum]] [[Matt 27:52|arose|surrexerunt]] with Christ. And in the hour of the Lord's resurrection, as Matthew relates, [[Matt 28:2|there was a great earthquake. For an angel of the Lord descended from heaven and coming rolled back the stone|terræ motus factus est magnus. Angelus enim Domini descendit de cælo, et accedens revolvit lapidem]]: for fear of whom the guards of the sepulchre became as if lifeless[[Matt 28:4||]]. Lastly, Christ, while still living on earth, worked numberless miracles, and in his name his disciples worked many wonders.

paras.t: Deinde in speciali exemplificat quædam prodigiorum istorum, videlicet sanguinem, qui de latere Christi jam mortui cum aqua supernaturaliter emanavit, de quo fertur in Psalmo : Ut intingatur pes tuus in sanguine. Mirabile etiam fuit, quod unigenitus Filius Dei sanctus et innocens, sanguinem suum fudit pro mundo, amarissimam ac turpissimam sustinens mortem. Propter quod apud Isaiam angeli sciscitati leguntur : Quare rubrum est indumentum tuum, videlicet corpus assumptum, tempore passionis sanguine rubricatum ? Nam et de Christo in Canticis fertur : Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus. Et ignem : in cujus specie Spiritus Sanctus descendit super Apostolos, juxta illud Actuum : Apparuerunt illis dispertitæ linguæ tanquam ignis, seditque supra singulos eorum. Vel, Ignem, id est Spiritus Sancti fervorem, quo Christus corda suorum mirabiliter inflammavit, ita ut duo ex illis assererent : Nonne cor nostrum ardens erat in nobis ? De quo ait Salvator apud Lucam : Ignem veni mittere in terram, et quid volo nisi ut accendatur ? Vel, Ignem : de quo et in Matthæo ait Joannes Baptista, Ipse baptizabit vos Spiritu Sancto et igni : ubi per ignem, secundum unam expositionem, intelligitur ignis tribulationis. Mirabilis autem fuit Ecclesiæ primitivæ persecutio. Et vaporem fumi, id est tenebras infidelitatis et supplicia, secundum Hieronymum, quibus Deus permissive excæcavit animas Judæorum, quos et per Romanos punivit. Unde quum Isaias visionem illam describeret, in qua sibi Judæorum excæcatio prænuntiabatur, dixit quod domus impleta est fumo. Vel ad litteram, ignis qui in die Pentecostes super credentes descendit, potuit aliquid de fumo habere seu causare quemdam vaporem, ad ampliorem divinæ majestatis ostensionem, sicut mons Sinai fumigabat. Quidam etiam per vaporem fumi, intelligunt compunctionem cordis et lacrimas Judæorum, qui ut in Actibus habetur, ad prædicationem Petri compuncti sunt corde, dicentes : Quid faciemus, viri fratres ? Unde et Zacharias : In die illa, inquit, planctus magnus erit in Jerusalem.
paras.en: Then he gives in particular some instances of these wonders, namely [[2:30|blood|sanguinem]], which flowed supernaturally with water from the side of Christ, already dead[[John 19:34||]]; of which it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 67:24|That thy foot may be dipped in the blood|Ut intingatur pes tuus in sanguine]]. It was a wonder also that the only-begotten Son of God, holy and innocent, shed his blood for the world, enduring a most bitter and most shameful death. For this reason the angels are read in Isaias to have asked: [[Is 63:2|Why then is thy apparel red|Quare rubrum est indumentum tuum]], that is, the body he had taken, reddened with blood at the time of the passion? For of Christ, too, it is said in the Canticle: [[Cant 5:10|My beloved is white and ruddy|Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus]]. [[2:30|And fire|Et ignem]]: in the form of which the Holy Ghost came down upon the Apostles, according to that of the Acts: [[Acts 2:3|there appeared to them parted tongues, as it were of fire: and it sat upon every one of them|Apparuerunt illis dispertitæ linguæ tanquam ignis, seditque supra singulos eorum]]. Or, *fire*, that is, the fervour of the Holy Ghost, with which Christ wonderfully inflamed the hearts of his own, so that two of them declared: [[Luke 24:32|Was not our heart burning within us|Nonne cor nostrum ardens erat in nobis]]? Of which the Saviour says in Luke: [[Luke 12:49|I am come to cast fire on the earth. And what will I, but that it be kindled?|Ignem veni mittere in terram, et quid volo nisi ut accendatur]] Or, *fire*: of which John the Baptist too says in Matthew: [[Matt 3:11|he shall baptize you in the Holy Ghost and fire|Ipse baptizabit vos Spiritu Sancto et igni]]: where by fire, according to one exposition, is understood the fire of tribulation. And wonderful was the persecution of the primitive Church. [[2:30|And vapour of smoke|Et vaporem fumi]], that is, according to Jerome, the darkness of unbelief, and the punishments, with which God, by permitting it, blinded the souls of the Jews, whom he also punished by the Romans. Hence when Isaias described that vision in which the blinding of the Jews was foretold to him, he said that [[Is 6:4|the house was filled with smoke|domus impleta est fumo]]. Or, literally, the fire which came down upon the believers on the day of Pentecost[[Acts 2:3||]] could have had something of smoke, or caused a kind of vapour, for a fuller showing of the divine majesty, as Mount Sinai smoked[[Ex 19:18||]]. Some, too, understand by the vapour of smoke the compunction of heart and the tears of the Jews, who, as we have in the Acts, at Peter's preaching [[Acts 2:37|had compunction in their heart|compuncti sunt corde]], saying: [[Acts 2:37|What shall we do, men and brethren?|Quid faciemus, viri fratres]] Hence Zacharias too: [[Zach 12:11|In that day|In die illa]], he says, [[Zach 12:11|there shall be a great lamentation in Jerusalem|planctus magnus erit in Jerusalem]].

paras.t: Sol convertetur in tenebras, et luna in sanguinem. Hoc (sicut nunc tactum est) Christo suspenso ac inæstimabiliter patiente, sol et luna quasi compassi sunt Creatori ac Domino suo, nec lumen suum præbuerunt his qui fontem luminis exstinxerunt. Non tamen in se ipso mutatus aut luce privatus est sol, aut luna effecta sanguinea, sed quoad apparentiam, et quia mundo induxerunt caliginem. Solet autem luna, quum patitur eclipsim, rubea apparere. Verumtamen quando directe supponitur soli, non rubea, sed nigra videtur. Unde si pro tempore suppositionis illius rubea apparebat, mirabiliter factum est : quod Hieronymus dicit credi posse, quamvis scriptum non sit, quia non omnia scripta sunt.
paras.en: [[2:31|The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood|Sol convertetur in tenebras, et luna in sanguinem]]. This came about (as was touched on just now) when, as Christ hung and suffered beyond all reckoning[[Luke 23:44||]][[Luke 23:45||]], the sun and moon as it were suffered with their Creator and Lord, and did not give their light to those who were putting out the fount of light. Yet the sun was not changed in itself or deprived of light, nor was the moon made bloody, except in appearance, and in that they brought darkness upon the world. Now the moon, when it suffers an eclipse, usually appears red. Yet when it is placed directly beneath the sun, it looks not red but black. Hence if at the time of that placing beneath the sun it appeared red, this was done by a wonder: which Jerome says may be believed, though it is not written, since not all things are written[[John 21:25||]].

paras.t: Antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et horribilis : per quem intelligi potest dies judicii impiis metuendus, ante quem facta sunt ista. Sed quia mox subditur, Et erit, Omnis qui invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit : quod Paulus ad Romanos, et Petrus in Actibus, exponunt de tempore Christi et initio evangelicæ prædicationis ; Hieronymus dicit, per diem istum potius intelligendum diem dominicæ resurrectionis, qui fuit diabolo impiisque Judæis terribilis et magnus in se. De quo cantat Psalmista : Hæc est dies quam fecit Dominus. Unde translatio Septuaginta interpretum continet : Antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et illustris. Quibusdam vero apparet, quod dies dominicæ resurrectionis non soleat dici horribilis ; et item, quod ad contenebrationem solis et lunæ præfatam, non habeat proprie condependentiam dies finalis judicii. Potest autem, ut arbitror, per diem Domini magnum et horribilem, intelligi dies captivitatis Judæorum, et totalis destructio Jerusalem et Judææ a Romanis, quem Christus apud Lucam prædixit : de quo die multa prædixerunt Prophetæ. De quo ait et Christus in Isaia : Dies ultionis in corde meo.
paras.en: [[2:31|Before the great and dreadful day of the Lord doth come|Antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et horribilis]]: by which may be understood the day of judgement, to be feared by the wicked, before which these things came to pass. But since straight after this follows: [[2:32|And it shall come to pass, that every one that shall call upon the name of the Lord, shall be saved|Et erit, Omnis qui invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit]], which Paul to the Romans[[Rom 10:13||]] and Peter in the Acts[[Acts 2:21||]] expound of the time of Christ and the beginning of the preaching of the Gospel, Jerome says that by this day is rather to be understood the day of the Lord's resurrection, which was dreadful to the devil and the wicked Jews, and great in itself. Of which the Psalmist sings: [[Ps 117:24|This is the day which the Lord hath made|Hæc est dies quam fecit Dominus]]. Hence the translation of the Seventy interpreters has: Before the great and illustrious day of the Lord come [the Septuagint's word is rendered "manifest" where St. Peter quotes it, Acts 2:20]. But to some it seems that the day of the Lord's resurrection is not usually called dreadful; and also that the day of the final judgement has no proper connection with the darkening of the sun and moon spoken of above. But by the great and dreadful day of the Lord may be understood, as I think, the day of the captivity of the Jews, and the total destruction of Jerusalem and Judea by the Romans, which Christ foretold in Luke[[Luke 19:43||]][[Luke 19:44||]]: of which day the Prophets foretold much. Of which Christ also says in Isaias: [[Is 63:4|the day of vengeance is in my heart|Dies ultionis in corde meo]].

paras.t: Et erit tempore evangelicæ legis : Omnis qui invocaverit, id est, intus cum attentione, cum cordiali affectu oraverit nomen Domini nominatum, id est Deum seu Christum nomine designatum, salvus erit a languore peccati in via per gratiam, et a damnatione inferni in patria per gloriam. Prope enim est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum, omnibus invocantibus eum in veritate. Porro invocatio ista, secundum Hieronymum, non est leve aliquid, nec incipientium, sed perfectorum. De qualibus scriptum est in Psalmo : Moyses et Aaron in sacerdotibus ejus, et Samuel inter eos qui invocant nomen ejus. Unde et in Ecclesiastico inducitur : Quis invocavit Deum, et despexit eum ?
paras.en: [[2:32|And it shall come to pass|Et erit]] in the time of the law of the Gospel: [[2:32|every one that shall call upon|Omnis qui invocaverit]], that is, shall pray inwardly with attention, with heartfelt affection, [[2:32|the name of the Lord|nomen Domini]] named, that is, God or Christ designated by the name, [[2:32|shall be saved|salvus erit]] from the sickness of sin on the way, through grace, and from the damnation of hell in the fatherland, through glory [*in via* and *in patria*: in this life and in heaven]. For [[Ps 144:18|The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him: to all that call upon him in truth|Prope enim est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum, omnibus invocantibus eum in veritate]]. Now this calling upon him, according to Jerome, is no light thing, nor a thing of beginners, but of the perfect. Of such it is written in the Psalm: [[Ps 98:6|Moses and Aaron among his priests: and Samuel among them that call upon his name|Moyses et Aaron in sacerdotibus ejus, et Samuel inter eos qui invocant nomen ejus]]. Hence in Ecclesiasticus too it is put: [[Ecclus 2:12|who hath called upon him, and he despised him?|Quis invocavit Deum, et despexit eum]]

paras.t: Quia in monte Sion et in Jerusalem erit salvatio, id est in primitiva Ecclesia, quæ primo collecta fuit post Christi passionem ac resurrectionem in urbe sancta Jerusalem, et in cœnaculo ubi Spiritum Sanctum recepit, quod situm fuit in monte Sion, juxta templum. In hoc itaque loco ac populo fecit Christus salutem, dando ibi primitias Spiritus Sancti, atque per prædicationem eorum qui ibi demorati sunt, totum sæculum convertendo. Propter quod scriptum est in Isaia : De Sion exibit lex, et verbum Domini de Jerusalem. Ibi enim Christus per se ipsum prædicavit, ibi fundata est lex novi Testamenti, et primo annuntiata per sanctos Apostolos, ac deinde per universum orbem, secundum quod Christus ait discipulis suis in die ascensionis : Eritis mihi testes in Jerusalem, et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ ; et in Luca : Oportebat pati Christum, et prædicari in nomine ejus pœnitentiam et remissionem peccatorum in omnes gentes, incipientibus a Jerusalem.
paras.en: [[2:32|for in Mount Sion, and in Jerusalem shall be salvation|Quia in monte Sion et in Jerusalem erit salvatio]], that is, in the primitive Church, which was first gathered after Christ's passion and resurrection in the holy city of Jerusalem[[Acts 1:12||]], and in the upper room where it received the Holy Ghost[[Acts 1:13||]][[Acts 2:1||]], which stood on Mount Sion, near the temple. In this place and people, then, Christ wrought salvation, giving there the first fruits of the Holy Ghost, and converting the whole world through the preaching of those who had stayed there. For this reason it is written in Isaias: [[Is 2:3|the law shall come forth from Sion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem|De Sion exibit lex, et verbum Domini de Jerusalem]]. For there Christ preached in person[[Matt 26:55||]][[Luke 19:47||]][[Luke 21:37||]][[John 7:14||]][[John 7:28||]]; there the law of the New Testament was founded, and announced first by the holy Apostles, and afterwards through the whole world, according to what Christ said to his disciples on the day of the ascension: [[Acts 1:8|you shall be witnesses unto me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and Samaria, and even to the uttermost part of the earth|Eritis mihi testes in Jerusalem, et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ]]; and in Luke: [[Luke 24:46|it behoved Christ to suffer|Oportebat pati Christum]], [[Luke 24:47|And that penance and remission of sins should be preached in his name, unto all nations, beginning at Jerusalem|et prædicari in nomine ejus pœnitentiam et remissionem peccatorum in omnes gentes, incipientibus a Jerusalem]].

paras.t: Et in residuis, id est in electis Judæorum reliquiis, quos Dominus vocaverit ad fidem et gratiam, intus clementer movendo, et foris per Apostolos exhortando. In his itaque fuit salvatio, quia per gratiam Christi salvati sunt. De quibus Isaias locutus est : Nisi Dominus Sabaoth reliquisset nobis semen, quasi Sodoma fuissemus. De quibus loquitur Paulus ad Romanos : Reliquiæ secundum electionem gratiæ, salvæ factæ sunt. Hi sunt illa millia Judæorum qui in Actibus Apostolorum credidisse leguntur, quorum aliquibus ante passionem Christus prædixit : Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum.
paras.en: [[2:32|And in the residue|Et in residuis]], that is, in the chosen remnant of the Jews, [[2:32|whom the Lord shall call|quos Dominus vocaverit]] to faith and grace, moving them mercifully within, and exhorting them outwardly through the Apostles. In these, then, there was salvation, because they were saved through the grace of Christ. Of these Isaias spoke: [[Is 1:9|Except the Lord of hosts had left us seed, we had been as Sodom|Nisi Dominus Sabaoth reliquisset nobis semen, quasi Sodoma fuissemus]] [Denis has "the Lord Sabaoth", as St. Paul quotes the verse in Rom 9:29]. Of these Paul speaks to the Romans: [[Rom 11:5|a remnant saved according to the election of grace|Reliquiæ secundum electionem gratiæ, salvæ factæ sunt]]. These are those thousands of the Jews who are read in the Acts of the Apostles to have believed[[Acts 2:41||]][[Acts 4:4||]], to some of whom Christ foretold before the passion: [[John 8:28|When you shall have lifted up, the Son of man, then shall you know that I am he|Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum]].

3.title: Elucidatio capituli tertii: Et erit post hæc: effundam spiritum meum.
3.title_en: Explanation of the third chapter: And it shall come to pass after this, that I will pour out my spirit.
3.note: Denis's third chapter begins at 2:28 (as in the Hebrew). This article's introduction and its commentary on 2:28–32 are shown under chapter 2.

paras.t: Quia ecce in diebus illis et in tempore illo, quum convertero captivitatem Juda et Jerusalem. Si locus iste ad litteram exponitur de die judicii, sicut communiter explanatur, tunc quod ait, In diebus illis et in tempore illo, non potest præcise referri ad tempus illud de quo in hujus capituli principio dictum est. Qui vero quod dictum est, Sol vertetur in tenebras et luna in sanguinem, exponunt pro tempore immediate præcedente diem judicii, faciliter transeunt, asserentes verba nunc exponenda ad illud tempus referenda. Sed quoniam ibi nullum tempus exprimitur, et paulo ante tempus expressum est, dicente Domino, Super servos meos et ancillas meas in diebus illis effundam Spiritum meum ; videtur Propheta nunc loqui pro tempore illo : quod ad litteram dici non potest, quum illud intelligatur de principio primitivæ Ecclesiæ, istud vero de fine ejus, quoad statum præsentem. Idcirco Hieronymus ad tropologiam convertitur : per quod non satisfit curioso lectori, quoniam litteralem sensum oportet poni pro fundamento.
paras.en: [[3:1|For behold in those days, and in that time when I shall bring back the captivity of Juda, and Jerusalem|Quia ecce in diebus illis et in tempore illo, quum convertero captivitatem Juda et Jerusalem]]. If this passage is expounded literally of the day of judgment, as it commonly is, then what he says, [[3:1|in those days, and in that time|In diebus illis et in tempore illo]], cannot be referred strictly to the time spoken of at the beginning of this chapter [that is, at 2:28, "And it shall come to pass after this", where this article begins]. But those who expound the words [[2:31|The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood|Sol vertetur in tenebras et luna in sanguinem]] of the time immediately before the day of judgment pass over this easily, asserting that the words now to be expounded are to be referred to that time. But since no time is expressed there, and a little before a time was expressed, when the Lord said, [[2:29|upon my servants and handmaids in those days I will pour forth my spirit|Super servos meos et ancillas meas in diebus illis effundam Spiritum meum]], the Prophet seems now to be speaking of that time: and this cannot be said literally, since that is understood of the beginning of the primitive Church, and this of its end, as to its present state. Jerome therefore turns to the tropological sense [that is, the moral reading]; but by this the inquiring reader is not satisfied, since the literal sense must be laid down as the foundation.

paras.t: Advertendum ergo, quod totum tempus a Christi adventu usque ad finem mundi, est ultima ætas, de qua ait Joannes in prima sua Canonica, Novissima hora est ; et Paulus, Nos, inquit, sumus in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt. Unde pro eo quod in principio hujus capituli dictum est, Et erit post hæc, Petrus sic allegavit, Et erit in novissimis diebus. Sic ergo quod nunc Dominus ait, In diebus illis et in tempore illo, referendum est ad tempus gratiæ ultimamque mundi ætatem, quantum ad ultimam ejus partem, sicut quod ait in principio capituli, refertur ad idem tempus eamdemque ætatem, quoad ejus principium. Totum nempe a qualibet suarum partium denominatur. In fine autem sæculi convertet Dominus captivitatem Juda et Jerusalem, id est, populum Judæorum ab Antichristo deceptum, et usque ad illud tempus a gentibus captivatum, reducet ad se, et a vinculis criminum absolutos, perducet ad fidem et caritatem veramque spiritus libertatem per prædicationem Enoch atque Eliæ.
paras.en: We must note, then, that the whole time from the coming of Christ to the end of the world is the last age, of which John says in his first canonical epistle, [[1 John 2:18|it is the last hour|Novissima hora est]]; and Paul: We, he says, are they [[1 Cor 10:11|upon whom the ends of the world are come|in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt]]. Hence for what was said at the beginning of this chapter, [[2:28|And it shall come to pass after this|Et erit post hæc]], Peter quoted it thus: [[Acts 2:17|And it shall come to pass, in the last days|Et erit in novissimis diebus]]. So, then, what the Lord now says, [[3:1|in those days, and in that time|In diebus illis et in tempore illo]], is to be referred to the time of grace and the last age of the world, as to its last part; just as what he says at the beginning of the chapter is referred to the same time and the same age, as to its beginning. For a whole is named from any one of its parts. And at the end of the world the Lord will [[3:1|bring back the captivity of Juda, and Jerusalem|captivitatem Juda et Jerusalem]]: that is, the people of the Jews, deceived by Antichrist and held captive by the Gentiles until that time, he will bring back to himself, and, loosing them from the bonds of their crimes, will lead them to faith and charity and the true liberty of the spirit, through the preaching of Enoch and Elias[[Mal 4:5||]].

paras.t: Congregabo omnes gentes in die judicii resuscitatas a morte, et deducam eas ministerio angelorum in vallem Josaphat, id est in locum illum qui est inter montem Oliveti et Jerusalem : non quod omnes poterunt in valle hac contineri, sed erunt in ea et in locis circumquaque adjacentibus ac vicinis. Christus vero apparebit in aere supra montem Oliveti, unde ascendit. Et disceptabo ibi cum eis, id est, redarguam eas, et justum ostendam judicium meum, ita quod opera omnium singulis innotescent, super populo meo et super hereditate mea Israel, id est propter peccata quæ commiserunt in filios Israel hereditarium populum meum : per quem hoc loco omnes electi fideles significantur; quos disperserunt in nationibus, a propria eos terra ejiciendo, et terram meam diviserunt, id est, terram quam dedi electis fidelibus, occupaverunt, quilibet partem sibi usurpando.
paras.en: [[3:2|I will gather together all nations|Congregabo omnes gentes]], raised from death on the day of judgment, [[3:2|and will bring them down|et deducam eas]] by the ministry of the angels [[3:2|into the valley of Josaphat|in vallem Josaphat]], that is, into that place which lies between Mount Olivet and Jerusalem: not that all will be able to be contained in this valley, but they will be in it and in the places lying round about and near it. And Christ will appear in the air above Mount Olivet, whence he ascended[[Acts 1:9||]][[Acts 1:12||]]. [[3:2|and I will plead with them there|Et disceptabo ibi cum eis]], that is, I will convict them, and show my judgment to be just, so that the works of all will be made known to each; [[3:2|for my people, and for my inheritance, Israel|super populo meo et super hereditate mea Israel]], that is, on account of the sins which they committed against the children of Israel, my people of inheritance, by whom all the faithful elect are signified in this place; [[3:2|whom they have scattered among the nations|quos disperserunt in nationibus]], by casting them out of their own land, [[3:2|and have parted my land|et terram meam diviserunt]], that is, they have seized the land which I gave to my faithful elect, each usurping a part for himself.

paras.t: Et super populum meum miserunt sortem: ita quod populum istum ac bona ejus sibi invicem sorte partiti sunt, quis quid acciperet. Et posuerunt puerum in prostibulo, id est, juvenes forma egregios in lupanaribus posuerunt, ut mercedem reciperent, quam pueri ab abutentibus, et peccata contra naturam patrantibus, sortirentur; et puellam, id est virgines speciosas (ponit enim singulare pro plurali), vendiderunt pro vino ut biberent, magis amantes turpissimas delectationes gulæ, quam proximos suos seu pueros et puellas. Hæc et multa similia multi impiissimi peregerunt. Possuntque ista specialiter accipi de gentibus quæ olim filiis Israel specialiter molestæ fuerunt. Denique de his peccatis dicit Dominus se facturum judicium, non quod de his tantum erit judicium, sed hæc quasi pro exemplo commemorat, quum sint contra caritatem fraternam, et pietatem omnibus naturalem: quemadmodum Christus in Evangelio, affirmans se omnes populos judicaturum, non facit mentionem nisi de operibus misericordiæ, vitiisque contrariis.
paras.en: [[3:3|And they have cast lots upon my people|Et super populum meum miserunt sortem]]: so that they divided this people and its goods among themselves by lot, who should receive what. [[3:3|and the boy they have put in the stews|Et posuerunt puerum in prostibulo]], that is, they put young men of outstanding beauty in brothels, to receive the hire which the boys would get from those who abused them and committed sins against nature; [[3:3|and the girl|et puellam]], that is, comely virgins (for he puts the singular for the plural), [[3:3|they have sold for wine, that they might drink|vendiderunt pro vino ut biberent]], loving the foulest pleasures of the gullet more than their neighbours, the boys and girls. These things and many like them were done by many most impious men. And these words can be taken especially of the Gentiles who were once especially troublesome to the children of Israel. Lastly, the Lord says that he will execute judgment for these sins: not that the judgment will be of these alone, but he mentions these as by way of example, since they are against fraternal charity and the compassion natural to all: just as Christ in the Gospel, declaring that he will judge all peoples, makes mention only of the works of mercy and the vices contrary to them[[Matt 25:31||]].

paras.t: Judæi excæcati dicunt, ea quæ dicta sunt atque sequentia, in sui Messiæ adventu implenda, ita quod ipsi tunc implebuntur spiritu Dei, et prophetabunt, omnesque nationes a quibus vastantur, tunc eis subjiciet rex Messias. Hæc miseri dicunt, quum sint carnales et litterales, non intelligentes quod sancti Prophetæ primum Christi adventum prænuntiarunt in omni paupertate, humilitate et passione, non in majestate et dominatione. Propter quod ait Jeremias: Quare quasi colonus futurus es in terra, et sicut viator declinans ad manendum? Et Isaias loquens de Christo: Inglorius, inquit, erit inter viros adspectus ejus. De quo Zacharias locutus est: Ecce rex tuus veniet tibi, ipse pauper et ascendens super asinam et pullum asinæ. Ideo loquitur de se ipso: Filius hominis non habet ubi caput reclinet.
paras.en: The blinded Jews say that what has been said, and what follows, is to be fulfilled at the coming of their Messias: so that they themselves will then be filled with the spirit of God and will prophesy, and King Messias will then make subject to them all the nations by which they are laid waste. This the wretched men say, since they are carnal and literal, not understanding that the holy Prophets foretold the first coming of Christ in all poverty, humility and suffering, not in majesty and dominion. Wherefore Jeremias says: [[Jer 14:8|why wilt thou be as a stranger in the land, and as a wayfaring man turning in to lodge?|Quare quasi colonus futurus es in terra, et sicut viator declinans ad manendum?]] And Isaias, speaking of Christ: [[Is 52:14|shall his visage be inglorious among men|Inglorius, inquit, erit inter viros adspectus ejus]], he says. Of him Zacharias spoke: [[Zach 9:9|BEHOLD THY KING will come to thee|Ecce rex tuus veniet tibi]], [[Zach 9:9|he is poor, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt, the foal of an ass|ipse pauper et ascendens super asinam et pullum asinæ]]. Therefore he says of himself: [[Matt 8:20|the Son of man hath not where to lay his head|Filius hominis non habet ubi caput reclinet]].

paras.t: Consequenter loquitur Dominus: Verum quid mihi et vobis, Tyrus et Sidon, et omnis terminus Palæstinorum? id est, quid concordiæ vel quid commune est mihi et vobis, o Tyrii atque Sidonii et Philistæi? Quasi dicat, Nihil. Quæ enim conventio lucis ad tenebras? Et quid tritico cum paleis? Numquid ultionem vos reddetis mihi? id est, quantum in vobis est, nitimini mihi resistere et nocere per hoc quod populum meum opprimitis. Dicit autem se Deus persecutionem pati, per hoc quod populus suus persecutionem sustinuit, quia hoc reputat sibi factum quod fit suis fidelibus, qui cum ipso sunt unum per caritatem. Propter quod ait apud Zachariam: Qui tetigerit vos, tanget pupillam oculi mei; et primo Regum ad Samuelem, Non te abjecerunt, sed me. Sicut et Christus in Evangelio: Quamdiu fecistis uni ex his, mihi fecistis; et alibi, Saule, Saule, quid me persequeris? Et si ulciscimini vos contra me, populum meum persequendo ad tempus, cito velociter reddam vicissitudinem vobis super caput vestrum, id est, debitam quam meremini, pœnam vobis infligam.
paras.en: Next the Lord says: [[3:4|But what have you to do with me, O Tyre, and Sidon, and all the coast of the Philistines?|Verum quid mihi et vobis, Tyrus et Sidon, et omnis terminus Palæstinorum?]] that is, what concord, or what is there in common, between me and you, O men of Tyre and of Sidon and Philistines? As if to say: Nothing. For [[2 Cor 6:14|what fellowship hath light with darkness?|Quæ enim conventio lucis ad tenebras?]] And [[Jer 23:28|what hath the chaff to do with the wheat|quid tritico cum paleis]]? [[3:4|will you revenge yourselves on me?|Numquid ultionem vos reddetis mihi?]] that is, as far as in you lies, you strive to resist me and to harm me by oppressing my people. Now God says that he suffers persecution in that his people have suffered persecution, because he counts as done to himself what is done to his faithful, who are one with him through charity. Wherefore he says in Zacharias: [[Zach 2:8|he that toucheth you, toucheth the apple of my eye|Qui tetigerit vos, tanget pupillam oculi mei]]; and in the first book of Kings, to Samuel: [[1 Kings 8:7|they have not rejected thee, but me|Non te abjecerunt, sed me]]. So too Christ in the Gospel: [[Matt 25:40|as long as you did it to one of these|Quamdiu fecistis uni ex his]], [[Matt 25:40|you did it to me|mihi fecistis]]; and elsewhere: [[Acts 9:4|Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?|Saule, Saule, quid me persequeris?]] [[3:4|and if you revenge yourselves on me|Et si ulciscimini vos contra me]], by persecuting my people for a time, [[3:4|I will very soon return you a recompense upon your own head|cito velociter reddam vicissitudinem vobis super caput vestrum]], that is, I will inflict on you the due punishment that you deserve.

paras.t: Consuetudo est Prophetarum, primo describere punitionem populi Judæorum, deinde gentium quæ eos impia intentione crudelique animo oppresserunt; tertio, gentium quæ istis consenserunt et cooperatæ fuerunt, quales fuerunt Tyrii, Sidonii, Philistæi, filii Ammon et Moab, ac Idumæi, quemadmodum patet in Isaia, Jeremia, Ezechiele, etc. Simili modo Joel procedit. Primo enim Judæorum vastitatem descripsit per erucam, locustam, bruchum atque æruginem. Deinde descripsit Assyriorum dejectionem. Nunc vero describit Tyriorum, Sidoniorum ac Palæstinorum pressuram, qui de Judæorum vastitate ab Assyriis et Chaldæis ac ceteris hostibus gloriabantur. Unde Dominus reddidit eis vicissitudinem, quia post captivitatem Judæorum a Chaldæis, etiam ipsi debellati fuerunt velociter ab eisdem, imo et partim ante ab Assyriis.
paras.en: It is the custom of the Prophets to describe first the punishment of the people of the Jews; then that of the Gentiles who oppressed them with wicked intent and cruel mind; thirdly, that of the Gentiles who consented to these and worked with them, such as were the men of Tyre and Sidon, the Philistines, the children of Ammon and Moab, and the Idumeans, as is plain in Isaias[[Is 23:1||]], Jeremias[[Jer 47:1||]][[Jer 48:1||]][[Jer 49:1||]], Ezechiel[[Ezech 25:1||]][[Ezech 26:1||]][[Ezech 35:1||]], etc. Joel proceeds in like manner. For first he described the devastation of the Jews by the palmerworm, the locust, the bruchus and the mildew. Then he described the overthrow of the Assyrians. And now he describes the affliction of the men of Tyre, of Sidon and of Palestine, who gloried in the devastation of the Jews by the Assyrians and Chaldeans and their other enemies. Hence the Lord returned them a recompense, since after the captivity of the Jews by the Chaldeans they too were swiftly conquered by the same, and indeed in part before that by the Assyrians.

paras.t: Causa autem pœnæ eorum subjungitur. Argentum enim meum et aurum tulistis, id est, argentum et aurum populi mei rapuistis injuste; et desiderabilia mea et pulcherrima, id est pretiosa vasa templi et ornamenta ejus præclara, intulistis in delubra vestra, id est in fana deorum seu templa idolorum ad ornatum eorum. Et filios Juda et filios Jerusalem vendidistis filiis Græcorum. Prædicti enim Tyrii et Sidonii et Philistæi, impenderunt auxilium hostibus Judæorum præfatis, sicque partem de præda atque mancipiis Judæorum adepti sunt, et eos qui cesserunt in partem suam, venundabant Græcis. Ut longe faceretis eos a finibus suis, id est, ad majorem cladem Judæorum faceretis eos remote abduci a terra Judææ.
paras.en: The cause of their punishment is then added. [[3:5|For you have taken away my silver, and my gold|Argentum enim meum et aurum tulistis]], that is, you have unjustly seized the silver and gold of my people; [[3:5|and my desirable, and most beautiful things|et desiderabilia mea et pulcherrima]], that is, the precious vessels of the temple and its splendid ornaments, [[3:5|you have carried into your temples|intulistis in delubra vestra]], that is, into the shrines of the gods, or temples of the idols, to adorn them. [[3:6|And the children of Juda, and the children of Jerusalem, you have sold to the children of the Greeks|Et filios Juda et filios Jerusalem vendidistis filiis Græcorum]]. For the aforesaid men of Tyre and Sidon and the Philistines gave help to the enemies of the Jews already named, and so obtained a share of the booty and of the captives of the Jews; and those who fell to their share they sold to the Greeks. [[3:6|that you might remove them far off from their own country|Ut longe faceretis eos a finibus suis]], that is, that you might have them carried far away from the land of Judea, to the greater ruin of the Jews.

paras.t: Ecce ego suscitabo, id est, a miseria relevabo, vel a captivitate liberabo, eos in loco, in quo vendidistis eos, id est in Græcia, ad quam ut ducerentur, venditi erant a vobis. Quod aliqui dicunt impletum tempore Cyri regis Persarum, qui dixit, Omnia regna terræ dedit mihi Deus cœli; deditque Judæis ubique licentiam redeundi in propria, ut Esdras refert. Videtur quoque impletum tempore Machabæorum, quando Judas et fratres ejus frequenter prævaluerunt Græcis terram Judææ intrantibus: quos sæpe non occiderunt, ut fratres suos in terra illorum captos reciperent liberos. Et convertam tribulationem vestram in caput vestrum, tradendo vos adversariis vestris.
paras.en: [[3:7|Behold, I will raise|Ecce ego suscitabo]], that is, I will lift up from misery, or free from captivity, [[3:7|them up|eos]] in the place [[3:7|wherein you have sold them|in quo vendidistis eos]] [Denis reads *in loco*, "in the place", where the Vulgate has *de loco*, "out of the place"], that is, in Greece, to which they had been sold by you to be taken. Some say this was fulfilled in the time of Cyrus king of the Persians, who said, [[1 Esd 1:2|the God of heaven hath given to me all the kingdoms of the earth|Omnia regna terræ dedit mihi Deus cœli]], and gave the Jews everywhere leave to return to their own land, as Esdras relates. It seems also to have been fulfilled in the time of the Machabees, when Judas and his brothers often prevailed over the Greeks who entered the land of Judea: these they often did not kill, so that they might receive back free their brethren who had been taken captive in their land. [[3:7|and I will return your recompense upon your own heads|Et convertam tribulationem vestram in caput vestrum]] [Denis reads *tribulationem*, "tribulation", where the Vulgate has *retributionem*, "recompense"], by delivering you to your adversaries.

paras.t: Et vendam filios vestros et filias vestras in manibus filiorum Juda, id est Judæis vel aliis per manus Judæorum. Quod constat impletum tempore Machabæorum, quando Judas et fratres ejus prævaluerunt principibus Antiochi regis et posteris: quibus prævalendo, captivam duxerunt magnam populi partem Tyriorum et aliorum locorum maritimorum, quos aliis vendiderunt, sicut subjungitur: et venundabunt eos Sabæis genti longinquæ, id est multum a Judæa distanti. Dicuntur autem Sabæi, secundum Glossam, a Saba regno ultra fines Æthiopiæ, de quo fuit regina Saba. Unde in Job habetur; Sabæi fecerunt tres turmas. Hieronymus vero asserit, quod regio ista sit trans Indiam; sed idem est, quoniam Æthiopia Indiæ pars est. Aliqui quoque affirmant, Sabæos Arabes esse. Hæc autem evenient, quia Dominus locutus est, id est, ista per me prædixit definitiva sententia, cujus dicere facere est, cujusque verbum non cassatur, juxta illud quod Balaam ait in Numeris: Non est Deus ut homo, ut mentiatur; neque ut filius hominis, ut mutetur. Dixit ergo, et non faciet? locutus est, et non implebit?
paras.en: [[3:8|And I will sell your sons, and your daughters, by the hands of the children of Juda|Et vendam filios vestros et filias vestras in manibus filiorum Juda]], that is, to the Jews, or to others by the hands of the Jews. This is known to have been fulfilled in the time of the Machabees, when Judas and his brothers prevailed over the captains of King Antiochus and his successors: prevailing over them, they led captive a great part of the people of Tyre and of other places on the sea coast, and sold them to others, as is added: [[3:8|and they shall sell them to the Sabeans, a nation far off|et venundabunt eos Sabæis genti longinquæ]], that is, very far distant from Judea. Now the Sabeans are so called, according to the Gloss, from Saba, a kingdom beyond the borders of Ethiopia, of which the queen of Saba was. Hence we read in Job: The Sabeans made three troops[[Job 1:15||]] [the margin gives Job i, 15, where the Sabeans fall upon Job's goods; the three troops are the Chaldeans', Job 1:17]. Jerome, however, asserts that this region lies beyond India; but it is the same thing, since Ethiopia is a part of India. Some also affirm that the Sabeans are Arabs. And these things will come to pass [[3:8|for the Lord hath spoken it|quia Dominus locutus est]], that is, he has foretold them through me by a definitive sentence, he whose saying is doing, and whose word is not made void; according to what Balaam says in Numbers: [[Num 23:19|God is not a man, that he should lie, nor is the son of man, that he should be changed. Hath he said then, and will he not do? hath he spoken, and will he not fulfil?|Non est Deus ut homo, ut mentiatur; neque ut filius hominis, ut mutetur. Dixit ergo, et non faciet? locutus est, et non implebit?]]

paras.t: Consequenter describitur pugna satellitum Antichristi contra sanctos et famulos Christi, quæ erit circa finem mundi. Hos autem satellites vel ipse Dominus ironice hortatur ad ea quæ subsequuntur, quia in propriam ea facient perniciem; vel ad servos Antichristi sermo dirigitur, prænuntiando magis quid facturi sint, quam exhortando ut faciant tanta mala. Ut sit sensus: Clamate hoc in gentibus, id est, ea quæ dicam clamabitis inter gentes, quibus dicetis: Sanctificate bellum, id est, justum bellum parate, et inite contra Christianos. Quamvis enim bellum illud erit injustissimum, quoniam conabuntur fidem Christi prorsus destruere, ipsi tamen justum illud reputabunt: quia ut dicit Apostolus, Mittet illis Deus spiritum erroris, ut credant mendacio. Suscitate robustos, id est, potentes sæculi hujus provocate ad adhærendum Antichristo, quem Christum esse dicetis. Ascendant, accedant omnes viri bellatores, applicando se exercitui Antichristi.
paras.en: Next is described the battle of the henchmen of Antichrist against the saints and servants of Christ, which will take place towards the end of the world. And either the Lord himself ironically urges these henchmen on to what follows, since they will do it to their own destruction; or the words are addressed to the servants of Antichrist, foretelling what they will do rather than urging them to do such great evils. So that the sense is: [[3:9|Proclaim ye this among the nations|Clamate hoc in gentibus]], that is, you will proclaim among the nations what I shall say, and you will say to them: [[3:9|Prepare war|Sanctificate bellum]] [Latin *sanctificate*, literally "sanctify": hence Denis's "just war"], that is, make ready a just war, and begin it against the Christians. For although that war will be most unjust, since they will try to destroy the faith of Christ utterly, yet they will think it just: because, as the Apostle says, [[2 Thess 2:10|God shall send them the operation of error, to believe lying|Mittet illis Deus spiritum erroris, ut credant mendacio]] [Denis reads *spiritum erroris*, "a spirit of error", where the Vulgate has *operationem erroris*]. [[3:9|raise up the strong|Suscitate robustos]], that is, stir up the mighty of this world to cleave to Antichrist, whom you will say is Christ. [[3:9|let them come, let all the men of war come up|Ascendant, accedant omnes viri bellatores]], joining themselves to the army of Antichrist.

paras.t: Concidite aratra vestra in gladios, et ligones vestros, quibus foditur terra, in lanceas: id est, aliis negotiis intermissis, instrumenta agriculturæ in arma convertite, ut sitis contra Christianos muniti. Infirmus dicat, Quia ego fortis sum, id est, nemo sit excusatus, sed etiam qui videntur ad bellandum inepti, animentur ad prælium.
paras.en: [[3:10|Cut your ploughshares into swords|Concidite aratra vestra in gladios]], [[3:10|and your spades|et ligones vestros]], with which the earth is dug, [[3:10|into spears|in lanceas]]: that is, setting aside other business, turn the tools of husbandry into weapons, so that you may be armed against the Christians. [[3:10|Let the weak say: I am strong|Infirmus dicat, Quia ego fortis sum]], that is, let no one be excused, but let even those who seem unfit for fighting be roused to battle.

paras.t: Erumpite de habitaculis vestris, et venite, omnes gentes, de circuitu, id est, undique ad Antichristum confluite. Ibi, id est in loco collectionis exercitus Antichristi, occumbere, id est cadere, faciet Dominus robustos tuos, o impia turba, id est, Antichristum cum quibusdam de potentibus suis occidet, quemadmodum dicit Apostolus : Quem Dominus Jesus interficiet spiritu oris sui, et destruet illustratione adventus sui. Et Isaias : Spiritu, inquit, labiorum suorum interficiet impium.
paras.en: [[3:11|Break forth|Erumpite]] from your dwellings [these words, *de habitaculis vestris*, are in Denis's text but not in the Vulgate], [[3:11|and come, all ye nations from round about|et venite, omnes gentes, de circuitu]], that is, flock together from every side to Antichrist. [[3:11|there|Ibi]], that is, in the place where the army of Antichrist is gathered, [[3:11|will the Lord cause all thy strong ones to fall down|faciet Dominus robustos tuos]] (fall down, that is, fall), O wicked throng: that is, he will slay Antichrist with some of his mighty ones, as the Apostle says: [[2 Thess 2:8|whom the Lord Jesus shall kill with the spirit of his mouth and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming|Quem Dominus Jesus interficiet spiritu oris sui, et destruet illustratione adventus sui]]. And Isaias: [[Is 11:4|with the breath|Spiritu]], he says, [[Is 11:4|of his lips he shall slay the wicked|labiorum suorum interficiet impium]].

paras.t: Consurgant, id est, resurgant a morte, et ascendant gentes de monumentis in vallem Josaphat, id est in locum illum, et ad loca in gyrum vicina. Veniet enim hora, in qua omnes qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem ejus. Quia ibi, non in ipsa valle, sed supra in aere, sedebo, ut judicem omnes gentes in circuitu, dando singulis quod merentur, et bonis et malis, juxta illud in Apocalypsi : Ecce venio cito, et merces mea mecum est, dare unicuique secundum opera sua.
paras.en: [[3:12|Let them arise|Consurgant]], that is, let them rise again from death, [[3:12|and let the nations come up|et ascendant gentes]] out of the tombs [[3:12|into the valley of Josaphat|in vallem Josaphat]], that is, into that place and the places round about near it. For [[John 5:28|the hour cometh wherein all that are in the graves shall hear the voice|Veniet enim hora, in qua omnes qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem]] of him. [[3:12|for there|Quia ibi]], not in the valley itself but above it in the air, [[3:12|I will sit to judge all nations round about|sedebo, ut judicem omnes gentes in circuitu]], giving to each what he deserves, both to the good and to the wicked, according to that saying in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 22:12|Behold, I come quickly: and my reward is with me, to render to every, man according to his works|Ecce venio cito, et merces mea mecum est, dare unicuique secundum opera sua]].

paras.t: Consequenter loquitur Dominus angelis sanctis. Mittite falces, id est, homines per modum frugum de terra colligite, ad judiciumque portate ; quoniam maturavit messis, id est, genus humanum ad finem ac maturitatem devenit, ita quod hora remunerationis jam instat, et tempus est ut electi congregentur in aream patriæ, reprobi vero in horrea tartari. Unde ait Salvator : Messis est consummatio sæculi, messores vero sunt angeli. Venite mecum, et descendite a cœlo super vallem Josaphat, o angeli universique Sancti : qui tunc cum Christo descendent, visibiliterque parebunt ad reverentiam Judicis, et terrorem accusationemque rebellium. Propter quod scriptum est in Judæ Canonica : Ecce venit Dominus in sanctis millibus suis facere judicium, et arguere omnes impios de omnibus operibus impietatis ipsorum. Et Isaias : Dominus, ait, ad judicium veniet cum senioribus populi sui et principibus ejus.
paras.en: Next the Lord speaks to the holy angels. [[3:13|Put ye in the sickles|Mittite falces]], that is, gather men from the earth in the manner of crops, and carry them to judgment; [[3:13|for the harvest is ripe|quoniam maturavit messis]], that is, the human race has come to its end and maturity, so that the hour of reward is now at hand, and it is time for the elect to be gathered into the threshing-floor of the fatherland, and the reprobate into the barns of hell. Hence the Saviour says: [[Matt 13:39|the harvest is the end of the world|Messis est consummatio sæculi]], [[Matt 13:39|the reapers are the angels|messores vero sunt angeli]]. [[3:13|come|Venite]] with me, [[3:13|and go down|et descendite]] from heaven upon the valley of Josaphat, O angels and all you Saints: who will then come down with Christ, and will appear visibly, for reverence to the Judge and for the terror and accusation of the rebellious. Wherefore it is written in the canonical epistle of Jude: [[Jude 1:14|Behold, the Lord cometh with thousands of his saints|Ecce venit Dominus in sanctis millibus suis]] [[Jude 1:15|To execute judgment|facere judicium]], [[Jude 1:15|and to reprove all the ungodly for all the works of their ungodliness|et arguere omnes impios de omnibus operibus impietatis ipsorum]]. And Isaias: [[Is 3:14|The Lord|Dominus]], he says, [[Is 3:14|will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and its princes|ad judicium veniet cum senioribus populi sui et principibus ejus]].

paras.t: Quia plenum est torcular, id est, vinea Ecclesiæ seu ipsa Ecclesia, quæ vinea nuncupatur, ad maturitatem devenit : sicut de messe prædictum est, quia per utrumque idem insinuatur. Exuberant torcularia, id est, corda hominum sunt impleta, ita quod ultra tempus promerendi nequaquam habebunt. Dicit autem Glossa, quod per messem maturam et torcularia redundantia, consummatio peccatorum et finis sæculi designatur. Propter quod subditur : quia multiplicata est malitia eorum, id est, in tantum creverunt eorum peccata, quod ultra toleranda non sunt, sed protinus punienda. Unde in Genesi, Sodoma et Gomorrha tunc deletæ narrantur, quando impleta fuit eorum malitia; et unumquemque tunc damnat Deus, quum mensuram pravitatis suæ impleverit. Hinc namque in Jeremia habetur : Non poterat vos Dominus ultra portare, propter malitiam studiorum vestrorum.
paras.en: [[3:13|for the press is full|Quia plenum est torcular]], that is, the vineyard of the Church, or the Church herself, which is called a vineyard, has come to maturity: as was said before of the harvest, since the same thing is signified by both. [[3:13|the fats run over|Exuberant torcularia]] [*fats*, that is, vats], that is, the hearts of men are filled, so that they will have no more time for meriting. And the Gloss says that by the ripe harvest and the overflowing presses the consummation of sins and the end of the world are signified. Wherefore it is added: [[3:13|for their wickedness is multiplied|quia multiplicata est malitia eorum]], that is, their sins have grown so great that they are no longer to be borne, but are to be punished forthwith. Hence in Genesis Sodom and Gomorrha are told to have been destroyed when their wickedness was full; and God condemns each man when he has filled up the measure of his depravity. For hence we read in Jeremias: [[Jer 44:22|the Lord could no longer bear, because of the evil of your doings|Non poterat vos Dominus ultra portare, propter malitiam studiorum vestrorum]].

paras.t: Populi, populi, id est, o populi universi, convenite in valle concisionis, id est in loco judicii, in valle damnationis ac separationis, in valle Josaphat jam præfata, ubi Dominus concidet cervices peccatorum. Siquidem ubi nostra translatio habet, In valle concisionis, Septuaginta et Theodotion transtulerunt, In valle judicii. Quia juxta est dies Domini, id est tempus justæ vindictæ seu remunerationis divinæ, in valle concisionis jam dicta.
paras.en: [[3:14|Nations, nations|Populi, populi]], that is, O all you peoples, gather [[3:14|in the valley of destruction|in valle concisionis]] [Latin *concisio*, "cutting down": hence "where the Lord will cut down"], that is, in the place of judgment, in the valley of damnation and separation, in the valley of Josaphat already mentioned, where the Lord will cut down the necks of sinners. Indeed, where our translation has *In valle concisionis*, the Septuagint and Theodotion translated, In the valley of judgment. [[3:14|for the day of the Lord is near|Quia juxta est dies Domini]], that is, the time of just vengeance or of divine reward, [[3:14|in the valley of destruction|in valle concisionis]] already spoken of.

paras.t: Sol et luna obtenebrati sunt, id est, ante diem judicii obtenebrabuntur. Quod quadrupliciter potest intelligi : Primo, quod Christo cum Sanctis descendente, amplioris claritatis lumine offuscabuntur, quum corpus Christi sit incomparabiliter splendidius sole lunaque. Sic enim et stellæ offuscantur in die, sole purius radiante. Secundo, quod quantum ad apparentiam sic continget, densis nubibus interpositis. Tertio, quia hominibus in maxima afflictione constitutis, omnia videbuntur teterrima et nociva. Quarto, quia ut aliqui magni expositores affirmant, nihil prohibet dicere, quod sol et luna tunc ad horam veraciter in se obscurabuntur ad ampliorem impiorum terrorem, statimque claritate perfundentur majori. Et stellæ retraxerunt splendorem suum, id est, obtenebrabuntur per modum de sole et luna prætactum.
paras.en: [[3:15|The sun and the moon are darkened|Sol et luna obtenebrati sunt]], that is, before the day of judgment they will be darkened. This can be understood in four ways. First, that when Christ comes down with the Saints, they will be dimmed by the light of a greater brightness, since the body of Christ is incomparably more splendid than the sun and moon: for so too the stars are dimmed by day, when the sun shines more purely. Secondly, that it will so happen as to appearance, through dense clouds coming between. Thirdly, because to men set in the greatest affliction all things will seem most gloomy and harmful. Fourthly, because, as some great expositors affirm, nothing forbids us to say that the sun and moon will then for an hour be truly darkened in themselves, to the greater terror of the wicked, and straightway be suffused with a greater brightness. [[3:15|and the stars have withdrawn their shining|Et stellæ retraxerunt splendorem suum]], that is, they will be darkened in the manner touched on concerning the sun and moon.

paras.t: Et Dominus de Sion rugiet, id est, per modum leonis horribiliter damnandis loquetur, ita ut dicat Joannes in Apocalypsi : Ex ore ejus exibat gladius ex utraque parte acutus. Ipse nempe est leo de tribu Juda. Et de Jerusalem dabit vocem suam : quod accipi potest de voce illa dulcissima, Venite, benedicti Patris mei. Rugiet namque ad impœnitentes et reprobos, loquetur vero bonis et rectis corde. Et movebuntur cœli et terra ; et Dominus spes populi sui, id est, electis tunc dabit vel conservabit plenam in ipso fiduciam, nec frustrati tunc erunt spe sua, et fortitudo filiorum Israel erit, confirmando et stabiliendo immobiliter atque feliciter corda prædestinatorum in se, ita ut dicant : Quis nos separabit a caritate Dei? et, Diligam te, Domine, fortitudo mea.
paras.en: [[3:16|And the Lord shall roar out of Sion|Et Dominus de Sion rugiet]]: that is, after the manner of a lion he will speak terribly to those who are to be damned, so that John says in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 1:16|from his mouth came out a sharp two-edged sword|Ex ore ejus exibat gladius ex utraque parte acutus]][[Apoc 19:15||]]. For he is the lion of the tribe of Juda. [[3:16|and utter his voice from Jerusalem|Et de Jerusalem dabit vocem suam]]: which may be taken of that most sweet voice: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father|Venite, benedicti Patris mei]]. For he will roar at the impenitent and the reprobate, but will speak to the good and the right of heart. [[3:16|and the heavens and the earth shall be moved|Et movebuntur cœli et terra]]; [[3:16|and the Lord shall be the hope of his people|et Dominus spes populi sui]]: that is, he will then give, or keep, to the elect a full confidence in himself, nor will they then be cheated of their hope; [[3:16|and the strength of the children of Israel|et fortitudo filiorum Israel]] he will be, by confirming and establishing the hearts of the predestined in himself, immovably and happily, so that they say: [[Rom 8:35|Who then shall separate us from the love of Christ?|Quis nos separabit a caritate Dei?]] [Denis reads "the love of God", as at Rom 8:39] and, [[Ps 17:2|I will love thee, O Lord, my strength|Diligam te, Domine, fortitudo mea]].

paras.t: Et scietis, o prædestinati universi, qui per Israel intelliguntur, quia ego sum Dominus Deus vester, id est summum bonum vestrum, amator, provisor, salvator, habitans in Sion cœlesti, id est in patria beatificæ visionis, de qua dicitur in Psalmo : Videbitur Deus deorum in Sion ; et ad Hebræos : Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis Jerusalem cœlestem, et multorum millium angelorum frequentiam. Cui et dicimus : Sicut lætantium omnium habitatio est in te. In monte sancto meo, id est cœlestis regni palatio. De quo in Psalmo cantamus : Domine, quis habitabit in tabernaculo tuo, aut quis requiescet in monte sancto tuo? Et erit Jerusalem illa cœlestis, Ecclesia triumphans, ex angelis atque hominibus constans, sancta, id est ab omni macula culpæ penitus libera. De qua in Apocalypsi dicitur : Civitas non eget sole neque luna ; et non intrabit in illam aliquid coinquinatum. Et alieni non transibunt per eam amplius, id est dæmones et peccata, de quibus oramus : Ab alienis parce servo tuo. Vel homines reprobi ultra locum non habebunt in prædestinatis hominibus glorificatis, quemadmodum olim, quando versabantur in via ac militanti Ecclesia. Unde in Isaia habetur : Induere vestimentis gloriæ tuæ, Jerusalem civitas Sancti, quia non adjiciet ultra ut pertranseat per te incircumcisus et immundus. Nunc enim reprobi miscentur electis, tunc vero incopulabiliter separabuntur.
paras.en: [[3:17|And you shall know|Et scietis]], O all ye predestined, who are understood by Israel, [[3:17|that I am the Lord your God|quia ego sum Dominus Deus vester]], that is, your highest good, your lover, provider and saviour, [[3:17|dwelling in Sion|habitans in Sion]], the heavenly Sion, that is, in the fatherland of the beatific vision, of which it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 83:8|the God of gods shall be seen in Sion|Videbitur Deus deorum in Sion]]; and to the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:22|you are come to mount Sion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to the company of many thousands of angels|Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis Jerusalem cœlestem, et multorum millium angelorum frequentiam]]. To it we also say: [[Ps 86:7|The dwelling in thee is as it were of all rejoicing|Sicut lætantium omnium habitatio est in te]]. In [[3:17|my holy mountain|monte sancto meo]], that is, in the palace of the heavenly kingdom, of which we sing in the Psalm: [[Ps 14:1|Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? or who shall rest in thy holy hill?|Domine, quis habitabit in tabernaculo tuo, aut quis requiescet in monte sancto tuo?]] [[3:17|and Jerusalem shall be|Et erit Jerusalem]], that heavenly Jerusalem, the Church triumphant, made up of angels and of men, [[3:17|holy|sancta]], that is, wholly free of every stain of fault. Of it it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:23|the city hath no need of the sun, nor of the moon|Civitas non eget sole neque luna]]; and: [[Apoc 21:27|There shall not enter into it any thing defiled|non intrabit in illam aliquid coinquinatum]]. [[3:17|and strangers shall pass through it no more|Et alieni non transibunt per eam amplius]], that is, demons and sins, of which we pray: [[Ps 18:14|from those of others spare thy servant|Ab alienis parce servo tuo]] [the Latin *ab alienis*, "from strangers", is the word of the verse, *alieni*]. Or: reprobate men will no longer have a place among the predestined men in glory, as once they had when they lived in the way and in the Church militant. Hence it is said in Isaias: [[Is 52:1|put on the garments of thy glory, O Jerusalem, the city of the Holy One: for henceforth the uncircumcised, and unclean shall no more pass through thee|Induere vestimentis gloriæ tuæ, Jerusalem civitas Sancti, quia non adjiciet ultra ut pertranseat per te incircumcisus et immundus]]. For now the reprobate are mingled with the elect, but then they will be separated, never to be joined again[[Matt 25:32||]].

paras.t: Et erit in die illa, videlicet in die æternitatis in patria : Stillabunt montes dulcedinem, id est, majores Sancti in patria omni Spiritus Sancti suavitate exuberabunt, eruntque exsultationes Dei in gutture eorum ; et colles, id est Sancti minores, fluent lacte purissimæ voluptatis. Solent enim Prophetæ per corporalia quædam, spirituales æternæ beatitudinis opulentias enarrare : quod etiam in novo agitur Testamento, quemadmodum Christus ait apud Lucam : Ego dispono vobis regnum, ut edatis et bibatis super mensam meam. Et per omnes rivos Juda ibunt aquæ : id est, flumen Spiritus Sancti incessanter irrigabit, vel potius in data irrigatione conservabit, rivos gloriæ confitentium Deo in patria confessione laudis perpetuæ. Inebriabuntur enim ab ubertate domus Dei, et in sæcula sæculorum laudabunt eum. Et fons de domo Domini egredietur, id est de intellectuali superbenedictæ Trinitatis cœlo : de quo fonte fertur in Psalmo, Quoniam apud te est fons vitæ ; et irrigabit torrentem spinarum, id est corda Sanctorum, quæ spinis tribulationum in hoc mundo confixa fuerunt, et per modum spinarum siccata a carnalis voluptatis humore, imo aliquando in hoc mundo spinis vitiorum fuerunt confossa.
paras.en: [[3:18|And it shall come to pass in that day|Et erit in die illa]], namely in the day of eternity in the fatherland: [[3:18|the mountains shall drop down sweetness|Stillabunt montes dulcedinem]], that is, the greater Saints in the fatherland will overflow with all the sweetness of the Holy Ghost, and: [[Ps 149:6|The high praises of God shall be in their mouth|exsultationes Dei in gutture eorum]]; [[3:18|and the hills|et colles]], that is, the lesser Saints, [[3:18|shall flow with milk|fluent lacte]] of the purest delight. For the Prophets are wont to describe the spiritual riches of eternal beatitude by means of certain bodily things; and this is done in the New Testament too, as Christ says in Luke: [[Luke 22:29|I dispose to you, as my Father hath disposed to me, a kingdom|Ego dispono vobis regnum]], [[Luke 22:30|That you may eat and drink at my table|ut edatis et bibatis super mensam meam]]. [[3:18|and waters shall flow through all the rivers of Juda|Et per omnes rivos Juda ibunt aquæ]]: that is, the river of the Holy Ghost will water unceasingly, or rather will keep in the watering once given, the rivers of the glory of those who confess God in the fatherland with the confession of everlasting praise [Juda is taken to mean "confession", that is, praise; see v. 20]. For [[Ps 35:9|They shall be inebriated with the plenty of thy house|Inebriabuntur enim ab ubertate domus Dei]], and [[Ps 83:5|they shall praise thee for ever and ever|in sæcula sæculorum laudabunt eum]] [Denis puts both Psalms in the third person: "the house of God", "shall praise him"]. [[3:18|and a fountain shall come forth of the house of the Lord|Et fons de domo Domini egredietur]], that is, from the intellectual heaven of the superblessed Trinity, of which fountain it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 35:10|For with thee is the fountain of life|Quoniam apud te est fons vitæ]]; [[3:18|and shall water the torrent of thorns|et irrigabit torrentem spinarum]], that is, the hearts of the Saints, which in this world were pierced with the thorns of tribulations, and after the manner of thorns were dried of the moisture of carnal pleasure; nay, which at times in this world had been run through with the thorns of vices.

paras.t: Ægyptus in desolationem erit, et Idumæa in desertum perditionis : id est, gentes istæ, per quas aliæ reprobæ nationes dantur intelligi, in die judicii perpetua desolatione plectentur, deserenturque a Deo, et in infernale chaos incident ; pro eo quod iniquæ egerint in filios Juda, per quos intelliguntur omnes Deo veraciter confitentes, et effuderint sanguinem servorum Dei innocentem in terra sua, id est in Ægypto et Idumæa, imo ubique terrarum.
paras.en: [[3:19|Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom a wilderness destroyed|Ægyptus in desolationem erit, et Idumæa in desertum perditionis]]: that is, these nations, by which the other reprobate nations are given to be understood, will be punished at the day of judgment with everlasting desolation, and will be forsaken by God, and will fall into the chaos of hell; [[3:19|because they have done unjustly against the children of Juda|pro eo quod iniquæ egerint in filios Juda]], by whom are understood all who truly confess God, [[3:19|and have shed|et effuderint sanguinem]] the [[3:19|innocent blood|innocentem]] of the servants of God [[3:19|in their land|in terra sua]], that is, in Egypt and Edom, nay, everywhere on earth.

paras.t: Et Judæa in æternum habitabitur. Per Judæam, quæ interpretatur confessio, designatur hoc loco patria cœlestis, in qua est incessabilis confessio laudis divinæ. De qua Judæa et confessione loquitur Isaias : Venient in Sion laudantes, et lætitia sempiterna super capita ipsorum. Quemadmodum enim aliqui sunt Judæi secundum carnem, qui non sunt veri Judæi, juxta illud Apocalypsis, Dicunt se Judæos esse, et non sunt ; sic ista terrena Judæa, respectu cœlestis Judææ, nomen Judææ nequaquam meretur.
