Frequenter quoque in Scripturis utriusque Testamenti attenditur significatio penes rei proprietatem, seu nominis interpretationem, magis quam quoad rem ipsam, hoc est quantum ad id a quo nomen imponitur, non quantum ad id cui nomen imponitur, quemadmodum Petrus ait in sua epistola : Salutat vos Ecclesia quæ est in Babylone collecta : ubi per Babylonem intelligitur Roma, illo in tempore confusionibus plena, imperante Nerone. Babylon autem interpretatur confusio. Simili modo nunc per Judæam significatur patria Beatorum, cujus quædam obscura figura erat terrena Judæa. Denique, quod terrena Judæa non habitabitur in æternum, certum est, præsertim quum apud Isaiam populo Judæorum, Synagogæ seu Jerusalem, Dominus pro finali retributione promittat : Non erit tibi sol amplius ad lucendum per diem, nec splendor lunæ illuminabit te. Daniel quoque apertissime ait, civitatem et sanctuarium fuisse dissipanda propter Christi occisionem, et quod finis Judæorum, vel civitatis seu templi, esset vastitas. Præterea tota hæc terra, in quam projecta est Adæ posteritas, est via, peregrinatio et exilium, non paradisus et patria. In temporalibus quoque et carnalibus bonis beatitudo hominis non consistit. Et Jerusalem illa cœlestis habitabitur in generatione et generationem, id est sine fine. Per quod significat cœlestem felicitatem nullo termino concludendam.
paras.en: [[3:20|And Judea shall be inhabited for ever|Et Judæa in æternum habitabitur]]. By Judea, which is interpreted *confession* [*confessio*: the praise of God as well as the confession of faith], is designated in this place the heavenly fatherland, in which there is an unceasing confession of the divine praise. Of this Judea and this confession Isaias speaks: [[Is 51:11|shall come into Sion singing praises, and joy everlasting shall be upon their heads|Venient in Sion laudantes, et lætitia sempiterna super capita ipsorum]]. For just as there are some who are Jews according to the flesh and are not true Jews, according to that of the Apocalypse, [[Apoc 3:9|who say they are Jews and are not|Dicunt se Judæos esse, et non sunt]], so this earthly Judea, in respect of the heavenly Judea, by no means deserves the name of Judea. Often too in the Scriptures of both Testaments the signification is looked for in the property of the thing, or in the interpretation of the name, rather than in the thing itself: that is, with regard to that from which the name is given, not with regard to that to which the name is given [a scholastic distinction: the quality from which a name is taken, as "confusion" for Babylon, and the thing that bears the name, the city itself]. So Peter says in his epistle: [[1 Pet 5:13|The church that is in Babylon, elected together with you, saluteth you|Salutat vos Ecclesia quæ est in Babylone collecta]]: where by Babylon is understood Rome, which at that time, under the reign of Nero, was full of confusions. For Babylon is interpreted *confusion*. In like manner, by Judea is here signified the fatherland of the Blessed, of which the earthly Judea was a kind of dim figure. Finally, that the earthly Judea will not be inhabited for ever is certain, especially since in Isaias the Lord promises the people of the Jews, the Synagogue or Jerusalem, as its final reward: [[Is 60:19|Thou shalt no more have the sun for thy light by day, neither shall the brightness of the moon enlighten thee|Non erit tibi sol amplius ad lucendum per diem, nec splendor lunæ illuminabit te]]. Daniel too says most plainly that the city and the sanctuary were to be destroyed on account of the slaying of Christ, and that the end of the Jews, or of the city or the temple, would be waste[[Dan 9:26||]]. Moreover, this whole earth, into which the posterity of Adam has been cast out, is a way, a pilgrimage and an exile, not paradise and the fatherland. Nor does man's beatitude consist in temporal and carnal goods. [[3:20|and Jerusalem|Et Jerusalem]], that heavenly Jerusalem, shall be inhabited [[3:20|to generation and generation|in generatione et generationem]], that is, without end. By this he signifies that the heavenly happiness is to be closed by no limit.

paras.t: Et mundabo sanguinem eorum, quem non mundaveram, id est, sanguinem sanctorum innocenter effusum, quem impii æstimabant se juste fudisse (vel vitam bonorum, quam perversi reputabant inutilem), demonstrabo mundum fuisse, et sine causa justa effusum. Vitam quoque illorum puram fuisse ostendam, impios condemnando, sanguinem sanctorum ulciscendo, bonos glorificando. Quod videntes reprobi, dicent : Nos insensati, vitam illorum æstimabamus insaniam, et finem sine honore : quomodo ergo computati sunt inter filios Dei, et inter Sanctos sors illorum est? Denique in igne conflagrationis, multi justorum tunc reperiendi, mundabuntur a venialibus culpis, vel a mortalibus per contritionem deletis, quantum ad culpam. Et Dominus commorabitur in Sion cœlesti seu triumphanti Ecclesia, prout dictum est plenius. Deus enim, qui quum sit infinitus, omnia implet et adest ubique, ibi esse et habitare asseritur, ubi clarius cernitur, et evidentius gratiosiusque operatur : quod est in cœlesti Sion, ubi videtur facie ad faciem. De hac etenim Sion ad litteram scriptum est in Isaia : Erubescet luna, et confundetur sol, quum regnaverit Dominus exercituum in monte Sion.
paras.en: [[3:21|And I will cleanse their blood, which I had not cleansed|Et mundabo sanguinem eorum, quem non mundaveram]]: that is, the blood of the saints innocently shed, which the wicked thought they had justly shed (or the life of the good, which the perverse reckoned useless), I will show to have been clean [*mundum*, "clean", answering to *mundabo*, "I will cleanse"], and shed without just cause. Their life too I will show to have been pure, by condemning the wicked, avenging the blood of the saints, and glorifying the good. Seeing which, the reprobate will say: [[Wis 5:4|We fools esteemed their life madness, and their end without honour|Nos insensati, vitam illorum æstimabamus insaniam, et finem sine honore]]: [[Wis 5:5|how they are numbered among the children of God, and their lot is among the saints|quomodo ergo computati sunt inter filios Dei, et inter Sanctos sors illorum est?]]? Moreover, in the fire of the conflagration [that is, the fire that will burn the world at the last day], many of the just who will be found then will be cleansed of venial faults, or of mortal ones already blotted out by contrition as to their guilt [that is, of the punishment still owed for mortal sins already forgiven]. [[3:21|and the Lord will dwell in Sion|Et Dominus commorabitur in Sion]], the heavenly Sion, or the Church triumphant, as has been said more fully above. For God, who, since he is infinite, fills all things and is present everywhere[[Jer 23:24||]], is said to be and to dwell there where he is seen more clearly and works more evidently and more graciously: and this is in the heavenly Sion, where he is seen [[1 Cor 13:12|face to face|facie ad faciem]]. For of this Sion it is written according to the letter in Isaias: [[Is 24:23|the moon shall blush, and the sun shall be ashamed, when the Lord of hosts shall reign in mount Sion|Erubescet luna, et confundetur sol, quum regnaverit Dominus exercituum in monte Sion]].

paras.t: Insuper quod dictum est, Stillabunt montes dulcedinem, etc., spiritualiter intelligitur de sanctis Apostolis pro tempore primitivæ Ecclesiæ, quando recepto Spiritu Sancto, multiformem gratiam, consolationem et sapientiam sibi infusam, fuderunt in alios, tanquam optimi dispensatores multiformis gratiæ Dei. Colles quoque, id est inferiores discipuli, fluxerunt lacte, de quo adstruit Paulus : Tanquam parvulis in Christo lac vobis potum dedi, non escam. De quo iterum : Perfectorum, inquit, est solidus cibus. Hoc igitur lac, est doctrina mediocris, imperfectorum capacitati proportionata, quales fuerunt quibus scripsit Apostolus : Non potui vobis loqui quasi spiritualibus, sed quasi carnalibus. Et per omnes rivos Juda, id est filios Ecclesiæ, ibunt aquæ, id est gratiæ Spiritus Sancti, de quibus dicit Salvator : Qui credit in me, sicut dicit Scriptura, flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ ; et in Apocalypsi, Ego sitienti dabo de fonte aquæ vitæ gratis. De quibus utique aquis loquitur Isaias : Omnes sitientes, venite ad aquas.
paras.en: Further, what was said, [[3:18|the mountains shall drop down sweetness|Stillabunt montes dulcedinem]], etc., is understood spiritually of the holy Apostles in the time of the primitive Church, when, having received the Holy Ghost, they poured out into others the manifold grace, consolation and wisdom infused into them, as the best [[1 Pet 4:10|stewards of the manifold grace of God|dispensatores multiformis gratiæ Dei]]. The hills too, that is, the lesser disciples, flowed with milk, of which Paul declares: [[1 Cor 3:1|As unto little ones in Christ|Tanquam parvulis in Christo]] [[1 Cor 3:2|I gave you milk to drink, not meat|lac vobis potum dedi, non escam]]. And of it again: [[Heb 5:14|for the perfect|Perfectorum]], he says, [[Heb 5:14|strong meat is|est solidus cibus]]. This milk, then, is the middling doctrine, proportioned to the capacity of the imperfect, such as were those to whom the Apostle wrote: [[1 Cor 3:1|could not speak to you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal|Non potui vobis loqui quasi spiritualibus, sed quasi carnalibus]]. And [[3:18|through all the rivers of Juda|per omnes rivos Juda]], that is, the children of the Church, [[3:18|waters shall flow|ibunt aquæ]], that is, the graces of the Holy Ghost, of which the Saviour says: [[John 7:38|He that believeth in me, as the scripture saith: Out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water|Qui credit in me, sicut dicit Scriptura, flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ]]; and in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:6|To him that thirsteth, I will give of the fountain of the water of life, freely|Ego sitienti dabo de fonte aquæ vitæ gratis]]. Of these waters Isaias too speaks: [[Is 55:1|All you that thirst, come to the waters|Omnes sitientes, venite ad aquas]] [the margin reads Is. iv, 1; the words are Is 55:1].

paras.t: Quod autem subjungitur, et fons de domo Domini egredietur, mystice de Baptismo exponitur. Imo quidam litteraliter inde exponunt, quamvis ordo textus non consonet, quia Prophetæ frequenter transeunt de tempore uno ad aliud. Itaque fons Baptismatis de domo Domini, id est a primitiva Ecclesia egressus est, quando et Petrus in die Pentecostes dixit compunctis Judæis : Baptizetur unusquisque vestrum in nomine Jesu Christi. De quo fonte scriptum est apud Zachariam : In die illo erit fons patens domui David et habitantibus Jerusalem, in ablutionem peccatoris. Et irrigabit torrentem spinarum, id est, corda peccatorum spinis atque aculeis passionum ac vitiorum perfossa ac læsa, gratia sacramentali perfundet ac fecundabit, ut oriantur in eis flores virtutum, et germina operum meritoriorum.
paras.en: As for what follows, [[3:18|and a fountain shall come forth of the house of the Lord|et fons de domo Domini egredietur]], it is expounded mystically of Baptism. Nay, some expound it so literally, although the order of the text does not agree, since the Prophets often pass from one time to another. And so the fountain of Baptism came forth from the house of the Lord, that is, from the primitive Church, when Peter too, on the day of Pentecost, said to the Jews who were struck with compunction: [[Acts 2:38|be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ|Baptizetur unusquisque vestrum in nomine Jesu Christi]]. Of this fountain it is written in Zacharias: [[Zach 13:1|In that day there shall be a fountain open to the house of David, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem: for the washing of the sinner|In die illo erit fons patens domui David et habitantibus Jerusalem, in ablutionem peccatoris]]. [[3:18|and shall water the torrent of thorns|Et irrigabit torrentem spinarum]]: that is, the hearts of sinners, pierced and wounded with the thorns and stings of the passions and vices, it will drench and make fruitful with sacramental grace, so that the flowers of the virtues and the buds of meritorious works may spring up in them.

paras.t: Postremo, aliqui passus hujus capituli, præsertim ab eo loco quo dictum est, Clamate hoc in gentibus, a diversis satis diversimode explanantur : quarum expositionum multiformis varietas videbatur mihi magis confundere atque obtundere intellectum, quam illustrare. Idcirco hac una explanatione, quæ textui consonantior esse apparuit, sum contentus. Ad gloriam ejus quem in cœlesti Sion desideramus per speciem contemplari : cui sit omnis honor et gloria, quum ipse sit super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: Lastly, some passages of this chapter, especially from the place where it was said, [[3:9|Proclaim ye this among the nations|Clamate hoc in gentibus]], are explained by different writers in quite different ways; and the manifold variety of these expositions seemed to me rather to confuse and blunt the understanding than to enlighten it. I have therefore been content with this one explanation, which appeared to agree better with the text. To the glory of him whom we long to contemplate by sight in the heavenly Sion: to whom be all honour and glory, since he is God, exalted above all things and blessed. Amen.
